title: J.P. Shadrick replaces Dave Pasch as Cardinals' play-by-play announcer
summary: For the first time in a quarter century, the Cardinals have a new radio play-by-play voice.
full_text: ' For the first time in a quarter century, the Cardinals have a new radio play-by-play voice. J.P. Shadrick, who has called NFL games on the radio for Westwood One and worked for the Jaguars' in-house media department, was announced today as the new radio voice of the Cardinals. Shadrick replaces Dave Pasch, who had been the Cardinals' radio voice for the last 24 seasons but announced in June that he was leaving the team to sign an exclusive contract with ESPN. Pasch had previously been splitting his time between ESPN and the Cardinals. "Dave Pasch is one of the great voices in our game and I appreciate the high standard that he left behind," Shadrick said. "I'm eager to work toward matching that but also take it further in my own style." Shadrick will work with former Cardinals center A.Q. Shipley, who is heading into his second season as the team's radio analyst.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Xavier Legette cleared of concussion after hard fall during practice
summary: One of Carolina's key offensive players had an injury scare during Tuesday's practice, but should be OK sooner than later.
full_text: One of Carolina's key offensive players had an injury scare during Tuesday's practice, but should be OK sooner than later. Head coach Dave Canales told reporters in his press conference that receiver Xavier Legette appeared to have suffered a stinger on a rough landing after making a catch during the session. "Made a really nice play, high pointed it … came down really hard,” Canales said. “Went in, evaluated him, cleared him of a concussion. But it looks like a stinger, so we’re going to evaluate him more over the next day or so and make sure he’s in the right spot. "He wouldn’t be playing in this game, but we have a nice little window to get him turned around and just see where he’s at.” The Panthers are playing the Hall of Fame Game against the Cardinals on Thursday night, with their following practice slated for Sunday. Legette, the No. 32 overall pick in 2024, caught 35 passes for 363 yards with three touchdowns in 15 games last season.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Mike McCarthy on Aaron Rodgers's comments: These are grown men with different opinions
summary: The fact that Aaron Rodgers's scorched-earth attack on Dr.
full_text: The fact that Aaron Rodgers's scorched-earth attack on Dr. Anthony Fauci and ESPN, while appearing on ESPN, has prompted a comment from the team and a question to the head coach makes it, necessarily, a distraction. Still, coach Mike McCarthy's goal will be to keep any of it from interfering with the task at hand. "You know, these are grown men ," McCarthy told reporters on Tuesday. "They all have different opinions. There's no question about that. But at the end of the day, my job is to keep it about football, keep the focus on winning. That's why we're here. We have a good locker room. We have a player council that's in place and we had our second meeting yesterday, and so I think we're in a good spot." It remains to be seen whether Rodgers's rollicking Monday appearance with Pat McAfee was a one-time thing, or whether Rodgers will revert to his pre-2025 habit of showing up on the show every week — and saying whatever he wants. It also remains to be seen whether, if/when the Steelers encounter adversity, McCarthy's methods will become a direct or indirect subject of Rodgers's current approach (as he said on Monday) of no longer giving a shit.
author: Mike Florio

title: Zay Flowers, Ravens agree to four-year extension
summary: Flowers' deal is reportedly worth $140 million, with $108 million guaranteed.
full_text: The Ravens have locked up one of their young offensive players. Baltimore and receiver Zay Flowers have agreed to a four-year contract extension, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports. The deal is worth a reported $140 million, with $108 million guaranteed. Flowers’ deal puts him just behind Drake London in terms of average new money per year at $35 million. Jaxon Smith-Njigba’s contract leads the market at $42.15 million per year. The No. 22 overall pick of the 2023 draft, Flowers was already under contract through 2027 after Baltimore exercised his fifth-year option in the spring. Flowers became the first wide receiver in Ravens franchise history to be selected to the Pro Bowl in 2024. He was again selected to the Pro Bowl in 2025, having caught 86 passes for 1,211 yards with five touchdowns in 17 games. Overall, Flowers has caught 237 passes for 3,128 yards with 14 TDs in 50 games over his three seasons. He’s also registered nine receptions for 156 yards with a touchdown in two playoff games.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Mike Vrabel on A.J. Brown's dislocated thumb: Linemen do that on every other snap
summary: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel is not too concerned about wide receiver A.J.
full_text: '' Patriots coach Mike Vrabel is not too concerned about wide receiver A.J. Brown’s dislocated thumb . Asked about Brown's injury, Vrabel made clear that football players and coaches don't consider dislocating a digit to be a particularly big problem. "I think he's going to be OK," Vrabel said with a smile. "I told him the linemen do that every other snap, and it's not a national story when a lineman pops his finger back in place. But we had a little bit of fun with that." Still, while Vrabel doesn't think there's anything special about a football player playing through an injured thumb, he said he has been enjoying watching Brown compete on the practice field with cornerback Christian Gonzalez. "I appreciate what A.J. and Gonzo have done, just come in and compete and try to improve," Vrabel said. "It's been a good battle, and that's pro football. I love watching it, and I think there's a great amount of respect each of those players have for each other and understand the work that they're putting in now is going to pay dividends in the season. I think that's all you can ask from your front-line players, that they come out and they're focused on getting better each day, and they're intentional with their work. When they're out there, it sends a clear and easy message to the rest of the team about how we're supposed to challenge and compete. I think it's been a good competition." It would take more than a dislocated thumb to keep Brown out of that competition.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jaylen Warren: First day of practice in pads was "most tame, uneventful" he's seen
summary: Things are very different in Latrobe.
full_text: '' Things are very different in Latrobe. On the first day of practice in pads with a head coach other than Mike Tomlin in twenty years, the pads weren't popping like they used to. “That was the most tame, uneventful first day in pads I’ve seen in all my years at training camp,” running back Jaylen Warren told reporters after practice, via Nathan Schivins of the Latrobe Bulletin . Warren, in his fifth Steelers training camp, said that it was "not what we're used to." It's the latest example of the manner in which new coach Mike McCarthy is balancing player health with preparedness. Eyebrows initially were raised when McCarthy said last week that the Steelers will not tackle to the ground. The fundamental differences between training-camp intensity will surely be cited as the biggest difference between the two Mikes, in the event a franchise that never had a losing record under Tomlin finds itself under .500 when the dust settles on the 2026 season.
author: Mike Florio

title: Falcons have spent plenty on core players this year
summary: With the new contract for running back Bijan Robinson, the Falcons have recently given big deals to four young players who have become part of the nucleus of the team.
full_text: With the new contract for running back Bijan Robinson, the Falcons have recently given big deals to four young players who have become part of the nucleus of the team. Beyond Robinson, the Falcons have extended 2021 first-round tight end Kyle Pitts (three years, $54 million), 2022 first-round receiver Drake London (four years, $141 million), and 2023 second-round guard Matthew Bergeron (four years, $96 million). While some could reasonably quibble about the value of the various contracts when considering the players' on-field accomplishments to date (except for Robinson, who was a bargain), the new regime in Atlanta clearly regards all four players as key pieces for the present and foreseeable future. That raises a question. Who drafted those players? It was former G.M. Terry Fontenot. Although the Kirk Cousins-Michael Penix Jr. misadventure from 2024 likely doomed everyone whose fingerprints were on those bang-bang decisions that blew up for the Falcons, Fontenot clearly did his job capably when it comes to selecting players whom the Falcons have since compensated as "keepers." The other side of the coin is the question of whether the Falcons may be overcommitting cash and cap space to Pitts, London, and Bergeron. Each contract represents a prediction that they'll earn the money. If they do, great. If they don't, the Falcons could end up in a cap crunch with not much to show for it. Through it all, the Falcons are close. They finished in a three-way tie for first place in the NFC South last year. If they can get consistency from the quarterback position, they could (and arguably should) win the division — especially since their new coach is a two-time coach of the year who has instantly acquired a more capable across-the-board roster than he had during his six seasons in Cleveland. And who no longer has to compete with the Ravens, Steelers, and Bengals.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bijan Robinson agrees to three-year extension with Falcons
summary: Robinson's deal includes $51 million in guaranteed money.
full_text: Bijan Robinson has not been practicing at Falcons training camp amid contract negotiations, but it looks like it is time for him to get on the field. According to multiple reports, Robinson has agreed to a three-year extension in Atlanta. Robinson was under contract through 2027 with an $11.323 million salary locked in for the final year after the Falcons exercised their fifth-year option on his rookie deal. The extension is reportedly worth up to $75 million with $51 million in guaranteed money and $37 million at signing. The base value is $66.75 million, which makes Robinson the highest-paid running back in the league in average annual salary. Robinson may not remain in that spot for long, however. Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs and Colts running back Jonathan Taylor are also looking for extensions, so the picture at the top could change in the near future. Wherever Robinson winds up, the move is the latest in a series of big deals for members of the Falcons offense. Wide receiver Drake London, tight end Kyle Pitts, and guard Matthew Bergeron have also signed long-term deals with the team this offseason.
author: Josh Alper

title: Lane Johnson has missed three straight practices at Eagles camp for non-injury reasons
summary: Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson is not injured, but he is not practicing.
full_text: ''' Eagles right tackle Lane Johnson is not injured, but he is not practicing. Johnson is not on the practice field today, the third consecutive day he has been out of practice. It's unclear why Johnson isn't practicing, but his absence has been described as excused and not injury-related. The 36-year-old Johnson is a two-time first-team All-Pro and one of the Eagles' most important players. Philadelphia's offense faded down the stretch last year after Johnson suffered a foot injury in Week 11 and missed the rest of the season. Johnson's absence has given third-round rookie Markel Bell opportunities to work at right tackle with the first-string offense. Bell was a left tackle in college at Miami but will learn both sides in the Eagles' offense while backing up both Johnson on the right side and Jordan Mailata on the left.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jets TE Kenyon Sadiq out "a little bit" due to setback after hernia surgery
summary: Jets first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq is not practicing on Tuesday for the third straight day and head coach Aaron Glenn said in his press conference that the rookie tight end will miss more time.
full_text: Jets first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq is not practicing on Tuesday for the third straight day and head coach Aaron Glenn said in his press conference that the rookie tight end will miss more time. Glenn said, per multiple reporters, that Sadiq will be out "a little bit" after suffering a setback in his recovery from hernia surgery. Sadiq, who was the 16th overall pick in April, had the procedure in May. Glenn added that he is "very confident" that Sadiq will be available for the team's Week 1 road date with the Titans. 2025 second-round pick Mason Taylor, Jeremy Ruckert, Jelani Woods, and Chase Curtis remain available at tight end for the Jets.
author: Josh Alper

title: Browns sign CB Tyler Hall
summary: The Browns added a cornerback to their roster on Tuesday morning.
full_text: '' The Browns added a cornerback to their roster on Tuesday morning. The team announced the signing of Tyler Hall. Offensive tackle Jack Conley was waived in a corresponding move. Hall appeared in one game for the Seahawks last season. He spent time on Seattle's practice squad in each of the last two seasons and previously played for the Raiders, Rams and Falcons. He has 46 tackles, two tackles for loss, a sack and four passes defensed in 32 career games. Conley spent time with the Patriots and Lions after going undrafted out of Boston College in 2025. He signed with the Browns' practice squad in December and re-signed in January.
author: Josh Alper

title: Klint Kubiak on Fernando Mendoza: I don’t expect him to be perfect right now
summary: While the Raiders drafted Fernando Mendoza to be their quarterback of the future, they also signed Kirk Cousins so that Mendoza doesn't have to be QB1 to start the season.
full_text: '' While the Raiders drafted Fernando Mendoza to be their quarterback of the future, they also signed Kirk Cousins so that Mendoza doesn't have to be QB1 to start the season. Right now, Mendoza's job is to learn and improve during training camp. Because of that, some days will go better than others — which is to be expected from a rookie quarterback. According to Adam Hill of the Las Vegas Review-Journal , Mendoza put together a bounce-back performance on Monday after an uneven Sunday. Monday was also the Raiders' first practice in pads. After the session, head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters that Mendoza will continue to face adversity as camp continues. But Kubiak is encouraged by what he's seen from Mendoza overall. "There’s 60-to-80 plays in a game, and there’s going to be ups and downs ," Kubiak said in his Monday press conference. "What quarterback can get the rest of the other 10 players playing at their best? So, that’s what we’re looking for. "There will never be a perfect game or a perfect practice, but I think he’s doing a good job. I don’t expect him to be perfect right now." The Raiders' first preseason game will be next Thursday night when they host the Cardinals.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Sean Payton: No hurry with Taysom Hill, I'll see him in Canton this week
summary: Broncos head coach Sean Payton will be in Canton, Ohio this week to take part in Drew Brees's induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame and he'll also do a little work on a possible addition to his roster.
full_text: Broncos head coach Sean Payton will be in Canton, Ohio this week to take part in Drew Brees's induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame and he'll also do a little work on a possible addition to his roster. Payton said over the weekend that the Broncos will explore signing former Saints tight end Taysom Hill and Hill will also be in Canton for Brees's induction. That will give Payton a chance to see where things stand. "There's no hurry right now. I'm going to see him in five days ," Payton said Monday, via Jeff Legwold of ESPN.com. "We'll see where he's at and kind of go from there. ... The key thing is his health and, you know, where he's at mentally. I don't want to assume he wants to play." Hill released a statement last month saying that he doesn't "have a clear answer about what the future holds, but I know that returning to New Orleans is not in the cards." He had knee surgery in 2024 that was performed by the Broncos' team doctor Karim Meijer and Payton said that Meijer has followed up with Hill during visits in Denver since the operation.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nolan Smith apologizes for "unacceptable" reckless driving arrest
summary: Eagles linebacker Nolan Smith was arrested in Georgia in May for speeding and reckless driving and he made his first public comments on the matter on Monday.
full_text: ''' Eagles linebacker Nolan Smith was arrested in Georgia in May for speeding and reckless driving and he made his first public comments on the matter on Monday. Smith was clocked at 135 miles per hour in an area with a 70 mph speed limit and head coach Nick Sirianni said at the time that the team would address it with Smith. Smith confirmed that he spoke with General Manager Howie Roseman and Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie while apologizing for his actions. “I apologized to the organization , and I’ll make that apology now,” Smith said, via Jeff Neiburg of the Philadelphia Inquirer “I represent the Eagles no matter where I go, Georgia, Florida, it doesn’t matter. That’s one of the ones that I own up and I apologize for. It’s just like that. We make mistakes and it can’t happen again and that’s unacceptable. I did apologize to Howie, I did apologize to Mr. Lurie, and I can’t let my teammates down like that. They hold me to a different accountability on and off the field.” Smith said "nothing came from" the arrest and he was able to avoid a July 14 court date by paying the fines associated with his infraction. The Eagles picked up the fifth-year option on the 2023 first-round pick's contract during the offseason. They did the same with defensive tackle Jalen Carter before signing him to a long-term extension and Smith will try to land a deal of his own at some point in the future.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Bears S Coby Bryant will miss 8-12 weeks with knee injury
summary: Bears safety Coby Bryant, who was carted off from practice Monday, was diagnosed with a hyperextended left knee, bone bruise and small fracture, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
full_text: Bears safety Coby Bryant, who was carted off from practice Monday, was diagnosed with a hyperextended left knee, bone bruise and small fracture, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Bryant is expected to miss 8-10 weeks. He was one of the team's key offseason signings, joining the Bears on a three-year, $40 million contract. Bryant spent the past four seasons in Seattle after the Seahawks made him a fourth-round pick in 2022. He won a Super Bowl ring in his final season with the organization. Cam Lewis is behind Bryant on the depth chart, though Lewis was playing the nickel. The Bears may need to make a move at the position.
author: Charean Williams

title: Shane Steichen on Alec Pierce: He's heading in the right direction for sure
summary: Colts receiver Alec Pierce has been on the active/physically unable to perform list since the start of training camp due to offseason ankle surgery.
full_text: '' Colts receiver Alec Pierce has been on the active/physically unable to perform list since the start of training camp due to offseason ankle surgery. It's still unclear when he'll be ready to practice. Head coach Shane Steichen said in his Monday press conference that he doesn't have a better sense of Pierce's timeline to get back on the field. "I know that he's working," Steichen said, via transcript from the team. "He's heading in the right direction for sure. So, I feel really good about that moving forward.” Pierce, 26, signed a four-year, $114 million deal with the Colts in March to stick with the club. He’s coming off his best season, having caught 47 passes for 1,003 yards with six touchdowns in 15 games in 2025.
author: Myles Simmons

title: With Bijan Robinson at $22.25 million in new-money APY, where will Jahmyr Gibbs land?
summary: Gibbs could still try to blow up the market, even if Robinson didn't.
full_text: With Falcons running back Bijan Robinson getting a new contract that pushes the new-money APY at the position from $20.6 million to $22.25 million, Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs has acquired an important data point for his own talks. Will Gibbs try to match Robinson's number? Will Gibbs try to beat it? Will Gibbs try to blow it away? It's no coincidence that the initial reporting on the Robinson deal spoke not in terms of the new-money APY of $22.25 million but the maximum value of $25 million per year . Given the overall skillsets and impacts of Robinson and Gibbs, both should have been trying to get to at least $25 million per year in new-money APY. Robinson will get there only if he hits the targets for the various incentives and/or escalators. Gibbs still has a chance to get there with his base APY. And when it comes to the new-money APY — a sort-of fugazi way to value contracts but the accepted norm used throughout the league (except when it leads to ridiculous results) — the old money becomes a factor. Remember, there are no true extensions. Robinson's new three-year deal wonn't get stapled onto the end of his two remaining years. He'll have a brand-new five-year deal, which folds the existing cash from 2026 and 2027 into 2028, 2029, and 2030. Robinson was due to make $3.744 million in 2026 and $11.323 million in 2027. That's a total of $15.067 million in "old money." Gibbs is due to make $3.183 million in 2026 (he was drafted four spots lower than Robinson) and $14.293 million in 2027 (he earned a higher fifth-year option based on his performances in 2023, 2024, and 2025). That's a total of $17.476 million in "old money." Robinson's lower old-money total makes it easier to get a higher new-money average on his five-year deal. If Gibbs merely matches Robinson's new-money APY, Gibbs will need to make $2.409 million more than Robinson over the next five years. In other words, if Gibbs signs the exact same five-year deal that Robinson will sign, Robinson will have the higher new-money APY, which means he'll be regarded as making more than Gibbs. At a minimum, Gibbs will want (and should try to get) at least $2.409 million more over the next five years than Robinson will receive. That nuance won't matter if Gibbs and his agents hold the rope for a real $25 million per year APY. That would require a five-year, $92.476 million contract for Gibbs. Putting it in those terms, is a five-year deal that pays out an average of $18.49 million per year from signing a good deal for the Lions? Hell yes. Flipping it back to Robinson, the combination of the old money and the new money results in a five-year, $81.817 million base deal. At $16.36 million per year over the next five years for arguably the best player in all of football, that's a great deal for the Falcons. It underscores the fact that the best running backs in the NFL aren't getting their fair share. Robinson opted to accept a new-money APY bump of $1.65 million over the prior record. That doesn't mean Gibbs will do the same thing. If he takes that position, he'll be more than justified in doing so. Because if Gibbs were available to any team right now, they'd be lining up around the block to give him a five-year, $92.476 million contract.
author: Mike Florio

title: ESPN has no comment on Aaron Rodgers's comments on ESPN, about ESPN
summary: On Monday, Aaron Rodgers had some strong things to say about ESPN.
full_text: On Monday, Aaron Rodgers had some strong things to say about ESPN. While appearing on ESPN. Per an ESPN spokesperson, ESPN has no comment regarding Rodgers's comments. Rodgers's rant initially focused on Dr. Anthony Fauci, as Rodgers did a COVID victory lap — one that glossed over the fact that Rodgers was disingenuous at best when he misled reporters in August 2021 on the question of whether he had received a vaccine. Rodgers then pivoted to ESPN, for not covering Fauci's repeated invocation of the Fifth Amendment at a Senate hearing last Thursday. (Should it have been the lead item on SportsCenter ?) “How much time did the network spend on that?” Rodgers said. “How much time do they spend on my responses every week? On my vaccination status, on Taylor [Swift] and Travis [Kelce’s] wedding? Did they do even a minute? Did they do even a minute on Tony Fauci? No, I bet they didn’t.” Rodgers also chastised ESPN for not covering the Mike Vrabel-Dianna Russini situation. “Then there was another scandal this offseason, too, involving a voter for MVP, for coach of the year,” Rodgers said. “How much time did your network spend on that? . . . Like, you have literally an individual that maybe used to work at ESPN that covers our league at the highest level, and there’s a major scandal, and it’s just, like, nobody can fucking talk about it. What are we even doing here? . . . [I]f it’s affecting certain things, if there’s leaks going on, if there’s tampering going on, if that person is also an MVP voter and a coach of the year voter.” While ESPN did cover it to an extent, it wasn't as big of a deal as it could have been. A thorough item from Ben Strauss was posted by ESPN.com on a Friday afternoon , with no corresponding car wash of interviews on the various ESPN shows. And ESPN has kept its head low and its mouth shut regarding the question of whether the relationship between Vrabel and Russini impacted her reporting while she worked for ESPN. Rodgers also accused ESPN of being a "gutless organization" with "no integrity." Last year, Rodgers ended his weekly Tuesday visits with Pat McAfee on ESPN. It will be very interesting to see whether Rodgers, in his final NFL season, resumes making the appearances — and whether he continues to air personal grievances and settle old scores. And whether he continues to take shots at the company that ultimately owns the platform, without any pushback from ESPN.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bears sign DB Marlen Sewell, put DL Jonathan Garvin on IR
summary: The Bears announced a pair of roster moves on Tuesday morning.
full_text: The Bears announced a pair of roster moves on Tuesday morning. They have signed defensive back Marlen Sewell. He takes the roster spot of defensive lineman Jonathan Garvin, who was placed on injured reserve in a corresponding move. Sewell was undrafted out of Vanderbilt this year. He signed with the Chiefs after the draft, but was let go by Kansas City in June. He had 52 tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, a half-sack and two passes defensed for the Commodores last season. Garvin played in 38 games for the Packers between 2020 and 2022, but has not appeared in a game over the last three seasons.
author: Josh Alper

title: Steelers on Aaron Rodgers: "Our players are entitled to their own personal views"
summary: Monday's rollicking, grievance-airing appearance by Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers on The Pat McAfee Show prompted ESPN, one of the targets of Rodgers's ire, to say nothing.
full_text: Monday's r ollicking, grievance-airing appearance by Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers on The Pat McAfee Show prompted ESPN, one of the targets of Rodgers's ire, to say nothing . The Steelers issued a comment essentially supporting Rodgers's ability to say whatever he wants, whenever he wants, wherever he wants. "Discussions around culture and politics can bring differing perspectives, and our players are entitled to their own personal views ," Steelers spokesman Burt Lauten told WTAE-TV, via Steelers Depot . "With respect to that, I am certain there are a variety of opinions on many topics within our locker room." It's an accurate observation, but the real question is what does coach Mike McCarthy think about it? Coaches loathe distractions, and Rodgers gratuitously created one on Monday. Last year, Rodgers didn't appear once on McAfee's show during the season, breaking from a habit of showing up on Tuesdays and, from time to time, spouting off on all sorts of things that prompted scrutiny and criticism. It doesn't take a genius (which qualifies me for the job) to conclude that former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin found a way to persuade Rodgers to restrict his 2025 media appearances to the league-required midweek and post-game press conferences. Tomlin lived it with former Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger, whose prior habit of making weekly appearances on 93.7 The Fan in Pittsburgh created periodic issues that kept Tomlin from fully focusing on the task of preparing his team to win football games. Eventually, and possibly at Tomlin's suggestion, Roethlisberger stopped doing it. If Tomlin were still the coach in Pittsburgh, would Rodgers have gone scorched earth on Dr. Anthony Fauci and ESPN? Probably not.
author: Mike Florio

title: John Harbaugh "very encouraged" by Arvell Reese's start to training camp
summary: The Giants had their first padded practice of the summer on Monday and one of the newest members of the team stood out during the session.
full_text: The Giants had their first padded practice of the summer on Monday and one of the newest members of the team stood out during the session. Reporters at the practice singled out first-round pick Arvell Reese as the main attraction. The linebacker stuffed running backs at the line, made plays in pass coverage and was credited with a sack of Jaxson Dart over the course of the sessions. That's the kind of multifaceted impact on defense that made Reese a prized prospect and it left head coach John Harbaugh singing the rookie's praises. "Very encouraged," Harbaugh said, via a transcript from the team. "I think he looked good today from what I could see. I can't wait to see the tape, but he's playing really well. He's been playing well the whole camp since he got here. . . . You see the talent, obviously. I think he's very sharp for a first-year guy. He gets things right pretty much all the time, makes very few mistakes. He's a very serious-minded guy, and he's very determined. I mean, he's doing things well." After the Giants picked Reese, there were questions about how the Giants would deploy him in their defense. They settled on using him as an off-ball linebacker, but the early days of training camp show that Reese could have a wide-ranging impact come the fall.
author: Josh Alper

title: Calvin Ridley: I still have the speed and ability to succeed
summary: Calvin Ridley took a pay cut to remain with the Titans this offseason, but it wasn't because he thinks he's lost the ability that made him an offensive threat in past seasons.
full_text: Calvin Ridley took a pay cut to remain with the Titans this offseason, but it wasn't because he thinks he's lost the ability that made him an offensive threat in past seasons. Ridley only played seven games before he fractured his fibula last season and he had 17 catches in those games, which had him on track for his least productive full season since entering the NFL. Ridley said over the weekend that neither those results nor the injury have left him questioning if he can keep pace. "Hell yeah," Ridley said, via the team's website. "[I] can still beat all of them , still as fast as all of them. . . . If I stay healthy, I am going to be a good player on this team. I am going to contribute on this team." Ridley is the most experienced member of the Titans' receiving corps and he explained why he's been able to act as a mentor to younger teammates like Carnell Tate, Chimere Dike, and Elic Ayomanor. "That's because I used to kick ass," Ridley said. "And I still can." The Titans would love to see Ridley get back to his old ways as they try to make a jump up the standings in quarterback Cam Ward's second season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jaguars put OL Trystan Colon on reserve/retired list
summary: Veteran offensive lineman Trystan Colon's bid to make the roster in Jacksonville came to an end on Tuesday.
full_text: Veteran offensive lineman Trystan Colon's bid to make the roster in Jacksonville came to an end on Tuesday. The Jaguars announced that they have placed Colon on the reserve/retired list. There was no corresponding move, which leaves the Jags with an open spot on their 90-man roster. Colon signed with the Jaguars in June. He entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Ravens in 2020 and spent three seasons in Baltimore before moving on to the Cardinals and Lions. Colon appeared in 63 games and made 19 starts across those three stops. He won't be adding to that total this fall and the Jags will have to look elsewhere for depth on the offensive line.
author: Josh Alper

title: Lions put TE Anthony Firkser on injured reserve
summary: Tight end Anthony Firkser's return to the Lions turned out to be a brief one.
full_text: Tight end Anthony Firkser's return to the Lions turned out to be a brief one. Firkser signed with the team on July 31, but his run on the active roster ended when the team placed him on injured reserve Tuesday morning. Head coach Dan Campbell said at his press conference that Firkser fractured his fibula. When the Lions initially signed Firkser, they waived tight end Zach Horton in a corresponding move. Horton re-signed with the team on Tuesday to fill the spot opened up by Firkser's injury. Firkser played for the Lions in 2023 and 2025 and returned to the team after being released by the Commanders in July.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dan Campbell: Bijan Robinson's extension certainly won't hurt Jahmyr Gibbs talks
summary: Bijan Robinson's contract extension with the Falcons is done and that means a lot of attention will now shift to Detroit.
full_text: Bijan Robinson's contract extension with the Falcons is done and that means a lot of attention will now shift to Detroit. Jahmyr Gibbs has joined Robinson as a training camp observer over the last week as both running backs looked for new deals with the teams that drafted them in the first round in 2023. Now that Robinson has taken the plunge on a three-year, $66.75 pact, many will wait to see what impact it has on the Lions' talks with Gibbs. Lions head coach Dan Campbell was asked about that during a Tuesday morning press conference. "It's certainly not gonna hurt ," Campbell said. "It's not gonna hurt, but we'll see. I'm anxious to get Gibbs back out there. Every day that goes by, that's another day that you feel like you miss with him and getting him out there with the guys. It'll get done when it gets done." Gibbs was evasive on Monday about where things stand with his contract talks and whether he would start practicing at some point without a deal. Robinson's deal sets a new bar for backs and that should help make the latter question a moot point before too much more time passes.
author: Josh Alper

title: Commanders put Ahkello Witherspoon on reserve/retired list
summary: The Commanders confirmed the signing of Fabian Moreau on Tuesday morning and they also announced that another veteran cornerback has decided to call it a career.
full_text: The Commanders confirmed the signing of Fabian Moreau on Tuesday morning and they also announced that another veteran cornerback has decided to call it a career. Ahkello Witherspoon was placed on the reserve/retired list in order to make space for Moreau on the roster in Washington. Witherspoon signed a one-year deal with the Commanders in March after spending the last three seasons with the Rams. He also played with the Steelers after opening his career as a 2017 third-round pick of the 49ers. Witherspoon had 243 tackles, 13 interceptions, a forced fumble and three fumble recoveries in 96 career regular season games. He also had 14 tackles, a sack and a forced fumble in eight playoff contests.
author: Josh Alper

title: 49ers ravaged by injuries early in training camp: NFC contender barely survives first week of practice
summary: The most injured team in the NFL is dealing with more injuries
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers have been in training camp for just over a week now and the injuries are already piling up. The 49ers were one of the most injured teams in the NFL last season and based on how things are going early in camp, they might once again be a threat to earn that unwanted title.
The 49es held their first practice of camp on July 26, and in the nine days since then, it's been total carnage. The team had a total of 14 players who missed practice on Monday, which is 15.5% of their 90-man roster.
The 49ers have ranked among the NFL's 10 most-injured teams in 12 of the last 13 seasons After 5 training camp practices, the injuries are already adding up 🤕 pic.twitter.com/1dF7U8OsiL
Let's take a look at how just how bad things have gotten for the 49ers over the past week.
The 49ers signed Deebo Samuel over the weekend , which ended up being a good thing, because they need all the depth they can get at receiver. Here are the biggest injuries at the postition from the past few days:
Pearsall's injury is the most notable and that's because he's out for the season. The former first-round pick missed eight games last year due to an issue with his PCL. The 49ers were hoping that the knee injury would heal during the offseason, but that didn't happen. Pearsall did participate in the first three practices of training camp, but his knee started to swell up. The 49ers decided on Saturday that the knee probably wouldn't be able to heal on its own, so the decision was made for Pearsall to have surgery , which will knock him out for the season.
The injury to Evans isn't serious, but it is mildly concerning. The 49ers gave Evans a three-year, $42 million contract this offseason, but if there was one question mark with Evans, it was his durability. He turns 33 on Aug. 21 and he's coming off a season where he missed nine games due to injury. Evans sat out Monday's practice , which isn't a huge deal, but if the injury lingers, that could pose a problem for San Francisco.
Kirk was also a free agent addition and things got off to a rocky start for the veteran receiver. Kirk injured his calf during the first practice of training camp on July 26 and hasn't return to practice, but he did do some running on the side during Monday's session, so he appears to be on the mend.
On Stribling's end, the rookie receiver is dealing with hamstring tightness that knocked him out of practice on Saturday. Stribling was at Monday's practice, but he wasn't suited up. Instead, he was testing his hamstring with some sprints.
#49ers De'Zhaun Stribling is off to the side field working his way back from hamstring tightness 🙏🏼 pic.twitter.com/uc3zaMZwKf
The 49ers will be hoping that Evans, Stribling and Kirk all heal quickly, but all three injuries are in spots where the injury can sometimes linger, so it will be interesting to see what happens there.
The 49ers are so beat up at running back that they went out and signed Khalil Herbert on Sunday. Here are the key injuries at running back:
James fractured his rib in a friendly-fire situation that involved linebacker Fred Warner . The 49ers' star linebacker was trying to punch the ball out during a practice on July 27 and apparently he hit James so hard that he broke the running back's rib .
James' injury could have set up more training camp carries for rookie Kaelon Black, but he's also injured. The 2026 third-round pick suffered an adductor injury that kept him out of Monday's practice, and if it's serious, it could keep him out for a few weeks.
As for Guerendo, his injury didn't happen at training camp: He tore his pectoral while lifting weights during the offseason and is currently on the physically unable to perform (PUP) list .
The 49ers' defense got decimated by injuries last season, and so far, things aren't going much better this year. Here's a look at a few players who have already missed at least one practice due to injury this year:
Mustapha, who started 10 games at safety for the 49ers last season, has already missed a week of training camp. He injured his hamstring on July 27 and that injury has lingered into August with the safety missing the 49ers' practice on Monday.
On White's end, he injured his adductor on Saturday and although it doesn't appear to be serious, that's another injury that can linger. As for Sample, he injured his knee at some point last week and that injury kept him out of practice on both Saturday and Monday.
The 49ers will also be likely be missing offensive lineman Vederian Lowe for an extended time after he suffered a high-ankle sprain last week .
On top of all this, Kyle Shanahan hasn't been running the team in training camp due to injuries that he sustained in a car crash on July 14. Shananhan has been on the field for almost every practice, but he's letting assistant coach Chris Foerster run the show along with offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak and defensive coordinator Raheem Morris.
If you're wondering how bad things got last year, just consider this: Out of the 14 playoffs teams from 2025, the 49ers lost more key players to injury than any other team and it wasn't even close.
As you can see, no other team came close to San Francisco's number. The Chargers and Packers were the only other teams that had more than 30. To put the 49ers' number in perspective, the Broncos and Jaguars tied for the fewest games missed in this category with just three.
Earlier this year, there was a theory going around that all the 49ers' injuries were happening because they practice close to a massive electrical substation and although there's been no correlation found yet, the 49ers might want to think about moving all of their future practices as far away as possible from the substation, just to be safe.
author: John Breech

title: NFL training camp battles 2026: Son of ex-NFL linebacker among rookies competing for starting spots
summary: From early-round selections to undrafted free agents, these 10 key rookies are already making serious noise and pushing veteran starters during the first week of training camp
full_text:
NFL training camps are underway and rookies are experiencing positional battles to varying degrees. First-round picks typically have an easier path to playing time because positional needs are taken into account when making investments of that magnitude. Others have to work harder to make an impression.
Thinking back to last season, the Saints were giving both Spencer Rattler and Tyler Shough an opportunity to win the starting job. Rattler got the nod in Week 1, but Shough eventually took over. Texans left tackle Aireontae Ersery was cross-trained in training camp, but ultimately earned a longer look as C.J. Stroud's blindside protector. Who are going to be some of those rookies to step up this season?
Through a week of training camp, there are a number of rookies engaged in positional battles. CBS Sports takes inventory of situations around the league.
Many had waved away the potential shortcomings of Kansas City's right tackle situation after releasing Jawaan Taylor , but that, combined with left tackle Josh Simmons ' absence last season, should be cause for concern. Veteran Jaylon Moore was the presumptive starter on the right side entering camp, but undrafted free agents Esa Pole and Kahlil Benson have forced themselves into the conversation.
Fifth-round pick Cyrus Allen had also been making an impression at receiver before getting dinged up in practice.
There is a trio of offensive tackles who were taken in the first round and are competing: Caleb Lomu ( Patriots ), Max Iheanachor ( Steelers ) and Blake Miller ( Lions ). Monroe Freeling may have been in this category as well had it not been for an unfortunate health development with Taylor Moton .
Bisontis and former third-round pick Isaiah Adams are locked in a battle for the right guard position. Presently, Adams holds an advantage. The coaching staff hopes that both Adams and Bisontis will eventually occupy starting roles, supplanting veteran Isaac Seumalo in the process.
The Cardinals may preach taking it slow with the rookie lineman, but he was only a few spots away from a first-round label, and that comes with expectations.
The Texans' coaching staff has been gauging a competition between first-round pick Keylan Rutledge and veteran Jake Andrews for the center gig, but it is difficult to envision Rutledge not winning the job, given that the team traded up to select him.
Douglas is serving as a place-holder for a number of Dolphins rookies. Miami drafted 13 players and nine rookies are listed either first or second string on the depth chart.
The team drafted three receivers and all three should push for immediate playing time. Jalen Tolbert , Tutu Atwell and Malik Washington are the most accomplished of the veterans, but Douglas offers size (6-foot-4) that can not be matched. The aforementioned veterans average 5-foot-10. As the team works to identify weapons for Malik Willis , in place of Jaylen Waddle and Tyreek Hill, Douglas has a strong case.
Indianapolis allowed safety Nick Cross to depart in free agency, which created a void in the secondary. The franchise really likes last year's seventh-round pick Hunter Wohler , who missed all of last season due to injury, but drafted Haulcy as a contingency plan. The two are now competing for the starting spot against Cam Bynum.
Second-round pick CJ Allen has taken ownership of the defense since returning to the practice field. Fellow rookie, fourth-round pick Bryce Boettcher , may also secure a starting role in Lou Anarumo's defense before all is said and done.
Hecht lasting until the fifth round came as a surprise because the player's body of work suggested he should have been taken much earlier. He may be a bit on the lighter side, but that can be minimized by the sheer mass of humanity on either side of him at offensive guard. Carolina signed veteran Luke Fortner , who brings additional value having offensive guard experience, in free agency, and Hecht is tasked with overtaking him for the starting center role.
New York invested heavily in free agent cornerback Paulson Adebo , who was a third-round pick by the Saints. The starting spot opposite him boils down to three players taken in the top-40 overall: former first-round picks Deonte Banks , Greg Newsome II and Hood. The latter has the physical traits to be effective in man and zone coverage. New York is his fourth team in as many years.
Wide receiver Malachi Fields is another rookie to monitor when determining how he fits into a room that includes Malik Nabers , Darius Slayton , Darnell Mooney , Juju Smith-Schuster , Odell Beckham Jr . and others.
Drew Dalman abruptly retired this offseason after signing a lucrative free agent contract the prior offseason. At the time of his departure, the Bears did not know if they would be able to secure their desired target in the draft, so it was important for them to have a contingency plan in place. The Ravens , for example, intended to draft a center on Day 2, but were left empty-handed at the end of the weekend. One of those centers coveted by Baltimore was Jones, who is now competing with Bradbury for the right to hand off footballs to Caleb Williams .
Masses is said to be a standout early in Raiders training camp, which, as a big fan pre-draft, fits my personal agenda. Las Vegas is looking for a starter opposite Eric Stokes . Among the competition for Masses is fellow rookie Jermod McCoy , the fourth-round pick, working his way back from injury. Last year's third-round pick, Darien Porter , is also competing for the spot. Masses had five interceptions in his first and only season with the Golden Bears after transferring from Florida International.
Chicago's fourth-round pick Malik Muhammad is thought to be in competition with Tyrique Stevenson . However, that seems like a situation in which Stevenson retains the starting job at least to open the season.
Los Angeles' interior offensive line was entirely turned over this offseason. When Washington released center Tyler Biadasz , the Chargers recognized a rare opportunity to add a quality player. The team still needed help at offensive guard, but they addressed it in an unorthodox way through the selection of the former Florida center. Nonetheless, Slaughter, as well as Trevor Penning and Kayode Awosika , is in the mix for the starting left guard vacancy.
The son of former NFL linebacker Jeremiah Trotter has been making an early impression at Buccaneers training camp. The team signed veteran Alex Anzalone in free agency to fill the massive shoes vacated by Lavonte David . Christian Rozeboom and SirVocea Dennis are also under consideration for the other role.
There were several linebacker situations that were under consideration. Fourth-round pick Kaleb Elarms-Orr is pushing for roles occupied by Terrell Bernard and Dorian Williams in Buffalo. In Atlanta, Christian Harris is engaged in a competition with fourth-round pick Kendal Daniels . Finally, second-round pick Anthony Hill Jr . and Cody Barton are battling for a starting role in Robert Saleh's inaugural Titans defense.
author: Josh Edwards

title: Highest-paid players at every NFL position: A look at who is cashing the biggest check heading into 2026
summary: A look at the markets by position for 2026
full_text:
NFL training camps are well underway, and not only does that mean that the season is fast approaching, but the paydays are coming in bunches, too, as teams look to lock in their top players long-term.
It's no secret that the NFL is a money-making machine: from merchandise, to commercials, streaming services, to tickets and more. Money is often a big hurdle between teams and players, with contract holdouts, hold-ins and trades giving each season plenty of drama on the sidelines.
The NFL salary cap has more than doubled in the last decade-plus and now sits at over $300 million per team heading into the 2026 season. Some teams are known to be more willing to spend money, while others like to be more cautious with the paycheck.
Some players choose to take less to be on the team they want or to rebuild a solid core around them, while others demand the highest value at their position. Just who is taking home the biggest bag?
We broke down the highest-paid players by position, based on average annual value, to gauge where the market stands. All values are via Spotrac .
Patrick Mahomes agreed this offseason to terms on a revised contract that adds two years to his existing deal and makes him the highest-paid quarterback in average annual value. The three-time Super Bowl MVP and two-time NFL MVP is the first player in NFL history to sign a contract worth more than $500 million. He passed Dak Prescott , who previously held the title at $60 million per year. Followed by Mahomes and Prescott are Josh Allen , Joe Burrow , Trevor Lawrence , Jordan Love and Matthew Stafford , who all hold $55 million AAV deals, according to Spotrac.
Bijan Robinson landed his record-setting payday after holding out at Falcons training camp for roughly one week. The deal could reach up to $75 million. Robinson's $22.25 AAV topped the previous record holder, Saquon Barkley, by roughly $2 million. Robinson led the NFL in scrimmage yards (2,298) last season.
The 32-year-old went undrafted in 2017 before signing with the Baltimore Ravens . He signed with the Giants this offseason after earning Pro Bowl and second-team All-Pro honors in 2025.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba was essential to the Seahawks ' Super Bowl championship run last season and was named the NFL's Offensive Player of the Year. He had 119 receptions and 1,793 receiving yards, a league high, along with 10 touchdowns in the regular season. His breakout year came at the perfect time for Sam Darnold's offense and he has high expectations as he enters Year 4.
George Kittle is arguably the best tight end in the league right now and it shows in his contract. The seven-time Pro Bowler and two-time first-team All-Pro has spent his entire career with the 49ers . Kittle started and ended his season with injuries last year, missing five games due to a hamstring tear suffered in Week 1 and going down with an Achilles injury in their wild-card game against the Eagles . He still has goals of a Week 1 return for the 2026 season.
Laremy Tunsil was the No. 13 overall pick in 2016, selected by the Miami Dolphins . He then went to the Houston Texans before joining the Commanders in 2025. His resume includes five Pro Bowl honors and he has started all 139 games he's played in.
Tyler Smith beats out last year's highest-paid offensive guard Trey Smith , who earns an average of $23.5 million per year. The 2022 No. 24 overall pick has become pivotal on the Cowboys ' line and has three Pro Bowls during his time in the league.
Tyler Linderbaum was drafted No. 25 overall in 2022 by the Ravens, where he remained until this offseason, when he joined the Raiders . The three-time Pro Bowler took 99% of offensive snaps last season, starting all 17 games.
Will Anderson Jr . became the highest-paid non-quarterback in NFL history with his massive three-year, $150 million deal. According to Next Gen Stats, he was seventh in run-stop rate (12.6%), third in run stuffs (13) and second in pressures (85) among defenders with at least 150 run defensive snaps in 2025. His performance put him second in NFL Defensive Player of the Year voting. He was named DPOY in 2023.
Jeffery Simmons briefly held the title of highest-paid interior defensive lineman this offseason before Jalen Carter took the throne with a huge extension on the eve of the first practice of training camp. Carter's extension doesn't kick in until after the 2027 season and includes $106 million guaranteed.
Fred Warner has spent his entire career with the Niners and the team has him under contract until 2030. He is a four-time first-team All-Pro and a four-time Pro Bowler, starting all 121 regular-season and 12 playoff games he's appeared in. The defensive leader was limited to six games last season due to an ankle fracture.
For the second time in his career, Ward tops the highest-paid defensive back list after signing a two-year, $62.2 million extension that ties him to Cleveland through 2029. Ward was already signed through 2027 on a five-year, $100.5 million extension in 2022. He's a five-time Pro Bowler with 18 career interceptions.
Derwin James has played for the Chargers since the team selected him No. 17 overall in 2018. He earned his fifth Pro Bowl and fourth second-team All-Pro honor last season. He had a career-best three interceptions last season, to go with 94 combined tackles, seven passes defended, two sacks and one forced fumble.
This marks the largest deal for a kicker in league history, earned in thanks to Pro Bowls in each of his three seasons in the NFL. Aubrey went undrafted in 2022 and joined the USFL, becoming a two-time champion in the league, before heading to the Cowboys in 2023. He has made 88.2% of field goals attempted and 96.9% of attempted extra points. He has six total field goals over 60 yards, an NFL record.
Jordan Stout led the league with a net average of 44.9 yards last season and earned a Pro Bowl spot due to his 2025 performance.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Falcons sign Bijan Robinson to historic three-year extension, making him NFL's highest-paid running back
summary: Robinson led the NFL with 2,298 yards from scrimmage in 2025
full_text:
Move over, Saquon Barkley : there's a new highest-paid running back in the NFL .
The Atlanta Falcons have reached an agreement with Bijan Robinson on a historic three-year extension with a maximum value of $75 million, according to ESPN . The deal includes $51 million in guaranteed money, the highest ever for a running back (excluding rookie contracts). Robinson's average annual value on the new deal currently sits at $22.25 million ( via Spotrac ), with the potential to reach $25 million, exceeding Barkley's $20.6 million AAV.
An extension for Robinson has been looming since the start of training camp, and the back has been holding in as this deal continued to be hammered out. With pen being put to paper on this historic contract, Robinson has ample time to get back onto the practice field to gear up for the 2026 regular season and help Atlanta rebound from an 8-9 season in 2025.
$22.25 million (up to $25M)
Christian McCaffrey ( 49ers )
Kenneth Walker III ( Chiefs )
Robinson is entering his fourth season in the NFL after the Falcons selected the Texas product with the No. 8 overall pick at the 2023 NFL Draft . Upon arrival, the 24-year-old back has established himself as arguably the most dynamic back in the league.
Last season, Robinson set a franchise record, tallying 2,298 yards from scrimmage (which also led the NFL). His 5,648 career scrimmage yards are the most by a player at age 23 or younger in NFL history, and are the fourth-most scrimmage yards in the first three seasons by a player in NFL history.
Jeremiyah Love ( Cardinals )
Robinson's extension is just the latest in what has been a busy offseason for the new Atlanta front office led by first-year general managers Ian Cunningham and president of football Matt Ryan , who were both hired earlier this year. The Falcons reached extensions with other key figures, including wideout Drake London (four-year, $141.05 million extension), tight end Kyle Pitts (three-year, $54 million extension), and guard Matthew Bergeron (four-year, $96 million extension).
You can't look at Robinson landing this mega deal with the Falcons and not think about Jahmyr Gibbs , who is also currently holding in during Lions training camp as he seeks what may also be a market-setting extension. One of these two backs needed to go first, and Robinson has now laid a blueprint for what Gibbs and his camp could be looking for in their deal with Detroit, if not exceeding it just a touch.
"It's certainly not going to hurt," Lions head coach Dan Campbell told reporters Tuesday morning while reacting to the Robinson extension and what it means for Gibbs, via ESPN . "But we'll see. Look, I'm anxious to get Gibbs back out there. Every day that goes by, you know, that's another day that you feel like you miss with him and getting out there with the guys, and him doing his part. But it'll get done when it gets done."
Despite splitting touches with David Montgomery (who was traded to the Houston Texans this offseason) for the bulk of his career to this point, Gibbs has posted 49 career touchdowns, which are the most in the first three seasons by any player in NFL history. Over the last two seasons, he's third in the NFL in scrimmage yards (3,768) and first in scrimmage touchdowns (38).
Given his impressive career to this point, Gibbs has a strong chance to make Robinson's reign as the highest-paid running back in the NFL short-lived, provided he and the Lions can work out a deal.
