title: Monday Musings: The most impressive player at Chiefs camp so far
summary: We are five days into Kansas City Chiefs training camp this year and have only seen one full practice with the team in pads. As I drove back from St. Joe to Kansas City on Monday afternoon, a thought came to mind: who has been the single-most impressive performer, the MVP so to speak, of […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - JUNE 08: Drue Tranquill #23 of the Kansas City Chiefs on set during a production shoot at The University of Kansas Health System Training Complex on June 08, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Aaron M. Sprecher/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are five days into Kansas City Chiefs training camp this year and have only seen one full practice with the team in pads. As I drove back from St. Joe to Kansas City on Monday afternoon, a thought came to mind: who has been the single-most impressive performer, the MVP so to speak, of Chiefs camp so far? Drue Tranquill sneaky camp MVP through five practices. He’s been super active, especially picking up downfield routes. He’s stuck to WRs and taken away some throws — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) August 3, 2026 From Day 1 to Day 5, it sort of blew me away how easily I settled on linebacker Drue Tranquill to answer that question. Tranquill has shown off his ability to anticipate run plays and knife into the backfield from the weak-side linebacker position, but he has also played on the edge in a few looks that featured three down linemen and three linebackers; Tranquill was the fourth player on the edge, in a similar role to former Chiefs linebacker Leo Chenal during his time. He has looked stout against the run, but Tranquill feels like the answer because of his effort and energy to make plays in coverage. On Saturday, he seemingly baited quarterback Patrick Mahomes into throwing over the middle, watching his eyes and driving from the back side to make the interception in a seven-on-seven period. Throughout practices, Tranquill has played with urgency when dropping into coverage, sticking to pass catchers entering his zone and denying passes regardless of how far down the field the route goes. On one play Monday, Mahomes looked for wide receiver Jimmy Holiday down the field towards the sideline, but Tranquill back-handed the ball away, looking like a defensive back in the process. He seems to be having a complete camp, with high energy included. He’ll get animated after making a big play and bring fire out of teammates, like when running back Kenneth Walker beamed Tranquill with the ball after Tranquill finished a play aggressively in shells. It’s not a bad thing to stir the pot at camp, but that play — along with the interception mentioned before — symbolizes Tranquill’s mentality as one of the defense’s veteran leaders. “[We’re] trying to make an emphasis this year on getting the ball out,” Tranquill told the media after Friday’s practice. “We need to get the ball out more on defense.” Who has stood out to you the most from your intake of camp coverage, or your own in-person observations? Let us know in the comments.

title: Chiefs training camp notebook Day 5: Peter Woods pops in pads
summary: It was a sunny, warmer day in St. Joe for Kansas City Chiefs training camp practice, the fifth of camp and the first in full pads. The team came into Monday’s practice fresh off the first off day since the full team arrived on the campus of Missouri Western State University. Here’s the recap of […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 25: Peter Woods #99 walks toward the practice field during Kansas City Chiefs Training Camp at Missouri Western State University on July 25, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images It was a sunny, warmer day in St. Joe for Kansas City Chiefs training camp practice, the fifth of camp and the first in full pads. The team came into Monday’s practice fresh off the first off day since the full team arrived on the campus of Missouri Western State University. Here’s the recap of Monday’s practice: Attendance report Head coach Andy Reid spoke to the media after practice and provided details on the three active Chiefs who were unavailable on Monday : wide receivers Cyrus Allen and Xavier Worthy, and defensive end Ashton Gillotte. As they have each day of practice, cornerback L’Jarius Sneed and wide receiver Rashee Rice took the field with the team in full uniform. Each participated with pads on, although Rice seemed to be held out of 11-on-11, full-team period work against the defense. Sneed seemed to be in the same boat, although I have noted his movement as closer to 100% comparatively to Rice. Peter Woods properly introduces himself While observing the full-team periods, star defensive tackle Chris Jones reminded fans of his dominance with a few disruptive, blow-by snaps. However, rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods also stood out by disengaging from blocks ferociously or leveraging himself to plug a gap while fighting with an offensive lineman. Peter Woods was very pleased after these two 1-on-1 reps. #Chiefs pic.twitter.com/lI2mEZp71m — Harold R. Kuntz (@HaroldRKuntz3) August 3, 2026 I didn’t get a good look at his performance in the one-on-one pass-rush drills, but Harold Kuntz of FOX4 highlights a couple of notable reps that show off the skill Andy Reid pointed out when asked about Woods after practice. “I like what I’ve seen. He’s an explosive kid,” Reid said. “He’s learning; he’s smart, and he’s trying to hone in on some of these techniques we’re asking him to do. [I] like his effort. He’s got a ways to go, but you sure like the tools, the effort and how smart he is. I appreciate that.” On one particular one-on-one rep in the lineman drills, right guard Trey Smith stonewalled Woods, who tapped him on the helmet with respect after the rep. It was truly iron sharpening iron; Smith sounded excited about his new teammates across the line of scrimmage when talking to reporters on Monday. “Peter’s really talented,” Smith said. “The sky is the limit for him. In terms of his hand utilization, speed, power, he’s really sort of a full-package guy. He’s young, and he’s figuring out the game, but he has a willingness to learn. I’ve really, really enjoyed the way he has stepped into this program, this organization and how he’s trying to turn himself into a great player,“ Smith emphasized. ”Definitely has an outstanding future ahead of him, just really excited to help with his development where I can.” Who is catching passes from Patrick Mahomes? Without Worthy and Allen running routes for the Chiefs’ offense, the three starting receivers when running plays on air were wide receivers Rashee Rice, Tyquan Thornton and Andrew Armstrong. Rice wasn’t playing much during full-team periods, so players like Jalen Royals, Nikko Remigio and Jimmy Holiday saw more time in the mix with the starting offense. Similar to the way Allen was seemingly Mahomes’ favorite target for an early stretch of camp, Armstrong stepped up on Monday. Reid can see it. “Armstrong… he went through the rookie camp, and pushed through that. I thought he did a nice job there, and he has transferred that over,” Reid shared. “It looks like Pat has trust in him. So I think that’s a plus; he’s getting better every day. Big target, strong… I like that part of it.” On second-year wideout Jalen Royals, who hasn’t made the same pop as Allen or Armstrong in camp, Reid kept the praise simple. “I think Royals has kind of gotten better playing faster every day that he has been here.” What Andy Reid is looking for at right tackle On the first day of full pads, rookie Kahlil Benson got the nod as the starting right tackle for the fourth consecutive practice. However, veteran Jaylon Moore quickly rotated in with the starters in practice; the two seemingly split time between the first and second teams on the right side. “Let them compete, and just see where it goes,” Reid said of the position battle after practice. “Both of them can play, I think. We just have a young guy we haven’t seen much of, but he has some talent. Let’s see where that goes. “Moore keeps battling; he has had a couple good days, too,” Reid noted. “We’ll need all of them, that’s how it goes.” When asked about the inevitable mistakes Benson will make as a first-year player, Reid made his stance on the learning curve clear. “Not to make the same mistake twice, right? That’s what I’m looking for,” Reid said. “We’ll give you a chance here to learn, but if you start making it consistently, then we have a problem. But he has been doing a good job. There’s a hiccup here or there, but he fixes it, normally.” Andy points to pass-pro improvement for Brashard Smith In the early stages of camp, second-year running back Brashard Smith has seemingly been the most immediate backup to Kenneth Walker in the Chiefs’ starting backfield. He has been an outlet for quarterback Patrick Mahomes on screen passes and in the flat during practice, but he has also received plenty of handoffs in run-game work. If he is to continue seeing the ball with the first team, he will need to be effective in all facets of a pass down. “I know he can run the football; I know he’s good with the ball in his hands, catching the ball,” Reid said of Smith. “Can you do all the small things that a running back has to do with protection, the intricacies of the different routes we have for him? We’ll see how we’ve improved, protection being the big one.”

title: Andy Reid provides injury, team update after Monday’s Chiefs practice
summary: The fifth full-team practice of Kansas City Chiefs training camp took place on Monday with a few notable absences. Head coach Andy Reid addressed the injury status of multiple players to open up his post-practice press conference in St. Joe. Wide receivers Cyrus Allen, Xavier Worthy and defensive end Ashton Gillotte were the three active […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 25: Cornerback Mansoor Delane #5 walks toward the practice field during Kansas City Chiefs Training Camp at Missouri Western State University on July 25, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The fifth full-team practice of Kansas City Chiefs training camp took place on Monday with a few notable absences. Head coach Andy Reid addressed the injury status of multiple players to open up his post-practice press conference in St. Joe. Wide receivers Cyrus Allen, Xavier Worthy and defensive end Ashton Gillotte were the three active players unavailable to practice. Reid reassured reporters on Allen’s scary-looking injury from Saturday’s practice, confirming the report by Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star . “[It] ended up being a bone bruise on his shin area there, so it’ll be a day or two here,” Reid said about Allen. Later on, he added that the team has “to get the swelling out of there, so however many days it takes to get the swelling out.” “Gillotte has a hamstring strain, Xavier has a shoulder sprain… it’ll be a few days for that, and we’ll see how that goes,” Reid added in his opening statement. Reid was asked directly about rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane, who started this stretch of padded practices in the yellow, non-contact jersey with shorts. Throughout Monday’s practice, Delane could be seen running on and off the field during team periods. It sounds like Delane is simply refusing to miss out on his first training camp in Kansas City. “He’s a tough nut,” Reid described Delane. “A lot of guys probably wouldn’t go out there and play with what he’s got, but he wants to be out there; he wants to learn. That’s what he wants to do… we have to keep him out of contact. Right now, that’s important until that thing heals up. Footwork and all that is great; go do all of that, no problem, but we just have to wait until it’s healed up.” It’s also important to take note of Reid’s update on Mia Bieniemy, the wife of offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy, who is recovering from last week’s frightening incident . “On the Eric Bieniemy side of it, Mia’s doing better,” Reid said. “She keeps improving by the day. That’s a positive. There’s no timetable on EB coming back or any of that, he just needs to take care of business there. When he gets back here, he gets back here.” The Chiefs will be back at it in St. Joe on Tuesday morning, practice starting at 9:15 a.m. on “Ambassador Day.”

title: Chiefs training camp: 3 players with the most to lose
summary: Training camp is here, and the Kansas City Chiefs are ramping up practices in St. Joseph, Missouri. During the first week of camp, the Chiefs practiced with no pads, but the team will strap them up all the way on Monday, setting the table for what the roster will look like in 2026. Through the […]
full_text: ST JOSEPH, MISSOURI - JULY 30: Tight end Travis Kelce #87 participates during Kansas City Chiefs training camp at Missouri Western State University on July 30, 2026 in St Joseph, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images Training camp is here, and the Kansas City Chiefs are ramping up practices in St. Joseph, Missouri. During the first week of camp, the Chiefs practiced with no pads, but the team will strap them up all the way on Monday, setting the table for what the roster will look like in 2026. Through the ranks of the 90-man roster, some players can benefit from the camp sessions, but others could find themselves on the wrong end of the stick. It may just be practice, but camp performance can set the tone for how a player’s season will go, whether it is in a positive direction or negative. Let’s look at three players with the most to lose at camp: Offensive tackle Jaylon Moore With a year in the Chiefs’ system under his belt, Moore should be the full-fledged number one option at right tackle this season. Moore started six games in 2025 before an injury ended his season in December, but many called for him to start over Jawaan Taylor for most of the season. However, as the offseason has progressed, the room has become more crowded than it should be. Moore was fine when he played, but undrafted free agent Esa Pole also made an impact when he was able to see the field, which sparked debate in the offseason about a possible competition for the starting right tackle job in 2026. So far in camp, adding to the intrigue, undrafted rookie Khalil Benson has been the primary starter with the first-team offense while Moore has been working with the second team. This may be just to give Benson a shot to show that he has what it takes to compete at the NFL level, and the odds still favor Moore to end up being the starter — due to his experience and contract — but if he were to falter in camp, or play poorly in the preseason, it could jeopardize his future in the NFL. Safety Chamarri Conner Conner has had an up-and-down stint since he arrived in Kansas City in 2023. Early on in his career, he showed that he could be an exciting player, capable of making plays on the ball and creating highlight-level plays. Conner can make splash plays and has had the tendency to come up big in tough spots, but as an every-down player, he has not played at the highest level. Last season, the Chiefs attempted to line up Conner as an every-down safety, but it did not quite pan out. With the departure of free safety Bryan Cook this offseason, Conner should have been primed for a larger role in 2026, but this offseason the team signed Alohi Gillman to serve as the team’s free safety for the coming seasons, and Conner will also have to continue to compete with Jaden Hicks for the strong safety position this season. A poor camp and preseason from Conner could take him out of the running to be one of the starters at safety altogether, and now there are also other players who could find ways to get on the field over him in other situations. Gillman was only one of the offseason defensive back additions, but with Kader Kohou and Jadon Canady also in the mix to be the team’s Nickel, the defensive back room, while not proven, has become crowded, and if Conner fails to show significant improvement, he could find himself as a special teamer in 2026. Tight end Noah Gray Since being drafted in the fifth round of the 2021 NFL Draft, Noah Gray has lined up primarily as the Chiefs’ second tight end, and since then the team has not looked to push another player, or another group of players, into that role. Kansas City’s tight end depth has been poor for multiple seasons now, and it is not looking much better, and that is precisely why Gray could be a loser once camp and the preseason conclude. If any player behind him in the depth chart can make any sort of immediate impact, or show that they can surpass him, the addition would be welcome by Chiefs Kingdom. Gray has not been bad for Kansas City, but being a below-average run blocker and scheme-dependent pass catcher has not allowed the Chiefs to have much diversity from the primary backup for Travis Kelce. The entire tight end room behind Kelce will have plenty to prove, but if any combination of Jared Wiley, Jake Briningstool, Tre Watson, or Mason Pline can show solid run blocking with consistency in the passing game, they will likely overtake Grays ‘ position.

title: Former Rams cornerback has retired after 9 seasons
summary: Former Los Angeles Rams cornerback Ahkello Witherspoon has decided to hang up his cleats after nine seasons in the NFL. Washington, who signed Witherspoon in free agency, placed the veteran CB on the reserve/retired list on Tuesday. Witherspoon joined the team this offseason after spending the last three seasons with the Rams. He also played […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 04: Ahkello Witherspoon #4 of the Los Angeles Rams reacts after an interception during the second quarter of the game against the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium on January 04, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Former Los Angeles Rams cornerback Ahkello Witherspoon has decided to hang up his cleats after nine seasons in the NFL. View this post on Instagram Washington, who signed Witherspoon in free agency , placed the veteran CB on the reserve/retired list on Tuesday. Witherspoon joined the team this offseason after spending the last three seasons with the Rams. He also played three years with the 49ers and two with the Steelers. Even though his final NFL season ended with two stints on injured reserve, he was still an integral part of L.A.’s defense. Witherspoon started all 17 games and had a career year during his first season with the Rams in 2023. That season, he set career highs in combined tackles (52), tackles for loss (3), passes defensed (14), interceptions (3) and fumble recoveries (2). According to Pro Football Reference , he also allowed a 48.1 completion percentage and a 75.7 passer rating in coverage. It was a season that should’ve propelled him to Pro Bowl honors, but it kicked off the Rams’ ongoing playoff streak, so that’s what mattered most. He didn’t experience as much success the following season, as he started just five of 13 games played and recorded only a single interception. Despite that, his lone pick was perhaps the play of the year in a late-season win over the Cardinals. With Arizona driving for a last-second touchdown with 37 seconds to play, Witherspoon made an incredible diving interception on a deflected pass, securing the Rams’ 13-9 win. Deflected and PICKED in the end zone. What a grab by Witherspoon! 📺: #AZvsLAR on NFL Network 📱: Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DCKepFjgoT — NFL (@NFL) December 29, 2024 The turnover sealed the team’s ninth win in 11 games and eventually won them the NFC West crown, their first since the 2021 campaign. Injuries significantly limited his final season. Witherspoon suffered a broken scapula in Week 2 against the Titans and rebroke it in the wild card win over the Panthers. Even though Witherspoon’s NFL career didn’t end on a high note or with Super Bowl glory, his time in Hollywood showcased his potential most. He made clutch plays when it mattered and provided stability at a position where the Rams had lacked depth for years. Witherspoon deserves praise for what he brought to the team in his brief time there and has earned retirement following a solid career.

title: Davis Allen nursing quad injury
summary: Sean McVay informed reporters on Monday afternoon that fourth year tight end Davis Allen is dealing with a quad injury in training camp. McVay did not provide a concrete timeline other than the injury is going to require “some time”. In all likelihood, Davis Allen misses at least the next two weeks with it being […]
full_text: Sean McVay informed reporters on Monday afternoon that fourth year tight end Davis Allen is dealing with a quad injury in training camp. McVay did not provide a concrete timeline other than the injury is going to require “some time”. Rams TE Davis Allen is dealing with a quad injury. Sean McVay said the Rams will give Allen “some time” before he returns to practice because it’s a soft tissue injury. “You don't want to rush him back,” McVay said. “… Davis is going to be a big part of what we do this year.” — Sarah Barshop (@sarahbarshop) August 3, 2026 In all likelihood, Davis Allen misses at least the next two weeks with it being a soft tissue injury and the Rams typically being conservative with their injuries in training camp. Allen has steadily carved out a role in Sean McVay’s offense over the past several seasons. Whether serving as a reliable blocker, contributing as a pass catcher, or filling in whenever injuries have arisen, he has become a dependable member of the Rams’ tight end room. Any missed practice reps can slow momentum, particularly during training camp when timing and chemistry are being refined before the regular season. Fortunately for Los Angeles, this is one position where the roster is built to withstand a temporary setback. While any injury to a player is unfortunate, the Rams can afford an injury like this at the tight end position because of the impressive depth they have assembled. Veterans Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson remain the leaders of the group, while Terrance Ferguson adds another talented option capable of making plays in the passing game. Beyond the established names, undrafted rookie Dan Villari has also given the coaching staff another developmental option to evaluate. Villari’s athletic profile and versatility have made him an intriguing player throughout offseason workouts, and every additional practice rep provides another opportunity to prove he belongs on the 53-man roster. Having players like Villari available allows the Rams to continue operating their offense without dramatically changing practice rotations. The coaching staff has consistently emphasized competition at every position, and the tight end room is no exception. With multiple players capable of contributing, Los Angeles doesn’t have to rush Allen back before he is fully healthy. That luxury is one many NFL teams simply do not possess. The Rams have invested heavily in creating quality depth across the roster, and situations like this demonstrate why that approach matters. Training camp injuries are almost inevitable over the course of an NFL summer, but organizations with strong depth can continue developing players while avoiding unnecessary risks with veterans. Potential Impact If Allen misses additional practice time, one of the biggest beneficiaries could be rookie Max Klare. Additional snaps with Matthew Stafford and the first-team offense would provide invaluable experience for the young tight end as he continues adjusting to the speed of the NFL. Even if those opportunities only come in occasional packages or select practice periods, they could accelerate Klare’s development while giving the coaching staff another extended look at how he performs alongside the Rams’ top offensive players. By the time Allen returns, Los Angeles could emerge with even greater confidence in the overall strength and versatility of its tight end room.

title: Davante Adams is grateful for Rams practices
summary: Between an MVP quarterback throwing him the ball and an All-Pro cornerback covering him on those passes, receiver Davante Adams appreciates how much the L.A. Rams have upgraded training camp practices this year. Adams has Matthew Stafford and Trent McDuffie helping him get better every day as the Rams prepare for the San Francisco 49ers […]
full_text: Westchester, - August 01: Wide receiver Davante Adams #17 of the Los Angeles Rams during the Los Angeles Rams training camp on the campus of Loyola Marymount University in Westchester on Saturday, August 1, 2026. (Photo by Keith Birmingham/MediaNews Group/Pasadena Star-News via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images Between an MVP quarterback throwing him the ball and an All-Pro cornerback covering him on those passes, receiver Davante Adams appreciates how much the L.A. Rams have upgraded training camp practices this year. Adams has Matthew Stafford and Trent McDuffie helping him get better every day as the Rams prepare for the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1, so maybe it’s never too late for an “old receiver” to learn new tricks. “Iron sharpens iron,” said Adams about facing McDuffie in camp. The Rams had Adams, Sean McVay, and Nate Landman available to the media after Sunday’s practices . Here is some of what they had to say. McVay not worried about Myles Garrett Myles Garrett has missed the last four practices , so of course that was the first topic of conversation that McVay had to address. He doesn’t sound worried about it. The recently acquired superstar “is dealing with a little soreness in his lower half,” according to McVay. The Rams are “erring on the side of being smart” with Garrett and “there’s no reason for concern,” which is a much more comforting endorsement than what fans were hearing from McVay last year as it pertained to Stafford’s back. This could be a nothingburger, but after the reporting debacle at their last training camp, I’m confident the coach won’t be assuming anything this time around. After some coach speak about how the team is having great “back and forth”, with both sides of the ball pushing each other, I found it interesting he mentioned, again, how impressed he is with Stetson Bennett. “I think Stetson Bennett has really capitalized on a lot of reps that he didn’t get last year….To be able to run the one offense the way he has, I’ve been pleased.” It seems to me that Bennett is QB2 for the foreseeable future. Nate Landman misses Jared Verse Landman was the first player I’ve seen in these pressers who seemed a little less enthused about the trade for Garrett. Or does he just miss Jared Verse? “You don’t lose the human element, I do love Jared Verse. I’ve got some shared experience with him.” This was right after calling Garrett, “One of one.” He is truly excited about this year and by what the new players bring to the table and spoke about the synergy of the defense. “There’s no egos on this team. Just people who love football, that want to play football and do what’s best for the team.” When he spoke about defensive coordinator Chris Shula, he said he teaches all the players all of the roles for different plays. No guessing where a CB or Edge is going to be. “Not solely focusing on our job, but on how the defense works as a whole.” Personally, Landman is looking to improve as a leader on the field as well. “You’re always looking to improve. Nobody’s perfect in this game. Nobody’s above coaching, and so I’m looking forward to taking that new step, more confident in the calls, more confident defense, and my ability, and the guys around me, building trust and just focusing on doing my job.” Davante Adams Adams was asked if it’s a bonus having Stafford participating in this year’s camp, and he gave an emphatic yes. He thought it affected their performance last season. “(Stafford and I) are getting a whole different start than we had last year.” Adams is also excited to be able to go against McDuffie, one of the best corners in the league, day after day. “I don’t know if I’ll get a better look than what I get from Trent out there…it’s the epitome of iron sharpens iron” Adams is the third or fourth speaker I’ve heard in this year’s pressers giving a shout-out to Jordan Whittington, a receiver now getting reps at fullback. “J Whit is like the most fired up dude about playing fullback.” Finally, Adams talked about how Stafford consoled him on the flight home after losing the NFC Championship game to the Seahawks, saying that the quarterback was hopeful that he could help the receiver finally get the Super Bowl he’s been waiting for his whole career. Matthew turned around and said, ‘I’m sorry man I wanted that for you so bad.“ Not for him but for me. That’s the type of teammate you like to have in your corner, both in January and in August.

title: What Ty Simpson is being criticized for in training camp
summary: The Los Angeles Rams drafted quarterback Ty Simpson based almost completely on his potential, not solely on what he can already do, so developing his mechanics over the next year was always part of the plan. The fact that training camp can often be so public may not be doing the Rams or Simpson any […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - JULY 31: Ty Simpson #15 of the Los Angeles Rams practices during the Los Angeles Rams Training Camp at Loyola Marymount University on July 31, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams drafted quarterback Ty Simpson based almost completely on his potential, not solely on what he can already do, so developing his mechanics over the next year was always part of the plan. The fact that training camp can often be so public may not be doing the Rams or Simpson any favors as the team works on fixing those issues. From some training camp footage, some users on Twitter have taken to scouting what’s working—and not working—for Simpson in his first Rams training camp. Namely, that while the talent is obvious, mechanical issues stemming from his base and his footwork are just as apparent. This rep pretty much sums up Ty Simpson’s training camp so far in LA. The ball placement here is outstanding, but the footwork still needs a lot of refinement. He’s relying on his arm talent and fading off his back foot, which isn’t going to consistently generate the velocity or… https://t.co/Ra7UXP1Hry pic.twitter.com/UVTyMI13xb — SCOUTD (@scoutdnfl) August 2, 2026 Not that we should hand over all credibility to an anonymous account on Twitter named “SCOUTD”, but do you see any truth in this statement from the video above: “This rep pretty much sums up Ty Simpson’s training camp so far in LA. The ball placement here is outstanding, but the footwork still needs a lot of refinement. He’s relying on his arm talent and fading off his back foot, which isn’t going to consistently generate the velocity or accuracy he’ll need at the NFL level. The flashes are absolutely there. Now it’s about cleaning up the mechanics and becoming more consistent.“ Nothing said here sounds or looks to be incorrect or unfair. Simpson, with absolutely zero pressure in his face, does appear to be (for no reason) falling onto his back foot and robbing himself of a solid foundation when he throws this pass. It’s just one pass. It’s practice. He’s a rookie. Nobody’s saying it matters in the long run. But nevertheless, any small takeaways we can infer from Ty Simpson’s first training camp are newsworthy and interesting. He’s the biggest investment that the L.A. Rams have made in a quarterback since they traded for Matthew Stafford. He’s the biggest draft pick investment since Jared Goff in 2016. He’s labeled as the future of the franchise. So while Simpson should not see the field in 2026, emphasis on “should not” instead of “definitely won’t” because nobody can predict when that time will be necessary, anything we see from the quarterback today is worthy of debating prior to tomorrow.

title: L.A. Rams News: Blake Corum, Terrance Ferguson showing up
summary: Last season, the Los Angeles Rams found some new weapons with a healthy Blake Corum and rookie tight end Terrance Ferguson. So far, there is an expectation that they may be able to contribute even more. Corum is talented, but he’s somewhat struggled to stay healthy, but we’ll see how he does in Year 3. […]
full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - JULY 29: Blake Corum #22 of the Los Angeles Rams walks off the field during training camp at Loyola Marymount University on July 29, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last season, the Los Angeles Rams found some new weapons with a healthy Blake Corum and rookie tight end Terrance Ferguson. So far, there is an expectation that they may be able to contribute even more. Corum is talented, but he’s somewhat struggled to stay healthy, but we’ll see how he does in Year 3. Kyren Williams still appears to be the lead back as long as he stays upright and takes care of the football. Ferguson showed some real talent last year and fit right into L.A.’s shifting tight end room. The Rams seemed to use every tight end they had last year, and that may happen again in 2026. We’ll see. The excitement for this offense should be high as they have the potential to be a top unit. Pair that with what should be an improved defense and this Rams team should be fun for their fans. There is a lot to look forward to as long as this team still has the right pieces throughout the season. Comment on whatever you want and thank you for checking out Turf Show Times! Rams’ young talent showing up and locked and loaded for the season ahead (ramblinfan) “The second layer of skill talent is where the offense could look a little different than it did a year ago. Terrance Ferguson has had a fantastic offseason. “He is now proving to be a guy who can play all over the formation and looks like he could be a force after the catch, showing why the Rams coveted him in the 2025 draft and now believe he could grow into one of the NFL’s best tight ends. “Blake Corum has also worked to earn carries alongside Williams, seeing the game faster and looking like a guy who could add a big-play element to the Rams’ physical run game.” Former Matthew Stafford teammate could offer Rams insurance at OT (ramswire) “With Alaric Jackson having emerged from legal troubles and Warren McClendon having acquitted himself well in relief of a now-retired Rob Havenstein last season, the Rams’ Super Bowl push seems set at the tackles. However, considering Havenstein’s departure and the previous uncertainty with Jackson, a need for solid depth on a team with such high hopes has been underscored. Rookie third-rounder Keagen Trost bodes well for future plans, but adding Decker, who previously protected Matthew Stafford’s blind side in Detroit, would be a luxury fitting for what L.A. is trying to put together.” Rams hold Garrett out as he deals with ‘a little soreness’ (espn) “We want to make sure that he feels as good as possible,” McVay said. “And so I think, as you know, guys that have played a lot of football, we’ve got a lot of opportunities to be able to get better, but we also want to make sure that we’re getting an understanding of how to work best with him.” McVay said Garrett will not practice Monday, the final day of this four-day practice block for the Rams. McVay said the team will evaluate Garrett after an off day on Tuesday, but said, “I would expect him to be ready to go in the next block.”

title: How concerned should Rams be about Byron Young’s knee?
summary: Byron Young was listed as questionable with a knee injury ahead of last year’s NFC Championship game against the Seattle Seahawks. As we turn the corner into the new year, the Los Angeles Rams continue to manage Young’s knee. Young received his first day off in training camp as early as the second day. He’s […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 25: Byron Young #0 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during the third quarter against the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC Championship game at Lumen Field on January 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Byron Young was listed as questionable with a knee injury ahead of last year’s NFC Championship game against the Seattle Seahawks. As we turn the corner into the new year, the Los Angeles Rams continue to manage Young’s knee. Young received his first day off in training camp as early as the second day. He’s on a similar approach to that of quarterback Matthew Stafford : Byron Young: “I practiced yesterday, but don’t want to do too much to overload our workload,” Young said. “We got a plan to just take some time and get back there in a couple of days. But just day by day, we’re trying to last for 17 games and postseason. … It’s the same knee. It was challenging, but at the same time I trust the training staff. It’s been something I was dealing with for years now and they always came through for me.” Sean McVay: “It’s no different than Matthew,” McVay said. “We have guys that have accumulated a bunch of snaps, and the goal is, let’s be proactive instead of reactive. So we’ve always looked at him as a guy that kind of fits in that tier one category, similar to what we do with Matthew.” Read into the situation however you want. Some will call this smart treatment of one of the defense’s most important players. Others will say that it’s curious that Young is still sidelined by an injury that occurred more than six months ago. Rams edge Byron Young practiced yesterday and skipped today because they’re trying to keep his right knee in top shape for the season ahead. He says it’s something he’s been dealing with “for years now,” but they always get it right. — Greg Beacham (@gregbeacham) July 28, 2026 One thing that is certain is the knee injury will likely complicate Young’s future in Los Angeles. Entering a contract year, it’s fair to wonder whether the Rams intend to sign him even with the injury aside. Young is a great second EDGE player. He made the most of favorable opportunities while opposing offenses paid extra attention to Jared Verse. He’s clearly second fiddle to Myles Garrett, although anyone would be. And then there’s the fact that Young is already 28 years old after entering the NFL as an older college prospect. There are several factors that point to him being one-and-done in Los Angeles from a contract standpoint. Smart money may suggest letting another franchise make that investment. It’s not like the cupboard would be completely bare in the EDGE room if Young moves on in 2027. Garrett is now secured long-term. Josaiah Stewart was as efficient as any rookie pass rusher a year ago. He should be primed for a larger workload in his second season. If the Rams like what they see, that may make their decision on Young more straightforward. Young’s injury may not matter in regards to 2026. It almost certainly already matters when it comes to a new contract and his status within the team beyond this season. It’s a situation worth keeping an eye on.

summary: Fourth-down aggression has gotten more common in the NFL among offensive playcallers in recent seasons. Still, some playcallers are more aggressive than others. It appears new Las Vegas Raiders head coach and offensive playcaller Klint Kubiak has been among the least aggresssie play callers on fourth down in recent years. Pro Football focus conducted a […]
full_text: SAN JOSE, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 04: Offensive Coordinator Klint Kubiak of the Seattle Seahawks speaks to the media ahead of Super Bowl LX at the San Jose Convention Center on February 04, 2026 in San Jose, California. (Photo by Eakin Howard/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fourth-down aggression has gotten more common in the NFL among offensive playcallers in recent seasons. Still, some playcallers are more aggressive than others. It appears new Las Vegas Raiders head coach and offensive playcaller Klint Kubiak has been among the least aggresssie play callers on fourth down in recent years. Pro Football focus conducted a study of the most and the least aggressive teams on fourth down spanning the 2021-25 NFL seasons. The Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers went for it on fourth down the least amount of times in that time period. Also, the New Orleans Saints had the second fewest fourth-down conversions in that time span. Kubiak was with those three teams in the past three seasons. So, these stats are not all on Kubiak, but he is part of a trend. It’s not necessarily good or bad if a playcaller is overly aggressive or not. title: The Year 2 bar for Raiders defensive tackle JJ Pegues
summary: New year. New coaching staff. New evaluation period. Such is the case for head coach Klint Kubiak and his Las Vegas Raiders as the team continues its journey through training camp. The hotshot offensive-minded 39-year-old is the man leading the Silver & Black into the 2026 campaign and things are equal parts excitement and hope. […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 16: JJ Pegues #92 of the Las Vegas Raiders waits during a drill before a NFL Preseason 2025 game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the San Francisco 49ers at Allegiant Stadium on August 16, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The 49ers defeated the Raiders 22-19. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images New year. New coaching staff. New evaluation period. Such is the case for head coach Klint Kubiak and his Las Vegas Raiders as the team continues its journey through training camp. The hotshot offensive-minded 39-year-old is the man leading the Silver & Black into the 2026 campaign and things are equal parts excitement and hope. So far, Raiders players have talked about a new sense of urgency and energy permeating throughout team facilities as the the Kubiak regime — picked by general manager John Spytek and minority owner Tom Brady — is going through the meticulous process of not only changing a culture, but creating one that’s keen on attention to detail. The “get the small things right and big things happen” philosophy is a shared one across all three aspects of the game: Offense, defense, and special teams. This past weekend marked the fifth practice of training camp and Kubiak’s assessment of the team’s 90-man roster was only apt. “Yeah, the guys that like aren’t an established guy, which is probably 90 percent of the team, in order for them to make the roster it’s special teams and playing multiple positions,” Las Vegas head coach said after this past Friday’s team session. “Receivers that can play all three, fullbacks that can play tight end and vice versa, DBs that can play corner, nickel and safety, so that’s how you make the roster in the NFL.” One of the roster hopefuls: Defensive tackle JJ Pegues. The sixth-round pick (180th overall) in the 2025 NFL Draft heads into Year 2 with the Raiders after a rookie season that saw the Ole Miss product play in nine games and notching 11 total tackles (one for loss) and a fumble recovery on 137 defensive snaps (21 special teams snaps). The 24-year-old has ideal size at 6-foot-2 and 325 pounds and there’s a wide open competition at nose tackle — a spot where Pegues build would be an asset. And that’s where the Year 2 bar starts for the Mississippi native. By The Numbers JJ Pegues, Defensive Tackle, 2nd Year 2025: 9 games (zero starts), 11 total tackles (four solo), 1 tackle for loss, 1 fumble recovery; 137 defensive snaps, 21 special teams snaps Career: See above. Monster in motion 👹 Get to know new defensive tackle JJ Pegues ⬇️ — Las Vegas Raiders (@Raiders) April 27, 2025 On The Nose Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard’s pivot from a 4-3 to a 3-4 base defense increases the importance of a nose tackle in the middle of the defensive line. Lining up directly over the opposing center, the nose (or zero technique) controls both A-gaps, absorbs multiple blockers, and has the strength to not only anchor but move blockers to stop the run up the middle to free up their fellow defenders to make plays. The frontrunners early in camp are veterans Benito Jones (6-foot-1 and 335 pounds) and Adam Butler (6-foot-4 and 301 pounds). Of that duo, the 28-year-old Jones has the squatty build and experience to be in immovable anchor in the middle with Miami and Detroit, while the 32-year-old Butler, more of a penetrating-type, has played directly over the center during his stops in New England, Miami, and in Las Vegas. In the mix are Pegues, 2026 seventh-round pick (229th overall) Brandon Cleveland (6-foot-4 and 315 pounds) and undrafted free agent Gary Smith III (6-foot-1 and 319 pounds) from UCLA. Pegues showed glimpses of being able to anchor while flashing impressive power during preseason last year but couldn’t carve out substantial defensive snaps under then-head coach Pete Carroll’s coaching staff. One of those being Leonard, who served as defensive line coach and defensive run game coordinator for Carroll before impressing Kubiak in his interview for the defensive coordinator role and getting the nods. Pegues needs to put together a strong camp and preseason showing he’s a capable option as the nose tackle or depth at the position. He’s got the skillset to be a two-gap (run stopper) and one-gap (penetrator) nose tackle and the mass to attract plenty of attention. And both youth and cheap cost rookie deal (four-year, $4.467-plus million) are in Pegues’ favor. Another example of JJ Pegues' knockback power, he's been impressive at NT in the 2 preseason games #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/DiJTpUxgYr — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) August 18, 2025 Pressure & Versatility While Leonard is slated to use a 3-4 base defensive front, NFL offenses are more pass-centric and creative and to combat that, defenses are using more nickel and sub packages to counter and defend. That’s resulted in teams being in big nickel formations where a trio of safeties are on the field or more defensive backs with the defensive line being a hybrid of four-down, three-down, or even five-down linemen at the line of scrimmage. By showcasing the ability to penetrate as a nose tackle in odd or even fronts, Pegues increases his roster chances and value with versatility. Pegues providing an anchor and rusher in odd and even fronts makes him an indispensable commodity, but it’ll be easier said than done as a late-round pick with talent and potential. Las Vegas was without a true nose tackle in 2025 with players rotating trying to fill the spot but this offseason, there’s healthy competition. However, Leonard is no stranger to have a nose tackle-type on his defensive line as big John Jenkins (6-foot-3 and 360 pounds) filled that role in former defensive boss Patrick Graham’s four-down fronts. While not your standard flair of pass rusher, Jenkins did rack up 10 pressures and two sacks (according to Pro Football Reference) over the course of his two seasons in Silver & Black (2023-24) alongside 107 total tackles (seven stops for loss) with six pass deflections and a fumble recovery in 34 games (all starts). Seeking that kind of impact and statistical compilation is likely far from Pegues’ reach in Year 2 — Jenkins was in Year 11 and 12 the 2023 and 2024 seasons with 116 games of experience under is belt. A wild card for Pegues, though: Offense. During his collegiate days under then-Ole Miss head coach Lane Kiffin, Pegues’ was the Running Rebels’ short-yardage running back. Kiffin exploited Pegues’ power and athleticism to convert short-yardage situations at a high rate including seven rushing touchdowns (21 carries for 69 yards) during Ole Miss’ 2024 season. Kubiak isn’t shy about getting creative and perhaps, this is the Raiders coaching staff that experiments with the success Kiffin found with Pegues’ on offense? His college career did begin as a tight end with Auburn in 2020 before he shifted to defense the following season and transferred to Ole Miss in 2022. JJ Pegues might be the first DT/FB/TE to EVER be selected in the NFL Draft. Pegues reportedly “showed out” in both DL drills as well as FB/TE drills at the NFL Combine today. Several NFL teams reportedly see Pegues as a "chess piece" and want to use him as both a DT on defense… pic.twitter.com/CEqdbigkkh — Rookie Watch (@RookieWatxh) February 28, 2025 The Bar With Pegues showcasing consistency and versatility during training camp and preseason action, a rotational role behind veteran Jones as a zero technique is the expectation. Playing in 13 to 15 games while compiling 18 to 25 total tackles with a sack and four quarterback pressures while getting looks as a short-yardage mammoth back or lead blocker on offense is a reasonable Year 2 bar for Pegues.

title: Unlocked: 8 Raiders Sleepers Under Pressure to Make the 53-Man Roster
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have overhauled their roster heading into the 2026 season, and there’s a new wave of talent for Las Vegas this season from young standouts to veterans, and budding second year players. A look at a few Raiders that could sneak their way into the roster. I already touched on EDGE Cian […]
full_text: The Las Vegas Raiders have overhauled their roster heading into the 2026 season, and there’s a new wave of talent for Las Vegas this season from young standouts to veterans, and budding second year players. A look at a few Raiders that could sneak their way into the roster. I already touched on EDGE Cian Slone & WR Shedrick Jackson , so check those out as well. T Dalton Wagner I really like the odds for Dalton Wagner this season, the former UDFA finally made his first NFL appearance late in the 2026 season but he should have a chance at his first initial 53 man roster in his fourth NFL season. Wagner, 27, is primarily a left tackle but has some experience working on the right side as well which will be crucial for his chances at the immediate roster. Wagner is a capable depth tackle, and Las Vegas currently only has 3 tackles that are clear to make the roster in Kolton Miller, DJ Glaze, and Charles Grant. Wagner’s biggest competition is a natural roster spot, along with UDFA Isaiah Jatta but his experience in the NFL for the last four seasons could give him a good chance at the roster. T Isaiah Jatta Jatta ended his college career strong at BYU, and he’s an incredible athlete which does play in his favor. Jatta has experience working on the left and right side, and his technique is advanced. A large reason for his fall to undrafted free agent came with the limited experience, along side a high rate of penalties (11) to end his college career in 2025. Jatta has the ability to play both tackle spots, and for a fourth tackle that is crucial. Unlike Wagner, who’s likely limited to being a full backup LT, Jatta can provide the Raiders with a stable floor at both spots should more than one tackle go down. The biggest question, for Jatta & Wagner, is if the Raiders are comfortable with Trey Zuhn at LT, then there’s a hard path forward for a 4th tackle. 🎥 CFB Draft Prospects I’m 👀 Tonight 🔹BYU OT Isaiah Jatta 🔹BYU WR Chase Roberts ♦️San Diego State CB Chris Johnson NFL Draft Day 3s IMO 📹H/T @BGauvin23 pic.twitter.com/YlWRtDI5O3 — Clint Goss (@NFLDraftDome) October 3, 2025 WR Chase Roberts Roberts is likely the most traditional “X” receiver the Raiders have, a sign of Klint Kubiak’s nonconventional offensive system. At 6’4, 200 Roberts was a previous potential round 4-6 receiver but a 2025 season that saw his contested catch rate fall, drops spike, and poor athletic testing he landed as an undrafted free agent. The Raiders paid Roberts the 2nd most UDFA money in their class, and 3rd most for a WR this cycle. He’s coming off back to back seasons with 50+ receptions, 800+ yards, and 5+ touchdowns, and while he’s not one to burn defenders downfield, Roberts can operate as a functional intermediate receiver with good route running but the drop issues will need to be sorted. The Raiders WR room could be sorted already, though if an injury or surprise struggle occurs, Roberts has a good chance. WR Brandon Johnson Johnson is someone I note for one reason, connections. While I believe he’ll land on the practice squad, Johnson does have good connections to the Raiders staff. In 2022, he played for the Broncos hauling in 6 receptions, 42 yards, and a touchdown on a staff that consisted of Klint Kubiak, and Raiders WR coach Zach Azzanni. Johnson played for the Broncos, and Azzanni, again in 2023 with 19 receptions, 284 yards, and four touchdowns before falling the receiver coach to Pittsburgh for 2024-2025 where he only logged 9 yards. Johnson is a physical receiver at 6’2, 195, and he’s a traditional big slot/Z receiver. While I don’t think he can push for the roster, and it would take an injury to someone such as Dont’e Thornton, Dareke Young, or others, he’s someone I can see getting a call into the season. Zach Wilson finds Brandon Johnson and the @Broncos are in business. 📺: #AZvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ 📱: Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Wfkn8lnOsA — NFL (@NFL) August 25, 2024 RB Roman Hemby I don’t know if this is a sleeper, more than someone I think will get more attention that initially discussed. I’m a fan of Mike Washington Jr, but there’s a few things the 4th rounder needs to work on, notably his ball security and ability to create for himself. If Washington struggles out of the gate, there’s a strong chance Dylan Laube (someone I could have touched on here) or Hemby get a chance into the RB2 role. Hemby is coming off a 2025 season with 230 attempts, 1120 yards, and 7 scores which were all career highs outside of touchdowns. He’s shown the ability to be a good receiver, and he’s a capable runningback that can develop into a consistent RB2/RB3 type in the NFL. Hemby isn’t someone I would write into 53 man rosters, but he’s not someone I’d assume is left off either. DT Treven Ma’ae The Raiders interior defensive line could be sorted as is with Thomas Booker, Adam Butler, Jonah Laulu, Tonka Hemingway, JJ Pegues, and one of Gary Smith/Benito Jones/Brandon Cleveland but if things get interesting, or an injury occurs, Ma’ae projects as one of the first in the room to step in. Ma’ae is exceptionally versatile, with nearly identical experience at 3, 2, 4, and 5 technique through his college career. The 6’5, 298 pound defensive tackle flashed in pre-season last year, and if he does so again it could be hard to keep him off the roster especially with his initial athleticism, versatility, and power. The Raiders interior defensive line is going to be asked to do a lot, and play in a ton of schemes, which Ma’ae’s versatility could play a big part in. ILB Xavian Sorey Jr Ironically, a teammate of Quay Walker & Nakobe Dean’s at Georgia, Sorey may have a chance to take a snap with them again in Las Vegas. The former Georgia linebacker enjoyed success the last two years at Arkansas with 180 tackles, 17 TFL, 4.5 sacks, 2 interceptions, and 5 PBU. Sorey is athletic, he diagnoses the run well, and there’s struggles in coverage but he’s been a sound tackler who uses his frame (6’2/220), athleticism, and initial movement skills downhill well. Additionally, Sorey has some experience on special teams which will be the biggest path for him to make the 53 man roster. Sorey is young, and an undrafted free agent, but linebacker often sees among the highest rates for UDFA’s to make the initial roster, and if he can play on special teams while flashing traits on defense, there’s a good chance. Las Vegas is going to carry Walker/Dean, Cody Lindenberg, Tommy Eichenberg, and Segun Olubi on the 53 man roster and a 6th linebacker is tough, but if Sorey makes it hard to leave him off things change. The 6’2, 195-pound cornerback is an athletic monster, and he’s developed over the last two years even if he hasn’t seen the field since 2024. Richardson’s rookie year was rough with a 65% completion rate (30/42), 459 yards, and 3 TD allowed for a 119.7 QBR while adding just 3 PBU. Richardson was relegated to a special teams role in 2025 playing just 13 defensive snaps. Heading into year three, it seems as if Richardson may already be on the way out but he very likely would land with another team off pure athleticism and upside. The special teams value in 2025 wasn’t bad with 10 tackles, and just 3 missed tackles, but the Raiders are also deep at cornerback. Eric Stokes, Taron Johnson, Darien Porter, Hezekiah Masses, and Jermod McCoy all figure to make the roster and if Las Vegas doesn’t want to carry 6, then the room is solidified, but Richardson has a chance, and he’ll have competition but I think he ends up on the roster but at the very bottom. He is looking to hold down the defensive tackle spot opposite Adam Butler and continue his rise, finishing last season with four sacks in the last five games. Albert Breer of Sports Illustrated was at Raiders training camp on Sunday, and the play of Hemingway was highlighted in his article. To that end, 2025 fourth-round pick Tonka Hemingway is emerging as a player to watch, with high-end natural athleticism that his college coaches and teammates at South Carolina told NFL folks about a couple years ago. He looks like he’s developing into a potential force as a 3-technique. Hemingway becoming a star will be another notch on the belt of John Spytek finding young players for this defense. Of course it is early, and Hemingway has to perform when the season starts, but his creating buzz already shows it could be the year he makes the leap. title: Jacob Rodriguez making an early impact on Dolphins training camp
summary: Miami Dolphins second-round draft pick, linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, is already making an impression as the team moves into its second week of training camp. The rookie is aggressive during practice, making plays all around the field while multiple responsibilities are thrown at him. His attacking mentality, getting after the ball to make stops and force […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - JUNE 03: Miami Dolphins linebacker Jacob Rodriguez (10) participates in drills during Miami Dolphins Minicamp on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 at Baptist Health Sports Center in Miami Gardens, FL (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Miami Dolphins second-round draft pick, linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, is already making an impression as the team moves into its second week of training camp. The rookie is aggressive during practice, making plays all around the field while multiple responsibilities are thrown at him. His attacking mentality, getting after the ball to make stops and force turnovers, is noticeable anytime he is in on a defensive repetition. “I think just trying to play the game the right way,” Rodriguez, who met with the media on Sunday, said of his attacking mentality at practice. “I think football is a physical game and it’s meant to be played that way. You have to be physical when you do it, whether you’re attacking a ball carrier or the ball specifically, it really doesn’t matter as long as you do it violently with the right technique and proper form. I feel like that’s how it’s got to be played.” The Dolphins are looking to be a much more physical team in 2026 than they were in the past few seasons, and a player like Rodriguez could be the spark to make that happen. His impact could take another step forward on Monday when the team puts on pads for this first time. “Yeah, I’m very excited for that,” the rookie said Sunday. “I think what we’ve been doing so far has been great. It’s helping us a lot with technique and where to use our hands and how to do a lot of the ins and outs and stuff. But football is played, like I said, physically, and when football pads come on and shoulder pads and everything else with it, you start to get to play real football. And so there is a timing to a football play, and so that will just help us kind of get better as a team of playing football the right way and the timing of kind of each play.” Learning from the veterans Rodriguez recognizes he is a rookie with an opportunity to learn from Miami’s veteran incumbent linebackers, Jordyn Brooks and Tyrel Dodson, as he figures out how to be a professional football player and what works for him at this level. “I think just how they go about every day,” he explained of what he is taking from Brooks and Dodson. “I know like Jordyn and T-Dot and those guys have been in the league for such a long time. Like they know how to go about like day to day. They know what routine works for them and what doesn’t, so they’ve just been speaking on how to like create that. What might work for them, has worked for them for years, might not work for me. And so just trying to go out and figure out what works for me and stick to it.” Forcing fumbles and the peanut punch The Texas Tech product brought with him from college a reputation of forcing fumbles, forcing an NCAA Division-1 high seven in 2025. He has already shown that ability at camp, using the “peanut punch,” a move popularized by former Chicago Bears cornerback Charles “Peanut” Tillman to knock the ball out of the arms of a runner as he is being tackled, during camp. “I think it’s more something that you work on and now is the time to work on it,” Rodriguez explained of his training camp efforts at knocking the ball loose. “It’s in practices and OTAs [organized team activities] and now, and so if I want to take chances in a game of taking the ball away, I want to put myself in all the different positions that I can be in a game right now. And so, shoot, I’ve gotten a couple out, but that’s not counting how many I’ve thrown, you know? So no, it hasn’t surprised me, but I’m definitely looking for more. Definitely looking to try to create as many ball strips as I can. “I actually got to meet Peanut Tillman, and so we talked for a little bit about how he does it. You always watch guys like [San Francisco 49ers linebacker] Fred [Warner] who, you know, play the game the right way and they punch on opportunity. I think kind of just, you watch it. It’s like anything else, like you study it on film and then you go out and try to practice it and then you bring it to a real-life situation. So it’s kind of that part to whole, that kind of stepping stone, that process to it.” Does Rodriguez ever worry about breaking his hand when executing a peanut punch? “I mean, the worry is there, but like, you got to do it, you know, like you got to take a chance to take the ball away. And I think you see what you punch,” he replied when asked. “It’s like a boxer, like if you see the ball, you punch it. If you’re just kind of throwing a blind punch, then that’s when it kind of gets risky and like you could actually hit a face mask and actually break a knuckle or something. But if you’re seeing what you’re punching, it should be fine.” Despite being a rookie, Rodriguez’s punching ability provides him an opportunity to serve as a teacher to other players as well. Are there any players who have asked him about adding the technique to their repertoire? “I mean, some guys come like jokingly and then we’ll kind of get into a conversation about it, but like, I’m all about, shoot, everybody trying to go and take the ball away,” the 2025 Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year explained. “Like if we can take three or more a game, what kind of stat that would help us to win, it would be unbelievable. So anything I could do to help everybody kind of take the ball away, not that I’m perfect at it or have it figured out, but I’ve just been fortunate enough to get a few.” Miami’s large rookie class Rodriguez is one piece of a huge rookie class for Miami this season, including 12 other drafted players. What is it like to have so many young players on the roster? Rodriguez embraces the opportunity to not only grow with the group, but to be a part of the team as a whole. “Yeah, it’s great. I think all of us are so eager to play and do as much as we can, but I think a big thing we talk about is just doing your role the best. Right now, it kind of doesn’t even feel like it’s just kind of us rookies, it feels like everybody; we’re all in the hotel, we’re all getting up here early and staying late and we’re all in it together. So it’s not just us rookies, it’s kind of everybody, but it just feels good to be doing hard stuff with people.” The media asked about fellow linebacker, Miami fourth-round draft pick Kyle Louis, with Rodriguez responding, “So Kyle is goofy all the time. That’s why he plays so well. It’s because he plays free and he just has fun, and his life is about football. That’s how you love guys in the locker room to be, so it’s nice that he’s in our room and we get to hang out a lot, but knowing him from the whole recruiting experience until now, it’s been fun to get a closer relationship with him and have a good time. But no, he’s definitely kind of more of a goofy guy who just loves to play free and fast so it’s something we like to see on the field.” Jeff Hafley’s defensive system and the roles of linebackers The Dolphins are introducing a new defense this year, with head coach Jeff Hafley bringing the system he ran as Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator to South Florida. The system has been asking for a lot from the linebackers already, with them filling multiple roles as blitzers, run stoppers, and in pass coverage. Rodriguez is embracing the system being installed and the multiple responsibilities he is being asked to fill. “I think just playing with your feet in the ground,” he explained of the pass-coverage role. “I think a lot of times if you start crossing over, if you pick your feet up, you just have both feet on the ground with your eyes on the quarterback and just ready to break. I think the more efficient breaks that we can get, the distance that we can cover before the ball is caught is kind of what we’re looking for, and then we go play ball from there.” He…

title: Jordan Addison Just Got Even More Expensive (Again)
summary: One of the questions that the Minnesota Vikings are going to have to come up with an answer for relatively soon is what to do with wide receiver Jordan Addison. They’ve already picked up the fifth-year option on his rookie contract, which would appear to be the precursor to a long-term extension with the purple, […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 9: Zay Flowers #4 of the Baltimore Ravens and Jordan Addison #3 of the Minnesota Vikings pose for a photo following an NFL football game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2025 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the questions that the Minnesota Vikings are going to have to come up with an answer for relatively soon is what to do with wide receiver Jordan Addison. They’ve already picked up the fifth-year option on his rookie contract, which would appear to be the precursor to a long-term extension with the purple, and such an extension just continues to get more and more expensive. On Tuesday morning, the Baltimore Ravens announced that they had signed wide receiver Zay Flowers to a four-year, $140 million contract extension with $108 million in guaranteed money. Those terms are nearly identical to the extension that Justin Jefferson signed two years ago. Jefferson’s extension was also a four-year, $140 million pact with $110 million guaranteed. So, Zay Flowers is, officially, making “Justin Jefferson money.” Flowers and Addison went with back-to-back picks in the 2023 NFL Draft, with the Ravens taking Flowers at #22 overall and the Vikings selecting Addison at #23. Thus far in their careers, Flowers has the edge in receptions (237 to 175) and receiving yardage (3,128 to 2,396, with Flowers going over the 1,000-yard mark twice), while Addison has found the end zone more times than Flowers has (22 touchdowns to 14). Of course, Addison has had to compete with Jefferson for catches, which causes his numbers to take a bit of a hit. Flowers has led the Ravens in receptions in each of his three NFL seasons, while Addison has been the clear #2 wide receiver in the Minnesota offense. Them’s the breaks, I guess. Still, given this contract extension, its tough to imagine a contract extension for Addison coming in below this sort of level. That means the Vikings could, potentially, be paying two wide receivers “Justin Jefferson money,” with one of those receivers being the Justin Jefferson, who is still, arguably, the best wide receiver in football. I know that the Vikings still employ Rob Brzezinski, who is still one of the premiere cap guys in the business. Still, this could prove to be one of the first tests of Nolan Teasley’s priorities as GM of the Vikings. Handling this contract situation with Jordan Addison could prove to be tricky, and it will be interesting to see how the new front office handles it and, just as importantly, when they handle it. After all, I don’t think Addison is going to get any cheaper if the team puts it off or anything.

title: Vikings Training Camp Day 5: Defense Wins, Murray Leads QB Battle
summary: The Minnesota Vikings held their first padded training camp practice at TCO Performance Center, and The Real Forno Show‘s Tyler Forness was there live to break it all down. The headline: the defense dominated, Kyler Murray is outpacing J.J. McCarthy in the quarterback competition, and a fifth-round rookie cornerback may be stealing the show. Here’s […]
full_text: EAGAN, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 01: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings participates in a drill during Training Camp at Twin Cities Orthopedics Performance Center on August 01, 2026 in Eagan, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings held their first padded training camp practice at TCO Performance Center, and The Real Forno Show ‘s Tyler Forness was there live to break it all down. The headline: the defense dominated, Kyler Murray is outpacing J.J. McCarthy in the quarterback competition, and a fifth-round rookie cornerback may be stealing the show. Here’s everything Vikings fans need to know from Day 5 of camp. QB Battle Update: Processing Speed Is the Defining Factor The quarterback competition is the story of this camp, and Tyler Forness laid out the clearest picture yet of where things stand. J.J. McCarthy showed improvement over his rough Saturday outing — completing his first three passes and flashing some nice throws — but the same persistent issue remains. “The consistency of the processing is, I think, gonna be the biggest differentiating factor between the two. Murray has it, and McCarthy is still too slow.” — Tyler Forness Forness was pointed about what McCarthy must fix to win the job: “He has to fix that because you watch the talent, he can throw a football. He can do a lot of things. He’s a good leader… But this consistency element and processing, those are two things he does not have, and if he is going to win this job, those are the two things that he needs to have.” Meanwhile, Kyler Murray impressed with his veteran intuition and decision-making, particularly in seven-on-seven drills. A standout moment: Murray cycled through his progressions, found Tai Felton breaking away from coverage, and delivered a perfectly placed ball to the pylon for one of the best catches of camp. “That’s more of, I think, veteran intuition where, ‘Okay, I have nowhere to go with this football, but I need to give my receiver a chance.’ That’s the perfect kind of ball.” — Tyler Forness Key Practice Takeaways — Vikings Training Camp Day 5 Defense won the day — Dallas Turner drew chips from the offensive line, and Ivan Pace was flying around making plays, including a notable pass breakup in 11-on-11 drills J.J. McCarthy recovered from a poor Saturday but processing speed remains the key gap vs. Murray Kyler Murray flashed veteran poise, layered deep over routes with consistency, but threw a concerning late ball to Jordan Addison Tai Felton made arguably the catch of camp, a leaping, one-handed, toe-tap grab at the pylon Myles Price looked noticeably quicker and shiftier, creating six yards of separation on an in-breaking route in one-on-ones Charles “Chuck” Demmings , a fifth-round pick out of Stephen F. Austin (FCS), shadowed Justin Jefferson stride-for-stride in coverage — Forness called him a potential steal Blake Cashman is out with an undisclosed injury; Kevin O’Connell is expected to speak with media soon Jadeveon Clowney signed with the Houston Texans, thinning an already slim edge rusher free agent market for Minnesota Defensive scheme: Forness flagged a developing 3-3-5 defensive look under Brian Flores, utilizing the linebacker trio of Golda, Cashman, and Wilson as key blitzers A Rookie Corner Turning Heads One of the most compelling stories from camp is fifth-round cornerback Charles Demmings. After holding up against Jordan Addison and Justin Jefferson in one-on-one drills, Demmings continued his strong camp by running step-for-step with Jauan Jennings on a seam route and blanketing Jefferson on a corner route. Forness was effusive: “I think Chuck Demmings is a good player.
