title: Eli Apple is a cautionary tale for NY Giants CB Deonte Banks
summary: Former New York Giants cornerback Eli Apple was released by the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. It is possibe that will be the end of the NFL line for Apple, who has played just six games the past two seasons. That, in and of itself, is probably only a mild curiosity for Giants fans. After […]
full_text: New York Giants cornerback Deonte Banks | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Former New York Giants cornerback Eli Apple was released by the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. It is possibe that will be the end of the NFL line for Apple, who has played just six games the past two seasons. That, in and of itself, is probably only a mild curiosity for Giants fans. After all, it’s been about seven years since the former first round pick played for the Giants, and many Giants fans likely forgot Apple was even in the NFL. The Giants traded Apple to the New Orleans Saints after five games in 2018, and he has since played for the Carolina Panthers, Cincinnati Bengals, Miami Dolphins, Los Angeles Chargers, and then the 49ers. It remains to be seen if this is where Apple’s story in the NFL ends, but it still serves as a cautionary tale for the Giants and their 2023 first-round pick, Deonte Banks. There are a somewhat uncomfortable number of parallels between Banks and Apple. Both are former first-round picks who were heralded for an elite blend of size and athleticism coming out of college. Both flashed the potential to be good, perhaps even great, press man coverage specialists early in their careers. And both regressed over the following years as questions mounted. Some in the Giants’ fandom and media are ready to move on from Banks as well, tossing him in the dustbin of history as yet another bust. That said, Apple and Banks are two different men and their paths can absolutely diverge. As of this writing, Banks remains on the Giants, and was recently moved into the “lock” category to make the roster in Ed’s recent 53-man roster forecast. And at the very least, Banks may have secured his continued roster spot by emerging as a great kick returner. If that’s all he’s able to be, it’s a disappointing outcome for a former first-round cornerback, but still a useful piece for the Giants. The new kick-off rules are confusing and frustrating, but they do accomplish the goal of making the play matter in a way it didn’t until recently. A great kick returner can change the complexion of a game, and the Giants would certainly enjoy having their own Devin Hester. That said, if the Giants and Banks want to avoid his career path mirroring Apple’s, it falls to Addison Lynch and Dennard Wilson to help him realize his potential. And so far there has been more than, perhaps, a glimmer of hope over the course of spring and summer practices. Banks started out as a second team corner, but has worked his way into meaningful snaps with the starters. In fact, Banks has reportedly looked good enough in his opportunities that he’s counted among the pleasant surprises in the first week of camp. He has, reportedly, been sticky in coverage and has gotten his hands on passes – though he still struggles to haul them in for interceptions. Witness the bad drop Banks had on Monday. Athletic ability has never been a question for Banks, rather he’s struggled with consistency. “We tried to show him that his consistency was his deal,” defensive backs coach Addison Lynch said of Banks earlier in the off-season. “He just wasn’t consistent getting lined up fast, wasn’t consistent with his feet. He’s improved his consistency, so now his play is improved, now his confidence is up and he can just roll into the season.” For his part, Dennard Wilson (likely) wants to run a defense that uses man-match coverage, an aggressive variation of Cover 4 that uses post-snap coverage rules to transform a zone defense into a physical man coverage scheme. It’s a versatile scheme that deals with modern offenses well and is used by many defensive minds in the “Ravens 2.0” school. It would also play to Banks’ strengths in man coverage, but the versatile nature stresses defenders’ processing. That’s been an issue for Banks over the last two years under Shane Bowen, but Lynch may have reached Banks in a way that coaches were never able to with Apple. “I love how he’s handling it,” Lynch said. “Right now, he’s being an absolute pro. He’s doing the extra work, he’s in his book, he’s doing everything we ask him. He’s making plays on the ball and he’s doing a really good job handling himself play in and play out. He’s made major improvements that when he’s tired, he relies on his technique and he’s getting more technically sound, so everything with him is trending in the right direction.” Ultimately, while some may be done with Banks or believe he’s soon to be another former Giant, the Giants themselves should want him to blossom under Wilson and Lynch. He has rare athletic traits and if teams want to build through the draft, they need to develop the players they draft. Apple was never able to realize his potential with the Giants (or anyone else, for that matter), but that doesn’t mean Banks has to follow the same path. There’s still time for him to become the player the Giants hoped they were getting in 2023.
author: Chris Pflum

title: NY Giants training camp, practice No. 6: Discussion, news, updates
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — The New York Giants will be on the field for their sixth practice of training camp on Tuesday afternoon. Head coach John Harbaugh said on Monday that this second week is “the big week of camp.” It is the week when the Giants will be in pads for practice more […]
full_text: John Harbaugh watches Monday’s practice. | Getty Images WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — The New York Giants will be on the field for their sixth practice of training camp on Tuesday afternoon. Head coach John Harbaugh said on Monday that this second week is “ the big week of camp .” It is the week when the Giants will be in pads for practice more often than at any other time this season. Veteran defensive tackle D.J. Reader , in his 11th NFL training camp, understands the importance of the physical work padded practices allow. “You’ve got to callous the body. The thing that’s important in football is callousing the body to be ready to take on those blows throughout the season, because you’re going to get chinks in your armor, and if you didn’t build your armor up enough to be able to withstand those hits, those dents, those little scratches you’ll take in your armor, then shame on you,” Reader said. “I think it’s important to be able to callous the body. Do it with intent. Be smart about it, but you have to callous the body to go out there and play this game. You’re not just going to roll out there, roll out of bed, and be able to go out there on Sundays and get it done.” A couple of things to watch on Tuesday: Penalties — There were at least a dozen, probably more, during the team periods on Monday. Harbaugh was understanding because of the circumstances. Let’s see if Tuesday’s practice is cleaner. Veteran offensive lineman Jermaine Eluemunor knew Monday afternoon was unlikely to be as understanding during the team’s film session. “Obviously we’re going to see them all. He’s going to call everyone out in front of the team, but also you just got to know that you got to be better,” Eluemunor said. “Me, obviously, I think some of them were BS, but it’s whatever. Had a couple penalties last year. So, I think penalties are worse than sacks because it can affect the team. It can affect the drive. It can affect the momentum. And everyone on the team understands that. So, you got to take your licks and then come back out tomorrow and be better.” Offensive struggles — The offense is making some plays. Nothing, though, is coming easily. Part of that is strong play from the defense. Part of it is the time of year, with defenses traditionally ahead of offenses. Still, we haven’t yet had a day that was clearly won by the offense. Could today be the day? Funny moment from Monday In my rain-soaked state, I neglected to put this tidbit in Monday’s practice report . So, here it is. At the end of practice, defensive players were doing pushups — 10 for each of the four penalties they committed. At the end of his daily media session, Harbaugh complained about the quality of those pushups. “You know the thing that bothers me about their push-ups? They don’t go all the way up. You go all the way down, touch your chest on the ground, and you go all the way up and extend,” Harbaugh said. “But they kind of do this little, short push-up thing.” So, as he was about to exit the podium I mentioned to him that he should demonstrate the proper form to his team. Harbaugh glared at me for a few seconds, which seemed like a few minutes. Then he said: “Good point. I’m the coach, right?” Join the conversation! title: NY Giants RB Tyrone Tracy not worried about being overshadowed by Cam Skattebo
summary: Cam Skattebo is the New York Giants running back who gets all of the attention from fans and media. It is Tyrone Tracy, though, who is coming off back-to-back seasons of 1,000 or more yards from scrimmage.Does Tracy ever feel overlooked? “Not really,” Tracy said on Monday. “When you say he gets all the attention, […]
full_text: Tyrone Tracy | Getty Images Cam Skattebo is the New York Giants running back who gets all of the attention from fans and media. It is Tyrone Tracy, though, who is coming off back-to-back seasons of 1,000 or more yards from scrimmage. Does Tracy ever feel overlooked? “Not really,” Tracy said on Monday. “When you say he gets all the attention, I really don’t care about that, to be honest. I’m about football. About what I do on the field, how I carry myself on the field and off the field as well. But at the same time, I’m going to go out there and do what I need to do at the end of the day.” A fifth-round pick by the Giants in 2024, Tracy had 1,123 scrimmage yards as a rookie and 1,028 last season. He did not begin either of those seasons as the team’s No. 1 running back. What the Giants actually have at running back is a 1a and 1b with Skattebo and Tracy, whichever order you put them in. Tyrone Tracy says he does not feel overlooked because of the attention paid to fellow #NYG RB Cam Skattebo. pic.twitter.com/WMbG2lTa7q — Big Blue View (@bigblueview) August 4, 2026 Head coach John Harbaugh said Tracy will have “a big role” for the Giants. “Both those guys are going to be together back there playing a lot of football,” Harbaugh said. “You can’t play with one back anyway, and they’re both competing for everything at this point in time. Against themselves, against each other, against the opponent, against the defense. Both those guys are going to play a lot.” Tracy understands the assignment. “Iron sharpens iron, so he’s going to push me, I’m going to push him,” Tracy said. “And, obviously, we are two different running backs, so I think we complement each other really well. So, it’s not necessarily like me against him, but best believe that I’m going to push him to be the best that he can be, and he’s going to push me to be the best that I can be each and every day. Whether it’s running the ball, passing, blocking, being a good teammate. “Obviously, Skatt’s really loud. He’s loud. He’s a great leader, so that’s allowing me to be – pushing me to be a great leader as well. Each and every thing that we’re doing, I’m trying to challenge him, and he’s going to challenge me. So, I think we complement each other really well.” Tracy said all of the Giants’ running backs understand that Harbaugh wants an offense that leans on the run game. “We want to run the ball. I think if you look at Harbaugh and where he’s been, and all the running backs that he’s used really his whole career, they’ve all been successful,” Tracy said. “So, when he came here, we were all excited. You’ve got a running coach that’s coming to you, so as a running back room, we’re excited for him to be here, to be honest.” The mastermind behind the Giants’ run game is senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, a four-time offensive coordinator with a reputation for designing run concepts. “I think he has his schemes, to be honest. His schemes are so different. I’m sitting there in awe, really, each and every time he gets up to talk. He’s very detailed. He knows exactly what he’s talking about,” Tracy said. “If he says it’s going to be this way versus a certain look, I promise you, you go out there, and that look is going to end up exactly what he says. So, he’s been around the game. He’s been around winning teams. College level, too. When he was at Stanford, I think he said he ran the ball; one guy had like 40 carries one game for 200, 300 yards. He’s been around the game a long time. He has the stats to back it up, and he’s very knowledgeable. “So, Coach Ro, I mean, you can’t really say enough about him. He’s a good coach. Great coach with a lot of knowledge.” Tracy explained a little more about the run scheme. “There’s really no gray area, and it’s not just one way to run the ball,” Tracy said. “He’s calling the same run, but out of different formations, different motions, different pullers. There’s a whole bunch of different stuff going on, but again, he’s making it very simple and easy for us to learn.” Tracy said offensive coordinator Matt Nagy wants the offense to “look complicated to the defense, but simple to us as an offense.” “We want to be explosive,” Tracy said. “We want to move the ball down the field, and I think the way we’re doing that is being simple but also making the defense think a little bit.” Tracy, even if he doesn’t get much attention, will be a big part of it.
author: Ed Valentine

summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the Giants stories you need to know for Tuesday morning. full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the Giants stories you need to know for Tuesday morning. The four-word approach that has Arvell Reese destined to be a Giants’ menace | New York Post They smile, or even chuckle, at the mere mention of No. 52. A star is being born at Camp Harbaugh and his name is Arvell Reese. The prized rookie was the best player on the field on a penalty-filled day under a drenching rain when the pads came on for the first time. He was everywhere … in the backfield for a sack against left tackle Andrew Thomas, for a TFL, and on a couple of other occasions when he looked like a human magnet tracking device. On both sides of the ball, they are gushing about Arvell Reese. “No. 52 — that boy!” Tyrone Tracy Jr. said. “He’s big, strong, physical. He’s a great football player. “Arvell is See Ball, Get Ball. “I think that’s the best way to describe him: See Ball, Get Ball. He’s gonna run fast, he’s gonna hit hard and he’s gonna be around the ball at all times.” Giants running backs embracing ‘opportunity to show ourselves’ in John Harbaugh’s system | New York Post “We don’t see it as a lot of weight on our shoulders, we see it as opportunity,” said Tyrone Tracy Jr., who is coming off back-to-back seasons with more than 1,000 yards from scrimmage. “Opportunity to show ourselves, opportunity to really show the NFL who we are and what we can be. I think we can be a premier running back group.” Veteran receiver becoming QBs’ safety blanket as Giants rookie keeps big plays coming | New York Post Calvin Austin is emerging as a major security blanket for all the quarterbacks. Giants’ Arvell Reese flashes game-changing potential; Jaxson Dart, offense sputter again | The Athletic What happened while the Giants practiced in the rain. Why Jaxson Dart, Giants offense have scuffled early, and why John Harbaugh isn’t worried | The Athletic The goal for the New York Giants never was to have quarterback Jaxson Dart operating at his peak at the start of August. It was understood that it was going to be a process as Dart acclimated to a new offense. The expected growing pains have been evident in the first four practices of training camp. title: NY Giants training camp, practice No. 5: Arvell Reese dominates
summary: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — The New York Giants held their first padded practice of 2026 training camp on Monday, a sloppy, one-hour, 45-minute that began in a sprinkle, went for about an hour in a torrential downpour, and finished in heat and bright sunshine. “(Former) college (football) coach Tom Reed used to always tell […]
full_text: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — The New York Giants held their first padded practice of 2026 training camp on Monday, a sloppy, one-hour, 45-minute that began in a sprinkle, went for about an hour in a torrential downpour, and finished in heat and bright sunshine. “(Former) college (football) coach Tom Reed used to always tell us every single day, rain, sleet, snow, hot, it’s a great day for football. Every day.,” said head coach John Harbaugh. “We’d look at each other, really not that great a day, but he would say every day is a great day for football. “And that was kind of a little bit of the theme out here. I mean, it’s raining pretty good. And the guys are out there dealing with the elements, obviously impactful, but we’ll have to play in that at some point in time. So, we got a good day in the rain, and that was positive.” There were at least a dozen penalties, perhaps as many as 14, during the 11-on-11 portions of practice. Moat of those were false starts, though there were offside penalties, defensive pass interference, and offensive and defensive holding calls, as well. Harbaugh was surprisingly understanding of the sloppiness. “I think two things. I mean, I think you’ve got the elements a little bit and you’ve got the first day in pads,” Harbaugh said after practice, when it was sunny outside. “So, it’s not really unexpected, but we’ll be working on it.” False start penalties have been prevalent through the first five practices. Harbaugh said that might be due to the “absolutely designed” cadences the Giants are working into their offense. “Part of the offense has a lot of elements of cadence. I mean, that’s part of it. Cadence is something that we hope to use as a weapon, so to speak. It slows the defense down and keeps them honest a little bit, but you have to work at it. There’s got to be growing pains with that,” Harbaugh said. “If you don’t work through it, then you’re not going to get good at it. So yeah, it’s kind of tough on the offense, too. They have to get used to it in a lot of different circumstances. Play clock’s running down, we’ve got motions and shifts. They’ve got to remember a lot of things at the line of scrimmage in terms of calls and which linebacker we’re going to or whatever it might be. And then you’ve got play count or cadence, things that you have to execute. So, all that stuff going together is stuff that you’re working on. “It’s, what, the fifth day in camp right now? We’ll just keep working on that stuff. The goal is to get really good at it, and that’s what we’ll have to do. So, it’s not unexpected this early for that to be the case.” Winners The defense overall — The defense has had the better of the offense throughout most of the early part of training camp. That was the case again Monday. The offense had moments, but on a play-to-play basis the defense was clearly better than the offense. “I thought the defense probably got the better of the offense today up front,” Harbaugh said. “We’ll see it on tape, probably going to be the case. But we got a few plays out in the run game on offense, too, so I’m really looking forward to seeing it. “Everybody always says the defense is ahead of the offense early in camp. Probably found that to be true over the years, so it seems to be the case.” Arvell Reese — Somebody forgot to give the rookie linebacker the memo that there was no live tackling in practice. Reese dumped Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy at the line of scrimmage. He had a sack of Jaxson Dart, where he fortunately remembered not to hit the red jersey. Impressively, that sack came on a blitz with Andrew Thomas the nearest offensive lineman. Reese also had a couple of nice plays in coverage. Harbaugh said he was “very encouraged” by the play of the team’s No. 5 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. “I think he looked good today from what I could see.,” Harbaugh said. “I can’t wait to see the tape, but he’s playing really well. He’s been playing well the whole camp since he got here. “You see the talent, obviously. I think he’s very sharp for a first-year guy. He gets things right pretty much all the time, makes very few mistakes. He’s a very serious-minded guy, and he’s very determined.” Micah McFadden — After missing all but a dozen snaps last season due to a foot injury, McFadden is no longer a starter at inside linebacker. He reminded everyone on Monday, though, that he is a useful player. McFadden had an interception off a tipped ball, at least one tackle for loss, and a couple of other good plays in coverage. Calvin Austin — The dimimutive slot receiver has made plays every day thus far in camp, with Monday being more of the same. “Calvin’s had a heck of a camp,” Harbaugh said. “He runs the routes really well. He gets open. He makes catches. He deserves some attention, no doubt. He’s having a good camp so far.” Dalen Cambre — The second-year wide receiver had the play of the day for the offense. In the driving rain, Cambre leaped to take a deep 50-50 ball away from cornerback Korie Black. When the ball popped into the air, a stumbling Cambre grabbed it for a long catch before falling out of bounds. Losers My notebook — There was no protecting my notebook from the pouring rain. It is now in tatters, with some pages having simply disingtegrated, others being completely illegible, and me now questioning whether this notebook will dry sufficiently for me to use it again this week. Oh, one other thing. I am big fan of nice pens, especially gel pens. I knew this already, but gel pens are disastrous in the rain. There will be a basic stick pen in my pocket the rest of the week. Tae Banks’ hands — Toward the end of practice, as the sun had come out and things began to dry out a bit, a jotted a few potential winners and losers in my notebook. Banks was in the ‘winners’ column. He had a tipped ball that led to McFadden’s interception early in practice, then a nice play in run support that ened with a tackle for loss. Then, Jameis Winston lofted a pass toward the left pylon. The ball was at least 5 yards off target and Banks, looking like a centerfielder waiting for a fly ball, was alone waiting for the catch. Only, he didn’t make the catch. The ball fell through his fingers to the grass. The amount of time the mortified Banks, who has struggled with ball skills throughout his career, took to get back to the huddle showed he knew how bad that drop was. An important week The Giants have five more practices before leaving West Virginia to return to East Rutherford, N.J. Harbaugh said the Giants will be in pads for “most of them.” “This is a big week. The second week is the big week of camp. This is your opportunity to really grow as a football team,” Harbaugh said. “We always say the second everything. The second day, the second game, the second week of camp. You build your foundation in training camp for your team. The second week should be where you cover the most miles, gain the most ground. We want to put the most miles behind us as far as developing the foundation of our team this week. “This is just a go-to-work week. Just get to work and get better. That’s really what we’re focusing on this week. Not too much evaluating, just more really trying to build this week. You really have to build this week, and that’s what this week is for.” Remaining Greenbrier practice schedule Tuesday, August 4 — 1:30-3:30 p.m. Wednesday, August 5 — 1:30-4 p.m. (Open to the public) Thursday, August 6 — 1:30-4 p.m. (Open to the public) Friday, August 7 — 1:30-4 p.m. (Open to the public) Saturday, August 8 — 10 a.m. – 12:30 p.m.

full_text: WHITE SULPHUR SPRINGS, W.Va. — Pads come on Monday for the first time in New York Giants training camp. “It’ll just change the tempo of the period. Without the pads, you’re not wrapping. We’re not going to be tackling to the ground on Monday. We’ll be doing what we call wrap and release,” said head coach John Harbaugh. “We’re trying to stop the ballcarrier if we can on defense and get the pads behind us on offense, things like that. I’m sure inside will be a little more physical than it is out here without the shoulder pads. It just ramps up just a little bit. But other than that, everything will be exactly the same.” Fans will not be allowed at practice Monday or Tuesday. Be sure to come back after practice for a breakdown what happened. summary: The New York Giants are hard at work in their 2026 training camp, which is currently being hosted by The Greenbrier Resort. Jaxson Dart has produced highlight plays throwing to free agent tight end Isaiah Likely, rookie […]
full_text: Jaxson Dart (6) with Darius Slayton during training camp. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants are hard at work in their 2026 training camp, which is currently being hosted by The Greenbrier Resort. So far, the returns have been positive, starting with wide receiver Malik Nabers returning to the practice field. Jaxson Dart has produced highlight plays throwing to free agent tight end Isaiah Likely, rookie receiver Malachi Fields, and veteran Odell Beckham Jr. On the flip side, the Giants’ defense has been incredibly disruptive after a slow start on the first day of camp that featured multiple dropped interceptions — of course, you can’t drop interceptions if you aren’t getting your hands on the ball. Since then, the Giants’ pass rush has been all but dominant and the secondary has been disruptive, preventing the offense from finding much of a rhythm at all. We’re moving into a new phase of camp as the players don their pads on Monday, which will doubtless ratchet up the intensity. We’ll see how the defense responds when the offensive line is in pads and able to play more roughly. So we wanted to use the opportunity to take the temperature of the fanbase: How are you feeling about the Giants after the first week of camp? Are you hyped up and believe the Giants are ready to compete with the Cowboys and Rams to start the year? Are you cautiously optimistic? Encouraged by the news coming out of camp but not ready to buy in yet? Are you cautiously pessimistic? Guarding your heart after having been hurt by promising off-seasons before? Or are you out completely? Do you believe that the Giants lack the talent and no coaching can speed up what needs to be multi-year rebuild? Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Giants fans and fans across the country. title: Scouting Jets wide receiver Quincy Skinner
summary: The Jets’ first personnel move of training camp was to sign wide receiver Quincy Skinner to replace the injured Jalen Walthall. Today, we break Skinner down in detail. The 23-year old Skinner is listed at 6’2” and 205 pounds and caught 66 passes for 809 yards and eight touchdowns in four seasons at Vanderbilt. He […]
full_text: FLOWERY BRANCH, GA - JULY 26: Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Quincy Skinner Jr. #36 runs a route during Atlanta Falcons training camp on July 26, 2025 at IBM Performance Field in Flowery Branch, GA. (Photo by Jeff Robinson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Jets’ first personnel move of training camp was to sign wide receiver Quincy Skinner to replace the injured Jalen Walthall. Today, we break Skinner down in detail. The 23-year old Skinner is listed at 6’2” and 205 pounds and caught 66 passes for 809 yards and eight touchdowns in four seasons at Vanderbilt. He spent time with the Falcons as an undrafted rookie last year. Background Skinner – who is not to be confused with Quentin Skinner, another wide receiver who until last month was with the Jets but is now in Buffalo – was a three-star high school recruit. He headed to Vanderbilt, where he made eight appearances in his freshman season but only played two offensive snaps. His second season, in 2022, saw him start contributing as a rotational receiver. He had 17 catches for 238 yards and two scores. His role continued to increase in 2023 and he caught 20 passes for 204 yards and three scores. 2024 saw him start 12 of 13 games and post career-best numbers with 29 receptions and 367 yards. He added another three touchdowns. The Falcons picked Skinner up as an undrafted free agent after the 2025 draft and he caught three passes for 29 yards in preseason but did not make the team. Skinner was signed by the Jets on the second day of training camp, following an injury to Walthall. Let’s move onto some more in-depth analysis of what Skinner brings to the table, based on in-depth research and film study. Measurables/Athleticism Skinner’s workout numbers at his pro day were disappointing. He ran just 4.59 in the 40-yard dash, and posted a poor vertical and disappointing agility numbers. His broad jump (123 inches) and bench press (17 reps) were solid, though. Usage Skinner has primarily played on the outside both at Vanderbilt and in his preseason action with the Falcons. He played in the slot about 10 percent of the time in college, but it was less than that in his final year. He carried once in his college career, gaining 22 yards on an end around. Deep threat Skinner only had two plays of longer than 40 yards during his college career, but did make several downfield catches as he showed a good ability to track and locate the ball. He was targeted down the field more often in his final season but his success rate on such throws was lower. Hands Skinner caught 71 percent of his targets in 2022 but his catch rate dropped to 64 percent in 2023 and 60 in 2024. To some extent the 2024 drop can be explained by the fact he was targeted downfield more often than in 2022 but that wasn’t the case in 2023 when he was targeted on more shorter routes. His drop rate was solid in his first two seasons, as he had just one drop in each season. However, he had five in 2024. Skinner has a big catch radius and can use this to go up and get high throws and has shown a good ability to lay out for diving catches, and concentration on low throws. Routes Skinner shows some decent raw route running skills, as he looks smooth on his release and shows good deception and change of direction abilities. As alluded to earlier, he had more of a possession role in 2023 but was targeted more on downfield throws in 2024. His success rate doing the latter was not that high, but some of this was down to the quarterback play as he did show the ability to get open. Red zone Although he only had eight touchdown catches in his college career, Skinner did make a few nice plays in the red zone and has shown that he can be someone you can throw it up to (even though he will have to adjust to getting two feet down under the NFL’s rules). In addition to those eight touchdowns, he also scored on two two-point conversions. After the catch Skinner’s numbers after the catch are nothing special and he doesn’t break many tackles. However, he does have a few highlights of this nature. He wasn’t particularly successful on screen passes during his college career, averaging less than four yards per play when targeted behind the line. Skinner had one fumble during his college career. Run Blocking Skinner’s performance grades as a run blocker on sites such as Pro Football Focus were generally pretty good and the film backs this up as he is an effective contributor who gives a good effort, uses his size well and gets after it. He was called for offensive holding downfield on a quarterback scramble in his final season of college. Physicality Skinner had mixed results on contested catches during his career, with his success rate dropping off in his final season but did make some good plays when tightly covered. He had a 79-yard touchdown catch in college that was called back because he was flagged for offensive pass interference. Special Teams Skinner saw some action in his freshman year as a blocker on the kick return unit and in kick coverage, but didn’t generate any production and then barely played on special teams after that during his college career. With Atlanta, he blocked on the kick return unit and played as a vice and rusher on the punt return unit. He had one play where the gunner beat him cleanly on a punt return (although he missed the tackle), but impressed with his physicality on the kickoff return unit here. Instincts and Intelligence Skinner displays the ability to read coverages and time his route to find the soft spot in the zone. He also typically executed his blocking assignments well. In addition, it is also impressive how early he tracks and locates the ball when it is in the air. He was flagged for two pre-snap penalties in 2024, though. Attitude Skinner was someone whose coaching staff at Vanderbilt praised him for growing into a role as a vocal leader in the wide receiver room over the course of his career. His on-field discipline was solid as he had just five penalties in his career, although four were in 2024. Injuries Skinner played in 41 games in college and doesn’t seem to have had any issues with missing time for injury related reasons. Scheme Fit Skinner will look to get in the mix on the outside and should see time there in preseason, if he lasts that long. During his time with the Falcons, Skinner was a teammate of current Jets defensive lineman David Onyemata. Conclusions Skinner will be a long-shot to make the Jets’ roster, of course. However, he’s a player they worked out a while back and obviously kept on their watchlist so they will be keen to get a longer look. If he can impress in preseason, Skinner might have a shot at sticking around so he can try to compete for a role next season. His measurables, production and lack of any elite traits would tend to suggest this is unlikely, but there were a few impressive moments on film that show he might be capable of making some things happen.

The team is hoping to improve on a difficult 2025 campaign that saw the team finish with a 3-14 record. The team was very active in free agency and made four picks in the top 50 of the NFL Draft. title: Eagles News: Moro Ojomo was asked about his contract outlook
summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … ‘I can’t be thinking about that:’ Moro Ojomo opens up on his contract and future – NBCSPMoro Ojomo couldn’t be happier for his fellow defensive linemen, Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter, for getting huge new contracts. Even though deep down we all know what it […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JULY 30: Moro Ojomo #97 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during training camp at Jefferson Health Training Complex on July 30, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … ‘I can’t be thinking about that:’ Moro Ojomo opens up on his contract and future – NBCSP Moro Ojomo couldn’t be happier for his fellow defensive linemen, Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter, for getting huge new contracts. Even though deep down we all know what it means. It means Ojomo most likely won’t be here next year. Because nobody – even Howie Roseman – can pay big money to three interior linemen. And the way he’s been going, Ojomo is on track for pretty hefty payday. Ojomo said after practice Monday he can’t afford to think about his future. Because if he does, that means he’s not focused on what’s really important. “I think that when you get into those thoughts that it can be a rabbit hole,” he said. “So I’d rather kind of steer clean from them. At the end of the day, we’ve got a football season to play. I’ve got an agent and he’s hired for a reason, so he needs to do his job and (I’ll) do my job and we’ll see what happens.” As a 7th-round pick, Ojomo got a four-year rookie contract worth just $923,362 per year, which ranks outside the 250 highest-paid interior linemen in the NFL. Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Jalen Hurts strikes back – BGN JALEN HURTS UPDATE: Monday was a bounce back performance from Hurts and the offense after they were bested by Vic Fangio’s defense in the previous two practices. Encouraging to see. Mailbag: What simple improvements can the Eagles’ offense make? – PhillyVoice Question from @irisheagles (from Bluesky): Based on your limited viewing thus far, most likely UDFA to make the team. (Not named Rocco Underwood) My guy so far is S Maximus Pulley. Pulley had 85 tackles and 5 INTs (including two pick-sixes) for Wofford in 2025. He posted some All-22 of his highlights on YouTube. That’s a fun watch. Pulley reads quarterbacks’ eyes and makes big plays on the football against the pass, and he loves triggering downhill hunting tackles for loss in the run game. Fun player. In camp so far, he’s been around the football a lot when he has gotten reps, and he’s looked fearless playing the run. (Also, I don’t love what I have seen from Underwood so far. He has had some high snaps on punts, and as we pointed out in our Day 4 notes, the spin on his field goal snaps is imprecise.) Camp Notes – Good Day for Offense – Iggles Blitz We have talked about how deep this group is. They are going to make final cuts tough on Howie Roseman and the coaching staff. There are three locks. DeVonta Smith, Makai Lemon, Dontayvion Wicks. Hollywood Brown is a notch below that. He’s likely to make the roster, but does have to earn it. I’m guessing Cooper is in the lead for the number five spot now. There is a case for Wilson and Moore. Wilson has unique size at 6-6, 228 and is a good blocker. He’s willing to do the dirty work. Moore has good experience and has been a workhorse receiver in the past. Cooper seems to be playing the best for now and that has him in the lead. Lemon missed the team portion of practice today. Jeff McLane reported that it was due to an injury, but isn’t anything too serious. Eagles training camp diary: Jalen Hurts shines while rain moves practice indoors – The Athletic 10:52 a.m.: This is the play of the day and the best pass I’ve seen Hurts make all summer. He throws a dart to Moore deep down the middle of the field, placing the ball in a perfect spot over defenders for Moore to make the catch with nobody in front of him for a touchdown. The throw was probably 30-plus yards, and it hit Moore in stride. Hurts knew he threw a dime. He celebrated the pass in a way that’s atypical for the quarterback in a practice session. If he makes that pass in a game, talk radio spends the entire week on it, as opposed to his lack of touchdowns early in camp, which had been a topic over the weekend. A quick aside on that: The reason you haven’t read about the lack of touchdowns in camp so far in this space is that the context is required. They’ve only had one red-zone period before Monday’s session, and they’ve mostly been working on early-down installs from the middle of the field or his own territory. Unless Hurts throws deep balls, it’s not going to be a touchdown. Conversely, if they’re working in the red zone, you’ll see more touchdowns. Speaking of which… Nolan Smith Jr. calls arrest for speeding ‘unacceptable’: ‘I represent the Eagles no matter where I go’ – Inquirer Speaking publicly for the first time since his May 15 arrest in Twiggs County, Ga., for speeding and reckless driving, Eagles edge rusher Nolan Smith Jr. called his actions “unacceptable.” Smith was caught traveling 135 mph in a 70 mph zone, an incident that came four years after Smith was arrested in Barrow County, Ga., for speeding in a construction zone while driving on a suspended license. “I apologized to the organization, and I’ll make that apology now,” Smith said Monday after Eagles practice. “I represent the Eagles no matter where I go, Georgia, Florida, it doesn’t matter. That’s one of the ones that I own up and I apologize for. It’s just like that. We make mistakes and it can’t happen again and that’s unacceptable. I did apologize to Howie [Roseman], I did apologize to Mr. Lurie, and I can’t let my teammates down like that. They hold me to a different accountability on and off the field.” Saquon Barkley provides a surprise for a military family – PhiladelphiaEagles.com On Wednesday, Steven told Shemar and Jensen that they were attending Saturday’s Eagles Training Camp practice. Shemar watches all of the team’s social media posts and instantly dreamed of being along the players’ entrance to the practice field when Pro Bowl guard Landon Dickerson yells a hearty “Good morning!” to the fans in attendance. “Her love and admiration for the Eagles is just something to die for,” Steven said. A.J. Brown injury update: Patriots WR suffers dislocated thumb at practice – Pats Pulpit A.J. Brown was actively involved during the New England Patriots’ eighth training camp practice on Monday. The veteran wide receiver did so despite suffering a dislocated left thumb early during the session. He spoke about the injury during an appearance on NFL Network directly after the two-hour practice inside the Patriots’ indoor facility. “It was tough. I tried to get back into that flow state zone really quickly, because you’re going through a little pain,” he explained. “Obviously, the game is what it is and you’re going to get bumps and bruises. You got to keep going. I know it’s practice, but I’m not coming out of practice. You keep going.” Caleb Downs announced himself on Monday – Blogging The Boys The Dallas Cowboys held their first practice of training camp with pads on Monday and rookie defensive back Caleb Downs took notice. Let’s be clear here. The Cowboys have barely had a handful of practices in general, and just a single one wearing the actual gear that is to be worn when you play the sport of football. We are talking in excitement, but we also recognize that there is a long way to go in the grand scheme. But did you know that Caleb Downs is the greatest football player to ever live??? Washington Commanders Free Agency: Fabian Moreau returns – Hogs Haven The Washington Commanders have reportedly added another veteran cornerback to the roster. Rasul Douglas signed last week, and Washington’s former 3rd-round pick, Fabian Moreau, was the latest addition to the secondary. The Commanders are missing another Day 2 pick at training camp with Trey Amos still recovering from a broken fibula from his rookie season. Amos was reportedly dealing with some soft tissue issues that landed him on the active/PUP list. The Commanders announced the corresponding roster move, CB Ahkello…

title: Eagles Training Camp Practice Notes: Jalen Hurts strikes back
summary: Today marked the fourth Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. The players were in pads for the first time this summer while practicing indoors due to heavy rain outside. Here’s what I observed at the Jefferson Health Training Complex. EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES UP NEXT: The Eagles practice again tomorrow starting […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - JULY 30: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts during training camp at Jefferson Health Training Complex on July 30, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Today marked the fourth Philadelphia Eagles training camp practice ahead of the 2026 NFL season. The players were in pads for the first time this summer while practicing indoors due to heavy rain outside. Here’s what I observed at the Jefferson Health Training Complex. EAGLES PRACTICE NOTES JALEN HURTS UPDATE: Monday was a bounce back performance from Hurts and the offense after they were bested by Vic Fangio’s defense in the previous two practices. Encouraging to see. THE GOOD: The first-team offense was aided by going up against the second-team defense during the first 11-on-11 series. Hurts found Dontayvion Wicks crossing to the left downfield for a chunk gain. Hurts hit DeVonta Smith on an out to beat Mac McWilliams along the right sideline. Hurts’ success wasn’t limited to facing the Eagles’ backup defenders. During 7-on-7, Hurts made his flashiest completion of camp thus far by throwing with anticipation over the middle into the end zone to split the safeties and connect with Elijah Moore for a touchdown. Hurts found Darius Cooper for multiple completions over the middle. During a red zone sequence, Hurts hit DeVonta on another out route for a touchdown. The Eagles lined up to go for a two-point conversion and Hurts rolled to his right only to throw across his body to find DeVonta again, who made the grab despite being tightly covered by Riq Woolen. During another red zone sequence, Hurts took a shotgun snap and pretended to drop back before taking off running to the end zone untouched for a score. This wasn’t a case where the quarterback benefited from wearing the red jersey that reminds defenders not to get close to him. This was about Hurts correctly identifying a weakness in the defense and exposing it with his legs. Hurts and his offense teammates were fired up to celebrate this score. THE BAD: Hurts did throw a pick six to Quinyon Mitchell in 7-on-7 … but it looked like there was a miscommunication with Moore stopping his route earlier than the quarterback expected. Hurts held the ball for a long time and got “sacked” by either Jalen Carter or Jordan Davis (unclear which) at one point. Hurts sailed a downfield pass to Tank Bigsby, who had a step on Zack Baun (but not by much), over the running back’s head and out of bounds. The wheel route is no longer undefeated. Hurts had a pass deflected at the line by Jalen Carter. Fortunately for the offense, the ball landed in Hollywood Brown’s hands for a short gain. EAGLES INJURY UPDATES: DID NOT PARTICIPATE: OT Lane Johnson (excused absence/not injury related) Johnson also missed Saturday’s practice. It’s unclear what’s been keeping him away. OG Micah Morris (shoulder) S Cole Wisniewski (hamstring) EDGE Keyshawn James-Newby (ankle) OG Jaedan Roberts (calf contusion) Roberts was carted off the field on Saturday but he reportedly avoided a major injury . Good news. LIMITED PARTICIPATION: WR Makai Lemon (?) Lemon was not listed on the team-issued injury report but he didn’t appear to participate in team drills. I couldn’t find him again after seeing him take part in some individual drills early in practice. Something to monitor. UPDATE: The Inquirer’s Jeff McLane says that “whatever it was that limited Makai Lemon at practice, I’m told it wasn’t significant.” OT Cameron Williams (knee contusion) Williams was able to partake in some team drill activity. RETURNED TO PRACTICE: WR Elijah Moore and LB Jihaad Campbell were back in action after being excused from Saturday’s practice. Fred Johnson saw the first first-team reps at right tackle with Lane Johnson not practicing but Markell Bell also rotated in. Bell previously saw first-team right tackle action during spring practices but these were his first reps with the starters this summer. Good practice for the Eagles’ roster bubble wide receivers. Elijah Moore ran a sharp route to get open in the middle of the field for a completion of at least 15 yards. He later caught a touchdown from Hurts, as previously mentioned. Darius Cooper caught everything thrown his way, including when he made a diving grab on a Hurts throw over the middle. Johnny Wilson made a couple catches over the middle on passes from Andy Dalton. Wilson did fail to secure a Tanner McKee pass to him that was a little low but still catchable. BACKUP QUARTERBACK BATTLE UPDATE: Dalton was first up as the Eagles’ QB2 in 11-on-11 but the Eagles rotated him and Tanner McKee. Dalton looked sharper than McKee on Monday; the 38-year-old veteran quarterback ripped the ball over the middle to Wilson for multiple first downs. Dalton’s red zone sequence resulted in a touchdown pass to a wiiide open Will Shipley in the flat before he found Hollywood Brown on an out route for the successful two-point conversion. McKee seemed guilty of holding the ball too long at times and he wasn’t able to cash in during his red zone opportunity. Dalton has the edge over McKee early in camp. I like what I’ve seen from A.J. Epenesa in camp thus far; he’s been active. Epenesa “sacked” McKee while rotating in as a first-team edge rusher. Seems like he might be a nice rotational player. (RELATED READING — Eagles Film Review: A.J. Epenesa signing is very sensible.) Chance Campbell was in good position to stop a Saquon Barkley stretch run to the right side early in practice. Nolan Smith had tight coverage on Stone Smartt to force a short incompletion during 7-on-7. He celebrated with an exuberant incompletion motion right in front of Smartt after the play. Moro Ojomo totally blew up a run in the backfield while going up against the second-team offense. I wrote down Eli Stowers’ name twice in my notes today. The first time was when he made a short catch on a play where McKee rolled right and threw a short pass to him. Stowers immediately got shoved out of bounds by Zack Baun. Later, Stowers couldn’t make a catch with edge rusher Arnold Ebiketie covering him. Stowers wanted a flag on the defense but the practice refs did not throw one. Cole Payton continues to be fearless. The rookie quarterback took a downfield shot to Erik Ezukanma, who got his hands on the ball but couldn’t control it to the ground with three defenders very close to him. Payton connected with Dae’Quan Wright for a catch-and-run touchdown. Wright wasn’t shy to initiate contact to power his way into the end zone. The undrafted rookie tight end’s desire to bulldoze through defenders is apparent from his college highlights. Tariq Castro-Fields got his hands on a Payton pass that Ezukanma was able to stay with and make the grab on a bouncing ball. Payton more cleanly hit Smartt for a two-point conversion. Quez Watkins almost made a sick one-handed catch in the back of the end zone via a McKee pass but it was ruled that he did not get both feet in. Yes, Quez Watkins is still on the team and has been since he returned to Philly on the practice squad last season. Veteran cornerback Jonathan Jones was flagged for defensive holding in the end zone while going up against Hollywood Brown in a red zone sequence. Not the best practice for Jones, who also gave up a touchdown to DeVonta. Undrafted rookie free agent safety Maximus Pulley made a diving grab that was ruled incomplete for not getting both feet in. McKee forced the pass into the end zone during a two-point conversion try. Good effort by Pulley. UAR BERNARD UPDATE: I’ve seen some BGN commenters ask about how the Eagles’ intriguing seventh-round defensive tackle is doing. So, here’s what I’ve got. Bernard’s not getting many reps, which is typical for third/fourth string defensive linemen. I only saw one of his 1-on-1 offensive line versus defensive line reps since that action was happening on the opposite side of the field while 7-on-7 was concurrently taking place…

title: Eagles veterans explain why the new scheme is offensive line-friendly
summary: The Eagles offensive line has been a dominant staple for the team for more than a decade, but heading into the 2026 season, the group was forced to make a lot of changes — both to the coaching staff and to the overall offensive scheme. As the guys get more reps in the new system […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 16: Lane Johnson #65, Fred Johnson #74, Tyler Steen #56, Cam Jurgens #51, Saquon Barkley #26, Landon Dickerson #69, and Jordan Mailata #68 of the Philadelphia Eagles huddle against the Detroit Lions at Lincoln Financial Field on November 16, 2025 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles offensive line has been a dominant staple for the team for more than a decade, but heading into the 2026 season, the group was forced to make a lot of changes — both to the coaching staff and to the overall offensive scheme. As the guys get more reps in the new system through the first few days of training camp, veterans like Lane Johnson and Jordan Mailata talked about how their job as tackles should actually be easier this year. All-Pro right tackle Lane Johnson explained that some of the new things they’re doing should open up the passing game and get more guys, more touches. But that wasn’t his favorite part about the changes. JOHNSON: “What I like about this, though, is that everything looks very complex to the defense, to the offense it’s pretty simplified. So, obviously, we have to pick up on communication and cadence, and stuff, but it’s very o-line friendly compared to maybe some past years I’ve been involved in.” Johnson went on to explain that there’s a lot more under center plays which makes it more difficult for defense’s to make reads pre-snap. JOHNSON: “For me, it’s like I always have a presence of a guard in pass protection where I have inside help, where I’ve never had help in my entire career in pass protection here, so it’s been a lot of games are different for me and Jordan [Mailata] as far as other offenses.” Jordan Mailata spoke with reporters the following day and very quickly agreed to Johnson’s assessment of things being easier for the tackles. He also elaborated on how the scheme overall will look different and make things more confusing for opposing defenses. MAILATA: “Stretching the defense a lot more than we did in the past — this is not a knock to our past schemes or our past coaches, but we get to stretch the defense and kind of stress them out a little more. They don’t know if it’s a pass or run and the play-action game being married is pretty key to the scheme. It’s been fun so far, but still early days, so we just gotta keep stacking days and go from there.” Mailata went on to explain that it’s fun to play a different style and it’s a little more aggressive than they’ve been in the past. He noted that it also is super fun to see the defense so tired, because they’re engaging the defensive line a lot more — like running to the left and then passing over the middle. By convincing the d-line that they’re running, it confuses the linebackers and then opens up the middle of the field for a pass. As far as technique, Mailata said there’s a bit of a change with regard to their footwork because rather than moving laterally, they’re going across the line of scrimmage — being more aggressive and meeting them across the line rather than at the line. MAILATA: “When we’re being taught the scheme, just the explanation of how the defense is going to see it and the plan, in those meetings you just see like — ‘Oh wow, that’s pretty smart. Why didn’t I think of that?‘ Mailata has repeatedly expressed how impressed he’s been with new OC Sean Mannion this offseason, and the offensive coordinator, on Saturday, described how he and new OL coach Chris Kuper are trying to prioritize assignment commitment for the guys up front. MANNION: “We want these guys to go out there, know exactly where to go, and play fast. So, throughout all of our teaching, we want to make as many things as black and white for them as possible, so we’re all on the same page and we’re off and running. At least we all know where we’re going, and we’re going with total assignment commitment to attack our aiming points, attack our targets, and that will ultimately allow us to play fast, play physical, have the play style that we want. But, we want to make everything as cut and dry, and black and white for the offensive line so they can fire off.“ Landon Dickerson also reiterated the groups new priority of having things be as simple as possible and being able to play a lot faster as a result. DICKERSON: “I think for the o-line as a whole, a big emphasis is eliminating the slow play, not having a lot of time on the clock, just getting up there, being able to make a call, stick with it, and run the play. So, I think just for us, it’s about getting to the ball and playing fast, which can help a lot.” The LG said that a lot of it is trying not to overthink things. Dickerson explained that in their last system, a lot of it was problem solving and identifying things at the line of scrimmage, but the new system is all about playing fast. It’ll be awhile before we see the offense at full speed, but that so many veteran offensive lineman are excited about doing something new this season — and something they can believe in — is encouraging if nothing else with just over a month until Week 1.

summary: Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Thorn: 2026 Defensive Line Rankings – Establish The Run3) Eagles. Edge – Jonathan Greenard/Nolan Smith Jr.. IDL – Jordan Davis/Moro Ojomo. IDL – Jalen Carter. Edge – Jalyx Hunt. Philadelphia already had a top-half pass rush last season, with all meaningful contributors returning, before dealing […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 26: Jalyx Hunt #58, Jordan Davis #90 and Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles look on against the New York Giants at Lincoln Financial Field on October 26, 2025 in Philadelphia, United States. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Thorn: 2026 Defensive Line Rankings – Establish The Run 3) Eagles. Edge – Jonathan Greenard/Nolan Smith Jr.. IDL – Jordan Davis/Moro Ojomo. IDL – Jalen Carter. Edge – Jalyx Hunt. Philadelphia already had a top-half pass rush last season, with all meaningful contributors returning, before dealing a pair of third-round picks for Vikings standout edge rusher Jonathan Greenard. This unit is led by elite interior rusher Jalen Carter, with Greenard’s elite length and get-off giving Philadelphia a very good No. 2 in the hierarchy and a stable of solid to above-average pieces behind them. Jalyx Hunt projects as the third-best option, while Moro Ojomo offers pocket-pushing power that helped him finish 11th among interior rushers in TPR in 2025. This is one of the deepest units in the NFL and firmly a top-five group entering 2026. Sean Mannion sets Eagles training camp expectations, talks Jalen Hurts, and more – BGN The Eagles were back on the practice field on Saturday, but before taking the field, new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion spoke to reporters — in just his second time speaking to Philly media since being hired. He explained his training camp expectations, why he’s enjoyed working with Jalen Hurts, and their approaches to installing a new offensive scheme. Five Eagles Training Camp Thoughts With BLG! – The Ringer’s Philly Special Sheil is joined by Brandon Lee Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation to discuss his biggest takeaways from the first week of training camp. One of the biggest questions this upcoming season will be the offense in its entirety. How has it looked so far in camp? What are the biggest concerns? Which defensive player does BLG think is ready to make a major leap next season? Eagles mailbag: Is Makai Lemon’s slow start to camp cause for concern? – PhillyVoice Makai Lemon hasn’t done much so far, but as noted in the first paragraph, we’re only three days into camp. Would it be a lot cooler if he was lighting it up? Sure! But it’s pretty normal for rookie receivers to take a little time to get their sea legs in camp. In DeVonta Smith’s first training camp, he sprained his MCL in the fourth practice, and then missed the next eight practices. Before the injury, he had probably shown a little more than Lemon has so far, but he too was mostly quiet. Lemon has talent. He’ll make some plays. If after the first 10 or so practices he’s still just not making catches then it would be a much more reasonable cause for concern. Newcomer Dontayvion Wicks already earning trust from Jalen Hurts – NBCSP After just a few days of training camp, the biggest highlight play belongs to receiver Dontayvion Wicks. It wouldn’t have happened without trust. On Day 2 of camp, Jalen Hurts rolled to his left and never set his feet before tossing up a 50-50 ball to Wicks, who had to climb the ladder and secure the catch through double coverage from Jakorian Bennett and Cole Wisniewski. “Just trust. Building that chemistry and trust,” Wicks said. “[Hurts] just coming out, he don’t see nobody, just throw it up and trusting me to go get that and that’s what I did.” Eagles’ 53-man roster projection: How the picture looks entering training camp Week 2 – Inquirer Wide receivers (6): DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Hollywood Brown, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore. Cut: Johnny Wilson, Danny Gray, Britain Covey, Quez Watkins, Erik Ezukanma, Samori Toure. The top four players should be considered locks. Cooper is competing with Wilson for a role that Nick Sirianni described as doing the “dirty work.” Keeping both seems redundant. Cooper currently has the edge in that competition. Moore is a wild card. If the Eagles decide to go with just five here, he likely would be the odd man out. Gray had the play of the day Saturday, but there’s a lot of traffic ahead of him. 2026 NFL training camp: Position battles on each depth chart – ESPN The departure of Reed Blankenship in free agency left a starting spot open in defensive coordinator Vic Fangio’s secondary. Cooper DeJean will move from nickel to safety in base packages and probably will be paired with second-year player Andrew Mukuba. Marcus Epps and Michael Carter II are vying for starting spots when the Eagles are in sub packages, which is most of the time. In the early stages of camp, Epps and Mukuba have been paired the most frequently, but Fangio has been rotating players to get different looks. Spadaro: The joy has returned for Hollywood Brown – PhiladelphiaEagles.com Hollywood Brown feels it. He is running free and has his explosiveness. The burst he displays on the football field is special, and that’s part of the joy Brown has in this 2026 Eagles Training Camp. “I’m faster than I’ve ever been. I feel like I’m playing that way, for sure,” he said. “It’s an awesome feeling. I had a Lis Franc injury in my rookie year and that is the kind of injury that is a career-ender, they say. It’s cleaned out, I took some time to rest in this offseason and I’m seeing the benefits of that. “I’m playing more freely. I’m having fun. Enjoying what we’re doing out here.” Brown, signed in the offseason during the free agency process, is part of a diverse and talented receiving room. It is early, far too early for a hot take, so we will leave that for a larger sample size, but Brown is moving around at receiver in the Eagles’ offense. We’re still in a bit of a discovery period and that’s the way it is in every NFL Training Camp. Who’s Eagles best rookie (so far) in camp? Why it’s not Makai Lemon – Delaware Online There was always going to be a learning curve for Eagles wide receiver Makai Lemon, their first-round draft pick. And that’s even more the case for tight end Eli Stowers, the Eagles’ second-round draft pick. Neither has stood out during the Eagles’ first three training camp practices. So far, it seems like the Eagles’ best rookie has been third-round pick Markel Bell, the massive 6-foot-9, 346-pound offensive tackle. Best NFL team fits for notable remaining free agents: Stefon Diggs to NFC East? – NFL.com MEKHI BECTON. Right guard has been a problem spot for the Seahawks for some time. Seattle is expected to run it back with returning starter Anthony Bradford, who is likely to be pushed by fifth-rounder Beau Stephens. Becton has the experience to be an instant upgrade as a stop-gap until Stephens can find his way to bona fide starter status or another year goes by with a better chance to find a suitable starter in the draft. Other options: 49ers, Cardinals, Eagles. 49ers sign RB Khalil Herbert and former Colts 6th-round edge rusher; waive Eli Apple – Niners Nation The San Francisco 49ers have signed running back Khalil Herbert to a one-year deal. They’ve also added Titus Leo, a 6’3”, 245-pounder who was drafted in the sixth round by the Colts in the 2023 NFL Draft. Leo has only appeared in four games during his tenure, most recently appearing on the Eagles’ practice squad in October 2025. We knew the 49ers were working out various defensive linemen. It was reported the team had a tryout with Ogbo Okonkwo, but ultimately went younger. Leo tested well at his Pro Day back in 2023, running a 4.69 40-yard dash, with a 129” vertical jump — an elite number. [BLG Note: Okoronkwo was on the Eagles last year. And Herbert participated in the Eagles’ 2026 rookie minicamp on a tryout basis.] 3 biggest surprises so far at training camp – Blogging The Boys Cowboys linked to trade for All-Pro LB Jordyn Brooks. The Cowboys selected Jaishawn Barham in the third round, and he’s been flashing so far at camp. Plus, they added Dee Winters during the offseason. They will battle it out at middle linebacker,…

title: Steelers stock report after Day Five of training camp
summary: LATROBE- There were plenty of reactions from people when it was reported that the Pittsburgh Steelers would not be having live tackling in camp this year. However, when the pads went on for the first time this season in Latrobe today, you could hear plenty of popping and the defense showing their physicality. Let’s take […]
full_text: Aug 03, 2026; Latrobe, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker (3) participates in a practice session at Training camp at Saint Vincent College. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LATROBE- There were plenty of reactions from people when it was reported that the Pittsburgh Steelers would not be having live tackling in camp this year. However, when the pads went on for the first time this season in Latrobe today, you could hear plenty of popping and the defense showing their physicality. Let’s take a look at who did well and who didn’t in the Steelers’ fifth training camp practice, in stock-up and stock-down style. Stock Up: S Jaquan Brisker No defender benefited from having pads on and being able to be more physical today than Jaquan Brisker. Brisker had a huge pass breakup during the 11-0n-11 team period. Later in that same period, Brisker came screaming off the edge on a safety blitz and had Mason Rudolph dead to rights for what would have been a huge sack if they were allowed to tackle. Jaquan Brisker just came screaming off the edge on a blitz that would have ended up being a sack in a game. Brisker is having his best practice of camp today. — Joey Bray (@byjoeybray) August 3, 2026 The Steelers are particularly thin at the free safety spot, so Brisker will have to shoulder the majority of those responsibilities early in the season. It was easily the best performance that Brisker has put together so far this camp. CB Doneiko Slaughter If you are looking for a sleeper in the Steelers defensive back room, look no further than Doneiko Slaughter. With how well his fellow corner Asante Samuel Jr. has been playing, something that hasn’t been talked about enough is how well Slaughter has been playing this camp. Slaughter was around the ball a lot today and made several huge plays, including a pass breakup and intercepting a Will Howard downfield shot. Will Howard airs it out downfield but it’s picked off by Doneiko Slaughter who is having a really nice camp. — Joey Bray (@byjoeybray) August 3, 2026 The 2025 undrafted free agent out of Arkansas is having a phenomenal start to camp and is standing out in what figures to be a loaded cornerback room. If he continues this kind of play into the preseason, the Steelers will have a big decision to make on how many corners to keep. QB Drew Allar No quarterback has had more “wow” throws this camp than third-round pick Drew Allar, and today was no exception. Allar set his feet and threw a beauty of a deep ball to Cole Burgess in stride for a 50+ yard touchdown. Allar is still very much a work in progress, and Mike McCarthy has been working with Allar and Will Howard more than the other quarterbacks on the roster. However, it’s impossible to deny the impact plays we are seeing Allar make. For someone who isn’t expected to do much, if anything, this season, there have been plenty of reasons to get excited about Allar, and today was no exception. Drew Allar steps back and launches a perfect 60-yard bomb to Cole Burgess. Beautiful throw by Allar. — Joey Bray (@byjoeybray) August 3, 2026 Stock Down: OT Troy Fautanu It was a rough go for Fautanu today. The starting tackle had two false starts during 11-on-11 team periods that resulted in him ultimately getting pulled from the drill for a few plays. TJ Watt also seemed to be getting the best of Fautanu in blocking drills. All of this is no reason to sound the alarm or hit the panic button. Fautanu is one of the Steelers’ most talented and promising young players who just had a tough day. QB Will Howard It was not a day to remember for Will Howard. He had his moments in team periods connecting with Brandon Smith several times but also had moments where his accuracy and timing seemed to be off. Howard was also granted the opportunity to lead the offense down the field on a two-minute drill to end practice. It was an opportunity for him to end practice on a high note, but the drive was ultimately unsuccessful as the defense dominated in both two-minute drills to end practice. It will more than likely come down to performance in the preseason for Will Howard as he continues to compete with veteran Mason Rudolph for the backup quarterback job. full_text: Jul 30, 2026; Latrobe, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Drew Allar (186) participates in training camp drills at Saint Vincent College. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LATROBE – The Pittsburgh Steelers put the pads on for the first time on Monday, taking another step toward their first game action of the year when they host the Green Bay Packers next Thursday. As always, there is much to discuss – including a breakout day from an under-the-radar quarterback, another big throw from Drew Allar, and Jaquan Brisker’s best day. Let’s get into it. Doneiko Slaughter throws his name in the mix While Asante Samuel has been the story of training camp, No. 19 Doneiko Slaughter made several plays to stand out on Monday. For starters, he picked off Will Howard on a deep throw to the left sideline. He also broke up a deep pass from Will Howard to Max Hurleman. With such a deep cornerback room, it’s understandable that the young Slaughter isn’t a name many were focused on, but he’s becoming a name to circle once preseason play begins for the Steelers next week. Drew Allar throws another splash touchdown It was a good day for Allar, who made the splash throw of the day – a 55-yard touchdown to Cole Burgess during seven-on-sevens. He also ripped a completion over the middle to Max Hurleman on fourth down during team period. Allar has played very well through the first week of practices – better than anticipated. Especially when the overwhelming expectation was how raw he would be as a talent. However, he’s looking more comfortable with each practice and continuing to impress. Aaron Rodgers is dialed in At this time last year, the offense was rocky, as was Rodgers. Through nearly a full week of practices, he has been absolutely dialed in. He and DK Metcalf connected on a total of four passes. Metcalf made an incredible one-handed grab over Jamel Dean. He also went up and over Dean for a nice chunk play before Rodgers fit a seed to the star receiver down the sideline for a big gain. Additionally, his connection with Pat Freiermuth has been one to watch. The two connected for a touchdown on Saturday, and Rodgers found No. 88 for another big gain during team period. Jaquan Brisker has best day of camp The first-year Steeler nearly made a big splash play. He read a pass from Rodgers and had the pass hit him in the stomach, nearly picking it off. Later on in team period, he came untouched off the edge for what would have been a sack in-game. Brisker’s versatility is what makes him such a good piece to have on the defense. He continues to flash. Other notes Brandin Echols picked off a pass that looked like a miscommunication between Rodgers and Roman Wilson. Couldn’t tell if he trapped it on the grass, but it appears it was ruled a pick Asante Samuel continued his streak of impressive pass breakups, batting down a pass intended for Michael Pittman Will Howard connected with Brandon Smith on the left side of the field off a play action pass in team period Esezi Otomewo nearly picked off a short pass on the same play Brisker would have had a sack.
