title: 2026 Los Angeles Rams training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Rams training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Los Angeles Rams  camp is taking place at Loyola Marymount University in L.A. Rams reporter Sarah Barshop has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Rams camp. We will update this file often. Can the Rams live up to the hype? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Rams camp 
 
 Myles Garrett out third straight day with soreness 
 Rams' McVay: No Aaron Donald update, but 'trending upwards' 
 Puka Nacua says it 'never crossed my mind' to not take part in camp 
 Rams unveil two new alternate uniforms for 2026 
 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 
 The Rams finished their second training camp block on Monday with what head coach Sean McVay called more of an unscripted practice. Matthew Stafford and  Stetson Bennett IV  took all of the quarterback reps for the Rams, with rookie Ty Simpson only taking part in individual drills.

 The first-team offense and the secondary exchanged several standout plays, including a pass breakup on receiver Puka Nacua by cornerback Trent McDuffie . Later, Stafford found wide receiver Davante Adams for a completion down the sideline.

 "I thought there was especially some really good back and forth with the ones," McVay said after practice. "Some really good plays on both sides, but that's what we're looking for is good quality play where you can really see guys playing through the cycle of the snap."

 McVay pointed to "some big breakups down the field" by McDuffie and cornerback Jaylen Watson .

 "Guys made plays on both sides and it felt like it was a quality operation," McVay said.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 
 McVay said he hasn't determined how he will allocate reps during the preseason between the quarterbacks other than Stafford not playing in any preseason games. Last year, Stafford and Jimmy Garoppolo sat out of the preseason while Bennett started the first two preseason games.

 
 
 Rams tight end Davis Allen is dealing with a quad injury. McVay said the Rams will give Allen "some time" before he returns to practice because it's a soft tissue injury. "You don't want to rush him back," McVay said. "He's played a lot of football and it'll give ... some of these other tight ends an opportunity to get snaps they wouldn't otherwise. But Davis is going to be a big part of what we do this year."

 
 
 Garrett (lower body soreness) did not practice for the fourth straight day. The Rams will re-evaluate him after the Tuesday off day.

 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 Coach Sean McVay praised quarterback  Stetson Bennett IV 's growth from last training camp, pointing out "the ownership of the offense" he has now.

 Bennett got the majority of the second-team reps last training camp while Matthew Stafford was dealing with a back injury and Jimmy Garoppolo was with the first team.

 "But then once Matthew came back, he didn't get any reps at all," McVay said. "And so for his ability to come in and to be able to run the one offense the way that he has, I've been really pleased with him."

 McVay said quarterbacks coach Dave Ragone "deserves a ton of credit" for the way he has worked with Bennett.

 "[Bennett has] played really well through the offseason program and up until now," McVay said. "And that's been a real positive for us."

 Bennett, a fourth-round pick in 2023, is competing with rookie first-round pick Ty Simpson to back up Stafford this season.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 The Rams held a jog-through on Sunday, meaning players were in T-shirts and shorts on the practice field. It was one of Stafford's scheduled days off of practice. 
 Defensive end Myles Garrett did not practice for the third straight day, as he is dealing with "a little soreness in his lower half," McVay said. The head coach said the Rams are just erring on the side of caution and that he is not concerned. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Rams running back Kyren Williams , who is entering his fifth NFL season, said he changed the way he worked out. While Williams has always prided himself on his versatility, he said he didn't do wide receiver drills this offseason. Instead, he focused on drills specific for a running back.

 "[In the past] I would work out and do a lot of receiver workouts and do a lot of different things because I want to be as versatile as I can," Williams said. "But this year I honed in on running back. I honed in on really training to be running back, training, like I said, those pad levels, those cuts. And when I am cutting, sinking my body. Because if I cut straight up, I'm not going nowhere.

 "My superpowers, when I'm low to the ground, I have both my feet in the ground and I'm playing it and I'm explosive."

 Williams said that is an area where he felt he "needed to get better at."

 "And I think it's been showing here [at] camp," Williams said.

 

 Another observation: 

 
 Myles Garrett did not practice for the second straight day. A team spokesperson said it was a scheduled rest day for the defensive end. 
 

 
 Friday, July 31 
 The Rams practiced in pads on Friday for the first time during training camp. It was a scheduled day off for quarterback Matthew Stafford , allowing for backup quarterback candidates Stetson Bennett IV and Ty Simpson to take the reps.

 Rams head coach Sean McVay said even in a padded practice, it can be tough to judge a quarterback's performance without looking at the tape because they are not being tackled. Still, McVay said, "I thought both Stetson and Ty did a nice job."

 "Stetson has really taken incredible strides, done a lot of good things, and I think Ty has improved tremendously from the spring until now as well," McVay said.

 McVay said he's seen that growth for Simpson in the way he is calling the plays in the huddle and even some things "mechanically about being able to speed up his release, some of the timing and rhythm in terms of with his lower half being married up with the routes."

 

 Other observations: 

 
 Along with Stafford, defensive end Myles Garrett and wide receiver Davante Adams had scheduled days off on Friday. 
 Former Buffalo Bills head coach Sean McDermott attended practice and chatted with McVay before it began. McDermott worked with Rams offensive line coach Ryan Wendell in Buffalo and knows McVay from their time together on the competition committee. "I think all of us as coaches are constantly curious and trying to just be able to kind of share with one another," McVay said. "And it was great to have him out here today." 
 

 
 Wednesday, July 29 
 Training camp just began for the Rams, but it won't be long before they travel to Melbourne, Australia for their Week 1 game against the San Francisco 49ers .

 Rams coach Sean McVay said the team has determined how they will handle travel, but said he didn't want to share the specifics. McVay did say it would be a "similar approach" to how the Rams handled traveling to London last season, when the team arrived less than 30 hours prior to kickoff. The Rams traveled to London from the East Coast after spending the week in Baltimore, which is a significantly shorter trip than it will take to get from Los Angeles to Melbourne -- the flight time is typically around 16 hours.

 "And really the goal for us is to try to keep guys in as close to a rhythm and routine as possible," McVay said. "This is new to us even, going this far. And so I trust our group and most importantly, what's going to be best for our players. And we always try…

title: Klint Kubiak not worried about Mendoza's rough practice

title: 2026 Las Vegas Raiders training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Raiders training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Las Vegas Raiders  camp is taking place at Intermountain Health Performance Center in Henderson, Nevada, and Raiders reporter Ryan McFadden has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Raiders camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 

 Latest news from Raiders camp 
 
 Three-time Pro Bowl guard Andrus Peat announces retirement 
 Cousins gets nod over Mendoza to open Raiders camp 
 What's next for Crosby, WR and CB rooms? 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Fernando Mendoza had an up-and-down practice Monday, but coach Klint Kubiak understands the rookie will not be perfect all the time.

 "There will never be a perfect game or practice," Kubiak said. "I think he is doing a good job. I don't expect him to be perfect right now."

 The lowlights of Mendoza's performance included a few off-target throws during the team period and the one-on-one period between defensive backs and wide receivers. In 11-on-11, Mendoza's pass to Malik Benson in the middle of the field was slightly high and put the rookie wide receiver in a bad position to be nearly hit by safety Tristin McCollum .

 On the next play, he threw an incomplete pass to wide receiver Phillip Dorsett II .

 Mendoza also had snap issues, struggling to maintain control of the ball, but he managed to salvage the play. Kubiak said it's an issue he wants Mendoza to clean up.

 "That's a part of playing the position," Kubiak said. "... That's why the quarterback has to be one of the best athletes on the field. He has to be able to grab a low snap and be able to jump on it when it's over his head."

 

 Mendoza did bounce back toward the end of practice. His best throw was to Benson on a crossing route that led to a big gain. Later, he quickly threw the ball to wideout Shedrick Jackson on a slant.

 Still, Kubiak said it's too early to determine how well Mendoza can handle adversity.

 "There are 60-to-80 plays in a game. There are going to be ups and downs," Kubiak said. "What quarterback is gonna get the other 10 players playing at their best, that's what we're looking for."

 Another observation: 

 
 Tight end Michael Mayer left practice early because of a busted nose, but Kubiak said Mayer should be fine. 
 
 
 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 Sunday featured quarterback  Fernando Mendoza 's worst performance of training camp, as the defense was overpowering throughout the morning.

 During 11-on-11 work, Mendoza attempted a deep pass to rookie wide receiver Malik Benson . However, Mendoza's pass was underthrown, and cornerback Decamerion Richardson deflected the ball. When the Raiders were practicing two-minute situations, Mendoza and the second-team offense had pre-snap issues, prompting a timeout and the second team's replacement with the third team.

 Mendoza also threw his first interception of camp. In the 7-on-7 period, defensive back Greedy Vance intercepted Mendoza's pass attempt to wide receiver  Phillip Dorsett II . Vance perfectly read the pass and jumped in front of Dorsett to secure the ball.

 The offense did make some plays. Kirk Cousins and Brock Bowers connected on a few big throws in the middle of the field. Undrafted rookie running back Roman Hemby had a nice run down the middle. And  Aidan O'Connell  had the play of the day, throwing a touchdown pass to wide receiver E.J. Williams Jr.

 But for the most part, the defense had the upper hand. Linebacker Quay Walker and second-year defensive tackle  JJ Pegues  each recorded a sack. Defensive end Maxx Crosby was a force against the run. In the two-minute period, he quickly blew past right tackle DJ Glaze to stop running back Ashton Jeanty for a loss of yards. Rookie defensive end Keyron Crawford even had a nice run stop on Hemby while playing with the second team.

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Edge rusher Kwity Paye returned after leaving Friday's practice early. Reserve tight end Carter Runyon was the only player absent from practice. 
 Darien Porter played the majority of the first-team reps at outside cornerback. Hezekiah Masses still had his fair share of reps with the starters, as the competition at that position picks up more steam. 
 Rookie Trey Zuhn III had some reps at right tackle sprinkled on his plate in Sunday's practice. The expectation is for him to contribute as an interior lineman, given that his size could create mismatches inside.

summary: Follow our daily updates from Dolphins training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Miami Dolphins  camp is taking place in Miami Gardens, and Dolphins reporter Marcel Louis-Jacques has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Dolphins camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Dolphins camp 
 
 Dolphins top pick Proctor embracing NFL learning curve 
 Miami, All-Pro LB Jordyn Brooks reach 3-year, $51.3M extension 
 Dolphins, Aaron Brewer reach 3-year, $52.5 million extension 
 Why Miami's rookies can thrive 
 
 

 

 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Malik Willis still isn't scrambling in team drills as the Dolphins want him to focus on making plays from the pocket in training camp, but he's displaying a keen ability to evade pressure and keep his eyes downfield.

 On multiple occasions during Monday's practice, Willis kept a play alive and found a receiver downfield. He spun away from pressure and found a wide open Malik Washington over the middle for an explosive gain, and lofted another off-platform throw to rookie tight end Seydou Traore -- who came down with a one-handed catch for a first down.

 Willis did throw an interception off a tipped pass, but the ball placement certainly could've been better. He also missed a throw to a wide open Caleb Douglas , who got hands on the ball but couldn't come down with it. But Willis has flashed some touch over the past few practices.

 More observations: 

 
 Linebacker Tyrel Dodson returned an interception for a touchdown in team drills, tracking the ball after it deflected off tight end Cole Turner 's hands. In Turner's defense, the ball from Willis was far too low. 
 Cornerback Ethan Bonner intercepted Quinn Ewers ' first pass of the team's game-winning drive drill, again off a deflected pass. 
 Both Willis and Ewers led their groups into field goal range during game-winning drive drills, and both kickers attempted field goals with each unit. Riley Patterson was good from 50 yards before missing from 43 yards, while Zane Gonzalez made both kicks. Both kickers were good from 52 yards on their third attempt. 
 Safety Lonnie Johnson Jr. appeared to suffer a lower body injury after thudding running back Jaylen Wright in team drills. He was attended to on the sideline and didn't return. 
 Tight end Greg Dulcich did not practice Monday for an unspecified reason, and the group's production tapered off without him. 
 Defensive end Chop Robinson blew by right tackle Charlie Heck on back-to-back plays to start the game-winning drill. The first one was credited as a sack, but Willis got the ball off just in time on the second play, hitting tight end Ben Sims over the middle for a first down. 
 

 
 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 The Dolphins' offense woke up in a major way in an exciting practice in front of fans Sunday morning. Running back De'Von Achane kicked things off with an explosive run on the first play of team drill, while wide receivers Tutu Atwell , Kevin Coleman Jr ., and AJ Henning each had receptions of at least 50 yards.

 Coach Jeff Hafley has introduced "competitive" practice segments in which the "loser" endures some sort of punishment; Sunday, that meant the defense owed Hafley 20 pushups after practice.

 "(Last practice) we beat the offense, today they got us back," rookie cornerback Chris Johnson said. "So we're looking forward to taking the lead back tomorrow."

 

 More observations: 

 
 Johnson turned in yet another strong performance, intercepting a Quinn Ewers pass early on in team drills. The 2026 first-round pick out of San Diego State has trained at both cornerback spots this summer and is destined for a big role this season. 
 Henning turned in his best practice in a Dolphins uniform, dating back to last season. He was the intended receiver on Johnson's interception, but made up for it with 50-plus yard receptions from both Ewers and Cam Miller -- the latter being an over-the-shoulder grab in stride on the final play of practice. 
 Despite the explosive passing plays, arguably the best throw of the day might have been a 10-yard pass from Malik Willis , where he perfectly lofted the ball to tight end Cole Turner just over linebacker Jordyn Brooks ' reach. Impressive touch from Willis, especially while on the move. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 Wide receiver Caleb Douglas turned in his best day of practice yet, and it's starting to become a trend for the third-round rookie.

 He started team drills off with a contested catch over the middle on the first play, and followed it up a few plays later with a contorting back-shoulder catch on the right sideline on a ball from Malik Willis . Douglas capped his day with a touchdown grab in the corner of the endzone during red-zone work, on another ball from Willis. His explosive athleticism was never a question; his next test will be remaining focused once pads come on next week.

 More observations: 

 
 Defensive tackle Zach Sieler beat rookie offensive lineman Kadyn Proctor for a sack on the final play of practice. Speaking afterward, Proctor said moments like that are a learning experience for him, and he appreciates competing with a veteran like Sieler. 
 Running back Donovan Edwards cut back and broke contain for a 15- to 20-yard touchdown run during red-zone work. He never quite built on an exciting sophomore season at Michigan, but he flashed some of his explosiveness on that play. 
 Willis scored on a designed quarterback run during red-zone drills. He's largely remained in the pocket during both spring and training camp practices, but he will certainly be utilized as a runner once the regular season begins. 
 

 

 Thursday, July 30 
 The Dolphins haven't run 7-on-7 drills in either of their first two training camp practices this summer, and that's not likely to change moving forward. First-year coach Jeff Hafley said he doesn't like 7-on-7 because he doesn't feel like it accurately simulates real game play, especially for quarterbacks.

 "There's no [pass] rush," Hafley said. "For the quarterback, they're not going to feel anything. There's no timing. There's no rhythm. I think you create a lot of bad habits."

 Players have largely agreed with their head coach, with running back De'Von Achane and wide receiver Malik Washington expressing their preference for 11-on-11 team drills. Ironically, Thursday's practice skewed heavily in favor of Miami's defense, which forced four turnovers during team drills.

 More observations: 

 
 Safety Zayne Anderson and linebacker Ronnie Harrison Jr . both recorded interceptions in Thursday's practice, while defensive end Chop Robinson and cornerback Chris Johnson each forced and recovered fumbles. 
 Running back Ollie Gordon II fumble for the second consecutive practice, and Achane committed his first fumble of the offseason. 
 Wide receiver Tutu Atwell struggled with drops, one of which led to Anderson's interception. He was a standout performer during spring practices, but showed some signs of rust to start training camp -- which isn't uncommon at this point of the year. 
 The Dolphins still aren't wearing shoulder pads but that hasn't hurt the level of physicality at practice -- especially Thursday's. 
 Rookie wide receiver Chris Bell continued to work on the side as he recovers from a torn ACL.

title: What McCarthy-Murray QB battle means for Vikings' locker room
summary: While J.J. McCarthy and Kyler Murray compete for the starting job, their teammates are focused on helping both of them succeed.
full_text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- NFL teams rarely conduct the kind of quarterback competition the Minnesota Vikings have engaged in this summer, and there are some good reasons why. 

 From a practical sense, there aren't enough starting-caliber quarterbacks around the league for many teams to pit one against another. Practice reps are at a premium as coaches install complicated offenses. 

 Then there is also the possibility of unintended consequences -- namely that human nature will push players to support their personal favorite. 

 

 Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell has cited the team's culture and leadership as bulwarks against any drama that his competition between Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy could otherwise create. During the first week of camp, ESPN asked four of the Vikings' eight 2025 captains how they were maintaining neutrality in the locker room, assuming they were. 

 If anything, what emerged was a sense that they, too, are being judged on how they perform during the process.

 "Some people from the outside might have some noise and say the team's going to be divided and it's going to be this or that," safety Joshua Metellus said. "And our job as captains and leaders is to make sure the team is connected and knows that at the end of the day, there is competition in every room. This is just the one that's highlighted the most.

 "So it's just more about getting the guys to understand what we're here for and understanding that we're here to get them better. So we have to be on our stuff on the defensive side to make sure they can get good looks, and it's not one-sided."

 

 In his 10th season, running back Aaron Jones Sr. had never entered a training camp without an established starting quarterback. He spent six seasons in Green Bay playing with Aaron Rodgers before the Packers transitioned to Jordan Love in 2023. Sam Darnold took almost every first-team practice rep when Jones arrived in Minnesota for the 2024 season, and McCarthy was understood to be the top quarterback when camp began in 2025

 This summer, Jones said he has tried to remember how his performance -- and that of the rest of the offensive huddle -- could ultimately impact the competition's outcome.

 "I just want to make sure that each guy's putting their best foot forward for both guys," Jones said. "They're in a battle, so every rep is important for both of them. Dropped balls and different things like that, they matter. So everybody being at their best for all of our quarterbacks. And it'll make us that much better in the end, no matter who's back there calling the shots when the season comes, and it holds us accountable in a way.

 "Not that you ever want to go to camp with a quarterback battle or anything like that, but it raises the level of everybody's play."

 

 There is no doubt, however, that many players developed a personal affinity for McCarthy during the previous two years, drawn either by his connective personality or his efforts to overcome a rookie season lost to injury. They know that even in his third season, he is only 23 years old with 10 games and 243 pass attempts to his professional career. During an appearance this spring on the Green Light podcast, Vikings tackle Brian O'Neill said of McCarthy: "I love that kid. If I was judged after my first 10 games in the NFL, I'm not playing right now."

 Last week, O'Neill said he is absorbed more with micro issues related to the competition. 

 "Nobody's asking me, 'Hey go do this with them, go do this with them, go do this with whoever,'" he said. "It's about playing and obviously working through it if there's any difference in the cadence in the huddle or how it goes on the field working through that, but my job is to make it right for either of them. So that's kind of all I can focus on."

 Murray, on the other hand, is much quieter than McCarthy and less familiar with his surroundings. Whereas McCarthy might sprint 40 yards downfield to celebrate a big completion during practice, Murray is more likely to be waiting at the line of scrimmage to fist-bump the receiver. And as a veteran, Murray seems aware that everything he says publicly will be scrutinized for deeper meaning.

 On the first day of camp, in fact, Murray did not directly answer a question about which Vikings players he worked out with during his summer break. (NFL reporter Jordan Schultz posted video  on July 24 of Murray and receiver Jordan Addison throwing near Dallas.)

 Perhaps the most important voice is receiver Justin Jefferson , who has chosen his words carefully throughout the process. He has said repeatedly that it "doesn't matter" which quarterback O'Connell ultimately selects. 

 "It's a competition," Jefferson said. "It's all on who comes to practice and who's the better guy. At this point, it's still early in training camp for any of us to understand or know who's the No. 1 guy. So it's just all about pouring into both of them and making sure that whoever's the guy at the end of the day, we're not starting over or starting fresh."

title: 2026 Minnesota Vikings training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Vikings training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action.  What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Vikings camp. We will update this file often. Who will win the starting quarterback battle between incumbent J.J. McCarthy and free agent addition Kyler Murray ? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Vikings stories 

 
 Vikings, O'Neill reach $96M extension 
 Top Vikings storylines after minicamp, from QBs to new GM 
 Will Vikings start Caleb Banks, other rookies on defense? 
 Jefferson says decision on Vikings starting QB 'coach's call' 
 
 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Neither Kyler Murray nor J.J. McCarthy took a step forward Monday during the fifth practice -- and first in full pads -- of their competition to win the Minnesota Vikings ' starting quarterback job. The pair roughly split first-team snaps during 11-on-11 team drills, with Murray getting 10 and McCarthy eight.

 Murray found Justin Jefferson crossing across the field after evading the pass rush, but he also threw high over the middle to receiver Jordan Addison . On the play, Addison and cornerback Isaiah Rodgers collided in the air, flipping Anderson and sending Rodgers sprawling.

 The practice ended with a rough two-minute sequence for both quarterbacks. In five snaps, McCarthy went 0-for-3 with two tipped passes and an interception on a throw to Jefferson that cornerback Byron Murphy Jr . stepped in front of. Murray took over for two snaps with the second team, going 0-for-2 with a pass behind tight end Josh Oliver on the first and a miscommunication on the second.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 
 Receiver Tai Felton , a third-round draft pick in 2025, made the catch of camp in 7-on-7 drills, leaping high to grab a Murray pass in the back corner of the end zone. Felton has been working as the No. 4 receiver behind Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings .

 
 
 Cornerback James Pierre returned to practice after sitting out at the end of last week. Rookie running back Demond Claiborne was in full pads but worked out on a side field for players who are rehabilitating injuries."

 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Quarterback Kyler Murray had by far his best day of training camp Saturday, pinpointing a series of downfield throws in traffic while taking the majority of the Vikings' first-team reps as his competition with J.J. McCarthy continues.

 Murray was on the field for 16 of the first-team offense's 22 snaps in 11-on-11 team drills. McCarthy took the other six. Murray hit receiver Justin Jefferson on a deep dig route over the middle and he threw another perfectly placed pass on his next series that receiver Myles Price dropped. All three of Murray's passes to Jefferson were complete, and Price's drop was Murray's only incompletion among seven passes in team drills.

 McCarthy did not find similar success while working mostly with the second team against the first-team defense. He threw one pass on the run that rookie linebacker Jake Golday tipped, and was intercepted by linebacker Blake Cashman . McCarthy's best throw of the day came during a stint with the first team, but tight end T.J. Hockenson was unable to come up with the ball in traffic in the end zone.

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 At one point Saturday, the Vikings had three rookies working in the same package on their first-team defense: defensive linemen Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange , along with Golday. 
 Cornerback James Pierre was not in uniform for Saturday's practice. Rookie running back Demond Claiborne was not seen in team drills. 
 
 
 Friday, July 31 

 Rain pushed the Vikings' third practice of training camp indoors Friday, and the condensed area left them working at close to a walkthrough pace. But their quarterback competition continued, and for the first time J.J. McCarthy (32) got more team snaps than Kyler Murray (26) during full-offense drills against either the scout team or the defense.

 Receiver Justin Jefferson , asked what he has seen from quarterbacks this week, said: "Improvement." Jefferson later said he hopes McCarthy will benefit from the competition no matter how it turns out.

 "Just obviously having somebody pretty much breathing down your neck and being pretty much being a replacement or a person that's taking that starting role," Jefferson said, "it's always going to be pressure. It's always going to be that competition feeling.

 "So I hope it definitely betters J.J. because he's definitely a younger guy. To be coming off of last year with a difficult year and improving every single day as he is, that's definitely great to see him come out here with that mentality."

 

 Other observations: 

 
 Rookie defensive lineman Caleb Banks , the No. 18 pick of the 2026 draft, opened camp working with the second team but on Friday worked almost exclusively with the first team alongside nose tackle Levi Drake Rodriguez and defensive end Jalen Redmond . 
 Left tackle Christian Darrisaw took his first veteran's rest day of camp Friday, part of the Vikings' plan to keep his left knee healthy following a season in which lingering soreness from an October 2024 injury limited him to 10 games. 
 

 
 Thursday, July 30 
 One of the Vikings' most important players offered up some excellent news Thursday after the team's second training camp practice.

 "Feel the best I've felt in two years," left tackle Christian Darrisaw said, referring to the long road to a full recovery from multiple ligament tears in his left knee in October 2024.

 Darrisaw returned from the injury in time to participate in training camp last summer, but he started only 10 games and left five of those early before the Vikings ended his season with two games remaining. He said Thursday that he turned the corner this offseason and has been "just feeling like myself truly" because he is not worried about the leg being stiff.

 "It's just like night and day from how I came into the season and how I'm feeling now," Darrisaw said.

 The Vikings are likely to give Darrisaw, 27, some regular rest during camp and practice week. But Darrisaw said he is on track to be a full-time player in games once again.

 "That's the goal," he said. "Stay healthy and just go out there and dominate."

 Other observation: 

 Perhaps the biggest takeaway Thursday from the competition between quarterbacks Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy is that Murray is more often pushing the ball downfield. He threw an accurate floater about 45 yards downfield to receiver Dontae Fleming , as well as a deep corner to receiver Justin Jefferson . He also missed tight end T.J. Hockenson down the right sideline.

 

 Wednesday, July 29 
 On the first day of their training camp quarterback competition, the Vikings were true to their word: Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy rotated evenly during team drills. There were two sets of 11-on-11 drills Wednesday. Murray took the first eight snaps, four coming with the first team and four coming with the second team. McCarthy then took the next eight under the same parameters. The second set was cut short, leaving McCarthy with only four snaps.

 That brought the Day 1 total to 16 total snaps for Murray and 12 for McCarthy.

Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Patriots camp

 Patriots' Brown knows Vrabel's rip comes from 'great place' 
 Kraft: Patriots' Gonzalez has offer to be 'highest-paid' CB ever 
 Too many receivers? A look at the Patriots' crowded WR room 
 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Wide receiver Romeo Doubs ' transition from the Green Bay Packers to the New England Patriots has flown a bit under the radar since the arrival of A.J. Brown in early June.

 So, in a sense, it was fitting that on the day Doubs was scheduled to visit reporters after practice that Brown was once again dominating headlines (he dislocated his left thumb but practiced through it).

 He seems just fine with it.

 "The process has been really good," the soft-spoken Doubs said . "I love where I am, I love where our team is, I love the intensity of camp practices and things of that nature."

 Though Brown is the clear-cut No. 1 receiver, the 6-foot-2, 210-pound Doubs has most often lined up alongside him as the No. 2 option. That's what many projected after the Patriots signed Doubs to a four-year, $68 million base-value contract in March as an unrestricted free agent.

 The Patriots' top seven receivers are worthy of roster spots -- Brown, Doubs, Kayshon Boutte , Mack Hollins ,  DeMario "Pop" Douglas ,  Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III -- making it one of the most competitive positions on the roster.

 Doubs had a touchdown catch Monday as the team worked mostly in the red zone, with practice moved inside due to rain.

 Of his chemistry with Drake Maye, he said: "It's growing. It's a day-to-day grind. It takes a certain amount of trust. I'm glad to be around a guy like Drake. He's a leader. He's poised."

 Maye credited Doubs for learning the offense since his arrival, noting it was different than what he was accustomed to with the Packers.

 "He hasn't been in an offense like that has some decision-making [for receivers]. I think he's getting better and better as he's gotten through OTAs and even in camp, he's making some great plays for us. He's kind of shifty and has a little wiggle to him that I didn't really expect throwing to him in camp."

 More observations: 

 
 RB Terrell Jennings , who opened camp on the non-football injury list, passed his physical and practiced for the first time. He joins 2025 undrafted free agent Lan Larison , 2026 seventh-round draft pick Jam Miller and 2026 undrafted free agent Myles Montgomery in the competition for a roster spot behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson . 
 DT Milton Williams said rookie OLB Gabe Jacas , who hadn't been with the team in the spring and signed his contract two days into training camp, has been getting ribbed by coach Mike Vrabel in meetings, and he's handling it in stride. Williams said Jacas has been called in front of the team about five times by Vrabel, and he recently lightened the mood with a joke. 
 Kyle Williams, who hobbled off the field late in Saturday's practice, did not participate Monday. 
 Vrabel wore a scout-team linebacker jersey at one point in a walk-through portion of practice, and when he filled a gap to make a "tackle," he had a mock celebration by thrusting his right arm in the air. 
 Rookie CB Karon Prunty (fifth round, Wake Forest) had a pass breakup on a play in which Maye attempted to connect with Brown on a deep ball, which had the defense buzzing. 
 Prunty was in coverage on the final play of practice, when backup QB Tommy DeVito threw a fade to Boutte in the end zone, with the receiver flashing late hands for an impressive tight-window TD. 
 Undrafted WR Nick DeGennaro (James Madison) and Prunty had a shared-catch play on a deep ball from No. 3 QB Behren Morton along the right sideline. DeGennaro came away with the football after a lengthy period of time, but it's hard to say what an official might have ruled in a game. 
 Starting inside linebacker Christian Elliss didn't finish practice, which had Chad Muma (fifth year) stepping into the top unit alongside Robert Spillane . 
 Undrafted free agent inside linebacker Khalil Jacobs (Missouri) seemed to take second-unit repetitions over veteran K.J. Britt . 
 Six-year veteran James Hudson III , who has primarily been a tackle throughout his career, aligned at right guard with the second unit. 
 This was the Patriots' first indoor practice of training camp, with the team moving due to rain. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Rookie outside linebacker Gabe Jacas practiced for the first time Saturday, as he officially was removed from the non-football injury list.

 It was a breakthrough for Jacas, whom the team traded up eight spots in the second round to select 55th overall in hopes he could spark its pass rush.

 Jacas was limited in the practice, not yet participating in team drills. But he still made his presence felt by knocking over outside linebackers coach Mike Smith, who was holding a blocking pad and absorbing contact from rushers.

 It had been a long time coming for Jacas, who was not with the team all spring after reporting for rookie minicamp May 7-9 as he underwent a procedure on his left knee. Jacas also didn't sign his contract until two days into training camp as the sides worked through a negotiation that included an injury waiver to protect the team.

 "He loves football. He's been itching to get back," coach Mike Vrabel said Saturday. "He texts me late at night, 'Hey, am I going to practice tomorrow?' You want guys that are looking for ways in, as opposed to looking for ways out. I think he just wants to get out there, get acclimated and be with his teammates. He just wants to play football."

 At one point in Saturday's practice, Vrabel worked one-on-one with Jacas on punt protection technique. Coincidentally, Jacas donned No. 50 -- the number Vrabel wore as a member of the Patriots.

 On defense, Jacas projects as a backup behind veteran starters  Dre'Mont Jones and Harold Landry III . With Landry opening camp on the physically unable to perform list (knee), second-year player Elijah Ponder has stepped into his starting role.

 Bradyn Swinson (2025 fifth-round pick), Xavier Holmes (2026 undrafted free agent), Jesse Luketa (four-year veteran who spent last year on the Rams' practice squad), Quintayvious Hutchins (2026 seventh-round pick) and Amari Gainer (joined Patriots practice squad in December of 2025) round out the depth chart along with Jacas.

 

 More observations: 

 
 Saturday was a "call it" practice, which Vrabel explained meant there was no script and players didn't know what play would be called, or what situation would be created, and they had to react accordingly. 
 WR A.J. Brown didn't finish practice, which might have been related to Vrabel saying several veterans would have their workloads scaled back as the team practiced in full pads for the third straight day. Vrabel said before practice that CB Christian Gonzalez , G Alijah Vera-Tucker , CB Marcus Jones , RB Rhamondre Stevenson and OT Morgan Moses would fall into that category. 
 Starting DT Christian Barmore returned to practice after missing Friday's…

 The legacy of Taysom Hill in New Orleans: 'There's only one' 
 WR Chris Olave signing four-year extension 
 Versatile Taysom Hill not returning to Saints for 10th season 
 

 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The Saints' offense bounced back in the team's first day in pads. It was a run-focused day featuring some usage of 12 and 13 personnel (sets with two and three tight ends).

 Saints quarterback Tyler Shough and the offensive unit had a solid end to practice when he completed a pass to Alvin Kamara , hit Travis Etienne Jr . near the sideline and connected again with Etienne, who found running room thanks to a hole opened up by Erik McCoy .

 Shough also had completions to Jordyn Tyson and Juwan Johnson (the last one coming with pressure from several defensive linemen). Rookie wideout Barion Brown had what might have been the play of the day, catching a deep pass down the sideline from Spencer Rattler while going against cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. 

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Charlie Smyth made five of six field goal attempts, missing his first kick of camp (wide right from 55 yards). Smyth kicked a 44-yarder again after his miss and made it. 
 Quincy Riley and Isaac Yiadom  substituted in with the first team at outside cornerback. Linebacker Danny Stutsman also got first-team reps. 
 The Saints practiced one-on-one individual drills for the first time. Tyson did not participate in those to limit his overall reps for the day, but Bub Means had a few solid reps. 
 Cesar Ruiz had another excused absence after the recent birth of his child. 
 Coach Kellen Moore did not say whether the Saints planned to bring in another receiver after the unexpected retirement of Ja'Lynn Polk . 
 

 
 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 The Saints' defense had a solid showing in a day that involved a lot of 11-on-11 red zone work. It specifically shined in the final period of the day. Linebacker Pete Werner punched the ball out of running back  Travis Etienne Jr .'s hands after he caught a pass from Tyler Shough ; safety Jonas Sanker blitzed and had a pressure to force an incompletion; and Chase Young had a pressure on an end zone interception from Shough that was caught by Julian Blackmon .

 On the first play of team drills, Shough made a nice downfield throw from the Saints' 35-yard line to Chris Olave in the end zone, but it was hard to tell if Olave, working against Quincy Riley , came down with the ball in bounds.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 The Saints practiced in their indoor facility because of a rainstorm, so practice was closed to fans. 
 Saints coach Kellen Moore said defensive tackle Bryan Bresee will have surgery for a torn ACL . 
 Tanner Brown rotated in as kicker and went 5-for-5 in field goals. So far he has missed one field goal in camp and Charlie Smyth has missed none. 
 Shough was knocked to the ground at one point in 11-on-11 drills, marking the second time this has happened in the first week of practice despite his red noncontact jersey. 
 Cesar Ruiz and Ja'Lynn Polk were excused absences again. Ruiz recently posted on social media that he and his wife welcomed their first child. 
 Edge rusher Michael Heldman , who signed with the Saints as a UDFA, had a nice series with the third team where he had two pressures on Zach Wilson in four plays, including one where the ball fell incomplete. 
 Rookie wideout Bryce Lance had back-to-back touchdowns while working with Spencer Rattler and the second team in 7-on-7s. 
 

 

 
 Friday, July 31 
 Chris Olave was a full participant in practice for the first time this offseason after agreeing to a contract extension on Thursday . For the first two days of camp, Olave did only individual position drills as they worked out the final details of the contract.
 "It was kind of a deal where we kind of had to meet halfway [because of] the injuries and everything that happened," Olave said of the extension. "The uncertainty in the future, especially with the blood clot and concussions. We kind of met halfway. They did a great job of communicating that. And I feel like, my agent and them came to a good deal for both of us."

 On Friday he participated in 11-on-11 drills, at one time lining up outside rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson . Olave and Tyson have been establishing their chemistry throughout the offseason, including a cohesive charity event set for Saturday. They showed off their bond in front of fans for the first time Friday.

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Guard  Cesar Ruiz and wide receiver  Ja'Lynn Polk were excused from practice for personal reasons. Dillon Radunz subbed in for Ruiz with the first unit 
 Nose tackle  Davon Godchaux was given a rest day, while cornerback  Kool-Aid McKinstry had a light practice after tweaking his ankle the day before. Isaac Yiadom got snaps in McKinstry's place. 
 Charlie Smyth went 5-for-5 on field goals again on Friday. Smyth is kicking with a cast on his thumb after a summer injury, but joked to the media that he is the only player who doesn't actually need to use their hands. 
 Coach Kellen Moore said the team doesn't have a planned scrimmage like last year, so they can prep for their three joint practices instead. 
 Center Erik McCoy said his confidence has never wavered after two years of injuries and has tweaked his workout regimen to try to strengthen past problem areas. 
 Former Saints first-round pick Andrus Peat  (No. 13 overall in 2015) announced his retirement after 11 seasons. 
 

 
 Thursday, July 30 
 Defensive tackle Bryan Bresee was the only notable absence from Day 2 of training camp after injuring his right knee Wednesday. Saints coach Kellen Moore said Bresee is getting a second opinion on a likely torn right ACL, but said initial results are "not great."

 Moore said that "it's tough" to lose Bresee and that younger players will have to be ready to step up. Veteran Nathan Shepherd and Vernon Broughton , a 2025 third-round pick who did not play most of last season because of injury, took snaps with the first string. The Saints will have to find a new combination of players to generate success from the interior of the defensive line without their 2023 first-round pick.

 "The goals don't change," Moore said. "We've still got plenty of guys in there that will be able to take advantage of an opportunity."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 The defense had a key sequence toward the end of practice in red zone work. Chase Young ran into Tyler Shough , knocking him to the ground, and Quincy Riley intercepted Shough on the next play when Shough was looking for rookie Jordyn Tyson . Shough shook that off and responded with a touchdown throw. 
 Tyson got plenty of reps in his second day of camp, including a touchdown in red zone work.

title: 2026 New York Giants training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Giants training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The New York Giants camp is taking place at The Greenbrier in White Sulphur Springs, West Virginia, and Giants reporter Jordan Raanan has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Giants camp. We will update this file often. How will the Giants handle increased expectations and a new coach? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Giants camp 
 
 Cam Skattebo admits doing 'dumb things,' will save backflips for TDs 
 Nabers 'looked good' in 1st practice since knee injury 
 Giants have spoken with Skattebo after Fanatics Fest flip 
 2026 New York Giants training camp preview 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 It was a rough day for the Giants' offense in pouring rain on the first day in full pads. The performance was really an extension of the early part of training camp for Jaxson Dart  & Co.

 A lot of penalties. Too many mental mistakes. Not enough positive plays. 
 
Dart threw an interception into the hands of safety Jevon Holland when the ball slipped out of the quarterback's hand while throwing. The Giants failed to score a touchdown on any of their drives and committed nine offensive penalties, everything from delay of games to endless false starts to holding by a wide receiver.

 "I think two things," coach John Harbaugh said. "I mean, I think you've got the elements a little bit, and you've got the first day in pads. So, it's not really unexpected, but we'll be working on it."

 Harbaugh added that he generally believes the offense is ahead of the defense early in camp. That seems not to be the case with his sloppy Giants as they digest new schemes.

 Other observations:  

 
 It was another strong practice from first-round pick Arvell Reese . The rookie linebacker had a run stop early in practice and later a sack when he beat left tackle Andrew Thomas . "The rookie has been impressive. Kid has a real chance to be special," veteran defensive tackle DJ Reader said. 
 Cornerback Deonte Banks is flashing early this summer. The former first-round pick has provided sticky coverage on receivers throughout camp. Monday's practice was no different. He tipped a pass that resulted in an interception by linebacker Micah McFadden . Banks later had Darius Slayton blanketed but dropped an interception that hit him in the chest. After some struggles, maybe Banks has it figured out? 
 
 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 It has been a quiet start to training camp from Odell Beckham Jr .

 Until Saturday.

 On the day when the Giants had their largest crowd of the summer at The Greenbrier in West Virginia, Beckham made the biggest play of the day. And received the biggest ovation of the summer to date.

 The veteran receiver made a leaping grab over a defender in the back of the end zone for a touchdown from quarterback Jameis Winston during 11-on-11 drills. It sent the crowd of approximately 2,000 fans into a frenzy and served as a reminder of what used to be.

 It was a big play for Beckham, who is battling for a roster spot with several other veterans. Braxton Berrios has stood out the most of the group this camp, until Saturday.

 "There's a lot of really good football players in our room right now," wide receiver Darius Slayton said. "From a competition-level standpoint, it's ... raised the competition level."

 Other observations: 

 
 Malik Nabers was back on the practice field after a day of rest Friday. He looked good running routes. This is a positive sign as he recovers from a serious knee injury that required multiple surgeries."[Saturday] seemed like a good day from what I can tell," coach John Harbaugh said. 
 Jaxson Dart and the offense have struggled the past few days. Saturday was an up-and-down practice for the second-year quarterback learning a new offense. It began with a feathery deep ball down the left sideline to Malachi Fields . Two plays later, Dart had a pass tipped by linebacker Tremaine Edmunds and intercepted by Paulson Adebo . Later, he had a bad interception to Edmunds and hit tight end Theo Johnson on a deep ball. Overall, Dart went 22-of-33 in live drills. 
 The Giants have the day off Sunday and return Monday for the first full practice with pads, which is the closest to real football we'll see before the preseason. Harbaugh said the Giants won't tackle to the ground. It will be "wrap and release," but it will be more physical. "It's almost that time," outside linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux said. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 

 Second-year linebacker Abdul Carter has enjoyed a strong start to training camp. It has him thinking big.

 His goal: "Be Defensive Player of the Year, for sure."

 Can it be this year?

 "Absolutely," he said.

 Why?

 "Just my process. I know who I can be and the belief in myself. I know what I'm capable of and I know if I put the work in and believe in myself, trust in myself, trust in my teammates, trust in my coaches, I can be whoever I want to be."

 Lofty goal after 4.0 sacks as a rookie. But Carter feels he learned a lot from last year, when he was benched twice for missing and being late to meetings. He thinks he hit his stride late in the season and can carry it into the next year.

 Other observations: 

 
 Second-year defensive lineman Darius Alexander ended practice with a leaping interception of Jaxson Dart near the line of scrimmage. The Giants were in field goal range at the time and it ended a sloppy practice that was filled with penalties on both sides of the ball. 
 Kicking update: It was Ben Sauls ' turn Friday and he made eight of his 10 field goal attempts. 
 
 

 Thursday, July 30 
 Pass rusher  Abdul Carter reminded everyone why he was the No. 3 overall pick last year. He was a menace in the second practice of the summer, constantly in the backfield and even getting credited with some sacks. Even more promising (though it was without pads) was that some of his best rushes came against standout left tackle Andrew Thomas . That is going to be a battle to watch throughout the summer.

 New coach John Harbaugh has liked what he's seen from Carter this offseason. He thinks it's just a matter of "consistency" with the young edge rusher who was benched on multiple occasions during his rookie year.

 
 Wide receiver Malik Nabers said he has "felt great" but doesn't want to put a timeline on his return. "When I'm ready, I'm ready," he said. It was also interesting that Nabers said he's been running routes for weeks and the reported timeline for his second surgery was incorrect. Bottom line: He still confirmed he had the second surgery. 
 Edge rusher Kayvon Thibodeaux had a tipped-pass interception that he returned for a touchdown. It's early but he has looked really good. Expect to hear his name a lot this summer going against the second-team offensive line. 
 Daily kicking update: Only one field goal was attempted during Thursday's practice and Dominic Zvada nailed a 57-yarder with room to spare. A good bounceback from the undrafted rookie. 
 

 
 Wednesday, July 29 
 The big news out of West Virginia was that star wide receiver Malik Nabers was back practicing with his teammates for the first time. But he wasn't on the field with the offense during team drills. 
 
Even without him, quarterback Jaxson Dart and the offense were the story. They looked good. Dart went 17-of-24, which included three spikes and a drop by tight end Theo Johnson . It was a promising sign for a unit that struggled a bit in the spring learning a new offense.

title: How does the Jets' starting defense look?
summary: Richard Cimini reports that Minkah Fitzpatrick picks off Geno Smith at Jets training camp.

title: 2026 New York Jets training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Jets training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  New York Jets  camp is taking place at the Atlantic Health Training Facility in Florham Park, New Jersey, and Jets reporter Rich Cimini has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Jets camp. We will update this file often. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Jets camp 
 
 Jets' Smith rues being 'distraction' after dispute with girlfriend 
 2026 Jets training camp preview 
 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 There was an unusual occurrence on the practice field -- an interception by the defense, the first of training camp for the starters.

 Former All-Pro safety  Minkah Fitzpatrick , one of the Jets' marquee additions, picked off Geno Smith 's first pass in 11-on-11 drills -- a noteworthy feat, considering last season's ignominy.

 You may have heard: The Jets were the first team in NFL history to go an entire season without intercepting a pass. We're talking about almost a full century; the league started tracking interceptions in 1933.

 The defensive backs, in particular, are determined to end the embarrassing slump. They dream about getting takeaways.

 "Shoot, I tell that to myself, even in my sleep," cornerback  Brandon Stephens  said after practice.

 It's one of the big reasons why they traded for Fitzpatrick and gave him a three-year, $40 million contract . Since entering the league in 2018, he's tied for ninth in interceptions (21).

 "He's extremely smart and he loves football -- and at safety, that's what you're looking for," coach Aaron Glenn said of Fitzpatrick. "Look, I've had some good safeties in my career. Early on, I like exactly where he's at."

 Fitzpatrick can line up in multiple spots. On his interception, he was in the deep middle. He got an assist from LB Demario Davis , who got nice depth in his pass drop. It forced Smith into an overthrow, with the pass going directly to Fitzpatrick.

 An easy pick -- if there is such a thing for this defense.

 Other observations:  

 
 Injury updates: Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq , who participated in the first three practices after offseason hernia surgery, got a rest day as part of his maintenance program. NT T'Vondre Sweat (hamstring), DE Joseph Ossai (undisclosed) and rookie CB D'Angelo Ponds (calf) still haven't practiced. They will be sidelined at least another week, per Glenn. Sweat is on the non-football injury list, Ossai the PUP list. 
 There were several dropped passes in wet, rainy conditions -- the first practice in pads. One player who didn't struggle was rookie WR  Omar Cooper Jr ., who made a terrific, over-the-shoulder catch on a deep ball from Smith. Cooper is expected to have a significant role. 
 RT Armand Membou is having a strong camp. After a solid rookie year, the 2025 first-round pick is poised for a breakout. Glenn praised his mindset, saying he noticed in last season's exit meeting that Membou "was on a mission and you saw it on his face. There was no B.S." Membou's daily battles with rookie DE David Bailey are must-see. 
 CB Azareye'h Thomas changed his number in the offseason, dropping 23 and opting for 1, famously worn by Sauce Gardner for three-plus seasons. Thomas recognizes the pressure that comes with that number, but he didn't make the switch because he wants to be the next Sauce. He cited his faith, saying he plays "for an audience of one" -- God. 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 

 Geno Smith pitched a perfect practice on Saturday.

 The Jets' starting quarterback completed every pass in 11-on-11 periods (11-for-11) and did the same in 7-on-7 (4-for-4). Yes, it was a non-contact unpadded practice, and, yes, most of the reps came in the red zone -- favorable circumstances for a quarterback. But let's not lose sight of the big picture. Any time a Jets quarterback can go an entire practice without the ball hitting the ground ... well, let's just say it's noteworthy.

 Coach Aaron Glenn credited offensive coordinator Frank Reich and quarterbacks coach Bill Musgrave with helping Smith to a quick start.

 "I think he and Frank are on the same page," Glenn said after practice. "Our quarterbacks coach is doing a hell of a job, teaching him and actually expanding his knowledge as far as what we're trying to do. And one good thing about Geno is, for as long as he's been in this league, he's still learning. I think that's a good trait for any player, that we don't know it all and we can pick up something new from a new coach."

 Smith's primary target was WR Garrett Wilson (five catches in 11-on-11), who came alive after two quiet practices. WR Adonai Mitchell , who caught two of Smith's four touchdown passes, continued his hot start to camp. Smith also got tight ends Jeremy Ruckert (two catches) and rookie Kenyon Sadiq (one) involved.

 More observations: 

 
 It was a shaky practice for rookie QB Cade Klubnik , who was intercepted once in 11-on-11 and once in 7-on-7. Things move quickly in the red zone -- too quickly for Klubnik, who appeared tentative at times. The Jets are hoping the former Clemson star can lock down the No. 2 job, but he has a long way to go. 
 Rookie edge rusher David Bailey , dominant on Thursday, was neutralized by RT Armand Membou . The No. 2 overall pick wasn't nearly as disruptive as he was in the previous practice. "He's a really good player," Bailey said of Membou. "Great feet. Strong. Extremely strong. Ridiculously strong. So he's been getting me better. He's a great person to work on my skillset." 
 The tight end position, perennially weak, now boasts two high picks from the last two drafts -- Kenyon Sadiq  (2026 first-round pick) and Mason Taylor (2025 second-round pick). If Taylor was upset by Sadiq's arrival, he did a good job of hiding it. He endorsed the move, saying, "I think we're building something special in the tight-end room." He said they can be "pretty dangerous." 
 A handful of Glenn's former Jets teammates watched practice, including Wayne Chrebet, Adrian Murrell, Ray Mickens, Fred Baxter and Glenn Foley. Laveranues Coles also was on hand. 
 The Jets have no practice Sunday, their second "off" day in three days. Their first padded practice is Monday. 
 

 

 

 Thursday, July 30 
 Prized rookie edge rusher David Bailey flashed quickness and closing speed, sacking Geno Smith three times in non-contact team drills.

 Bailey, the No. 2 overall pick, was a headache for tackles Armand Membou and Olu Fashanu . In fact, Bailey split a double-team block by Membou and running back Breece Hall on one of the sacks. Bailey is "a pain in the ass," guard Joe Tippmann said respectfully, speaking on behalf of the offensive line.

 This, of course, is exactly what the Jets expected when they made Bailey the highest-drafted defensive player in franchise history.

 "It'll be real exciting once we get the pads on," coach Aaron Glenn said after practice. "I think we all understand through these acclamation days, we're still in shorts, but just to be able to see the energy and the speed and the quickness off the edge, and the ability to hold a strong edge and the way that he wants to play the run game, it's everything that I imagined from that player."

 The Jets produced 26 sacks last season, second fewest in the league. Their hope is that Bailey, who led the FBS with 14.5 sacks, can provide instant electricity. He's off to a terrific start in camp, and it'll be fascinating to monitor his progress once the pads go on. The first padded practice is Monday.

 More…

title: 2026 Philadelphia Eagles training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Eagles training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Philadelphia Eagles camp is taking place in the Jefferson Health Training Complex, and Eagles reporter Tim McManus has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and -- of course -- the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Eagles camp. We will update this file often. How will quarterback  Jalen Hurts fare in the reimagined offense? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Eagles camp 
 
 Eagles, DT Carter agree to four-year, $152M extension 
 2026 Philadelphia Eagles training camp preview 
 Eagles coach Nick Sirianni adjusting to offseason changes 
 
 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Quarterback Jalen Hurts had his best day of camp to date. It started with a deep sideline throw to Dontayvion Wicks followed by a dot to Elijah Moore down the right seam. Hurts lit it up in the red zone, finding DeVonta Smith for a pair of touchdowns before running in for another score moments later, leading to a leaping celebration with Saquon Barkley and other teammates. There was one notable blemish on the day -- a short pass to Moore that was jumped by Quinyon Mitchell for a pick-six -- but the practice was defined by sharp, on-time throws, including one deep over the middle that led to a highlight diving catch by Darius Cooper .

 Other observations: 

 
 Right tackle Lane Johnson (excused/not injury related) was absent for a second straight practice. Rookie receiver Makai Lemon did not participate in team drills after taking part in individual drills earlier in the session. 
 The second-team defense got work against the first-team offense. Credit linebacker Chance Campbell for sniffing out a Barkley run to the outside and darting into the backfield to make a stop. 
 Andy Dalton appeared to outplay Tanner McKee as the battle for the No. 2 QB spot continues. Dalton fired a completion over the middle to Johnny Wilson with Jihaad Campbell looming in coverage. McKee underthrew Wilson later in the session and appeared to hold onto the ball for too long at times in the red zone. 
 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 The Eagles' defense flexed its muscles, making for some tough sledding for Jalen Hurts  & Co. over the one-hour, 40-minute session. Hurts had two passes batted at the line of scrimmage to start the session -- first by Zack Baun , then Jalen Carter . That set the tone for a day defined by heavy pressure and little flow to the pass game.

 Carter, fresh off signing a mega-extension , was a problem, and the same can be said for Jalyx Hunt , who has spent much of training camp to date in the backfield.

 Other observations: 

 
 Jeremiah Trotter Jr . got the nod at starting linebacker in Jihaad Campbell 's absence (excused/not injury-related) and made his presence felt, showing good anticipation to disrupt the short-to-intermediate passing game. 
 Safety Andrew Mukuba and rookie receiver Makai Lemon collided over the middle of the field going after what proved to be a Hurts incompletion. Fortunately, no one was injured on the play. Lemon has seen plenty of action as the primary slot receiver but has had a relatively quiet start to camp. 
 Receiver Dontayvion Wicks had another quality practice. He made a contested catch over the middle and muscled through Michael Carter II for some yards after the catch. 
 

 

 Thursday, July 30 
 New Eagles receiver Dontayvion Wicks made the play of the day and may have earned more of Jalen Hurts ' trust in the process. Near the end of Thursday's practice, Hurts unfurled a pass deep down the field to Wicks, who was double covered by defensive backs Cole Wisniewski and Jakorian Bennett . Wicks elevated over both of them and secured the catch.

 The former Packer is trying to solidify his spot as the No. 2 wideout in this offense alongside DeVonta Smith . Coach Nick Sirianni has clearly taken a liking to him, comparing Wicks to the accomplished Keenan Allen .

 Other observations:  

 
 There is a heavy amount of misdirection in Sean Mannion's offense. It helped open up big holes for the running backs Thursday, with Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby taking advantage for sizable gains. Bigsby brings some juice and likely earned some more playing time in 2026 after averaging 5.9 yards per attempt for the Eagles last season. 
 Rookie QB Cole Payton came down to earth following a strong performance Wednesday, throwing interceptions on back-to-back plays. 
 Second-year corner Mac McWilliams muscled an Andy Dalton pass away from running back Elijah Mitchell for the breakup. Credit veteran corner Jonathan Jones for blanketing DeVonta Smith down the field to force an incompletion. 
 
 

 Wednesday, July 29 
 There were some encouraging signs from the Eagles' new-look offense on Day 1 of camp. The learning curve they're working through is obvious -- there was one sequence where a pre-snap penalty was followed by a botched running play when  Jalen Hurts and Saquon Barkley were on different pages. But there were also moments where things clicked, like on a hookup between Hurts and DeVonta Smith where Hurts dropped to his right and zipped a strike to his now-No. 1 receiver down the left seam with Quinyon Mitchell tight in coverage.

 Hurts worked primarily under center and targeted the middle of the field a good amount, departures from how he has generally operated to this point in the NFL. There was enough good mixed in to consider it a positive opening to the summer.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterbacks Tanner McKee and Andy Dalton split second-team reps. The two rotated days as the primary backup in the spring. This is developing into an interesting competition. If the Eagles feel comfortable having either in that role, it would make it easier to trade one of them should a QB-needy team come calling. 
 Rookie QB Cole Payton showed some really nice touch on deep throws, including one that he shot over defenders and into the arms of receiver Britain Covey down the right seam. He has impressed so far this offseason. 
 Second-year wideout Darius Cooper had the catch of the day, laying out to snag a pass from Hurts deep down the middle of the field. 
 On the safety competition front, Andrew Mukuba and Marcus Epps got the bulk of the work in sub packages, with Cooper DeJean filling in for Epps when Vic Fangio's group was in base. 
 
 
 

 Tuesday, July 28 
 Jalen Carter reported to camp with the rest of his teammates, fresh off becoming the highest-paid defensive tackle in NFL history in both guaranteed money ($106 million) and average annual value ($38 million).

 Though it remains to be seen whether this proves to be a wise long-term investment, it rids the team of any possible short-term distraction as it begins preparations for the 2026 season. Carter did not participate fully in practice this spring, sparking questions about whether he would "hold in" while awaiting a new deal. The focus now shifts to the playing field.

 The Eagles have the formidable tackle duo of Carter and Jordan Davis secured for the foreseeable future after giving Davis a three-year, $78 million extension earlier this offseason.

title: 'Tempered': Inside Mike McCarthy's new vision for Steelers
summary: Pittsburgh's new coach is blending sports science and the city's steel-making roots to forge a different camp culture.
full_text:
LATROBE, Pa. -- After leaving their first team meeting of the 2026 training camp Wednesday morning, the Pittsburgh Steelers found new shirts hanging in their lockers at St. Vincent College.

 "Tempered" stretched across the black shirt in gold lettering, and the back expanded on the definition of the slogan: "More than talented. More than tough. Tempered."

 "[It's about] the parallels between the city of Pittsburgh, the Steel Mill industry, the tempering process of how steel was built -- and still is today -- and the parallels between coming together as a football team," coach Mike McCarthy told ESPN.

 McCarthy said as much to his team in their first meeting, that they should be a reflection of the city's gritty heritage. It's why McCarthy chose "tempered" as the defining word of his first training camp as the Steelers' new head coach.

 

 "We have to be tough, hard, and this is a blue-collar town," Steelers guard Spencer Anderson said, relaying what McCarthy told them. "Button up, bring your lunch pail and let's go, because that's always where we've been since 1933. ... Can't fold under the heat. And when the heat comes, you got to make steel -- or I guess do the right things, so to speak."

 But tempered in McCarthy's use has dual meanings. Not only can it mean toughened and made resilient, but it can also mean being controlled. To McCarthy, tempered isn't just about raw strength. It's about being controlled in the approach to building that strength. And through a week of training camp, McCarthy's practices have been deliberately, even scientifically, tempered to train the mind as much as the body.

 "Everything's calculated," McCarthy said, adding that he relies on GPS data on devices worn by players to help construct his practice plan. "Everything's regulated. There's obviously science behind it. We're in tune with the conditioning of our players. The commitment the players made in the spring was evident. ... This is all by design. There's history behind it. ... Everybody has a genetic background that you pay attention to. Some guys can rev higher than others. And so this is part of the process."

 Through five practices, the differences between McCarthy's approach and former coach Mike Tomlin's are palpable. One isn't necessarily better than the other, players stressed, but the practices are different.

 "We're used to a hundred miles an hour, nonstop, and we're kind of dead tired by the end of practice," Anderson said. "But now we can kind of temper it down, and we still have maybe 10% left in the tank. But obviously don't tell [McCarthy] I said that."

 Part of that, of course, is the team is still in its ramp-up period with shorter practices as mandated by the collective bargaining agreement. But McCarthy is also heavily reliant on sports science in formulating his practice plans. That's why Monday's practice, the Steelers' first in pads, was noticeably less physical than the first padded practices in the Tomlin era (2007 to 2025).

 

 "It did feel different when I'm used to all that physical," Pittsburgh running back Jaylen Warren said Monday. "But I understand why we don't do it, and the philosophy behind it. Just adapting to it. ... At the end of the day, we're trying to keep guys up, keep them healthy. The season's the most important thing and winning is the most important thing."

 Warren told reporters Saturday he was certain that even with McCarthy's changes, the team would still go through the signature backs-on-backers drill. During Tomlin's tenure, it was a highlight of padded practices, often beginning with the first one, in which running backs and linebackers matched up in a one-on-one battle. Monday, though, the running backs and linebackers didn't square off. Instead, the offensive linemen and pass rushers went against one another while the skill position players worked in a 7-on-7 period.

 "As long as we have it, I'm prepared," Warren said of backs-on-backers. "I'm trusting the process that they got us going through, so I ain't complaining about nothing."

 McCarthy, who said he is "absolutely" a fan of backs-on-backers, might still have the drill in a future padded practice, but one thing he won't have is live tackling. While most of the league also spurns live tackling in camp, Tomlin embraced it in his ultra-physical late afternoon practices.

 "The only thing that's different is we don't want to go to the ground and risk injury, but I think everything else will look the same," McCarthy said, affirming that his practices would still be plenty physical.

 To coach tackling without actually doing it, McCarthy and his staff are breaking down the basic elements of the skill. In fact, the majority of McCarthy's early practices are all about the fundamentals -- the "Steelers Six" -- coached through meticulously scripted and executed individual periods. That's a departure from a Tomlin era that featured extensive team periods and always opened with "Seven Shots," an intense goal line competition.

 

 "A lot of Coach T's camps, it was a lot of team periods and mano-a-mano type of thing, but this is kind of more, get good work, working smart and hard," Anderson said. "Not to say that we weren't working smart back then, but it's just Coach McCarthy explains to us that he's a big sports science guy, so he'll never run us into the ground or do things that'll make us feel like we're dead tired. I think it's a good balance of work and taking care of us."

 Through five practices, McCarthy's training camp hasn't featured a single goal-line team period. Instead, in addition to the extensive individual periods, McCarthy has emphasized situational football -- working first on two-minute offense and then beginning the second week of camp with third and fourth downs. By stressing those situations in his up-tempo practices, McCarthy is strengthening the team's nervous system and mental fortitude.

 "Everybody talks about the physical and the mental stress of a physical camp," McCarthy said, explaining the cadence of his practices. "Well, what the hell about the nervous system? Who's training that? How are you tapping that? How are you pushing that? Where are you getting that at? Where's the mental toughness? Where's the emotional toughness? How do you train that on a football field? This is all by design."

 And though McCarthy's approach is an adjustment for players who grew accustomed to Tomlin's camps, many are embracing change.

 "I got to," said Cam Heyward, the longest-tenured Steeler. "The dinosaurs didn't, and look what happened to them."

The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action.
