 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Steelers camp 
 
 Steelers' Broderick Jones cleared after eight months (neck) 
 Rodgers: 'Zero debate' 2026 will be last season 
 Jalen Ramsey, Joey Porter Jr. placed on PUP list 
 Steelers revamp wide receiver unit 
 Rodgers reunites with family ahead of final NFL season 
 

 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The Steelers' Monday morning meeting featured a different kind of film study before their first day in pads. Instead of practice footage, coach Mike McCarthy pulled up the viral video of tight end Pat Freiermuth pulling a kid out from the crush of fans crowding the fence in an attempt to get autographs from players after Saturday's practice.

 "That was hilarious," quarterback Will Howard said of the video, adding that they dubbed Freiermuth the "unsung hero of the week" for his quick thinking to protect the young fan.

 "Situational awareness. We talk about it all the time. On and off the field."

 A scrum broke out between a couple of adults Saturday as Freiermuth and his teammates worked the autograph line, a hallmark of the Steelers' practices at St. Vincent College. Freiermuth noticed a child in front of him and snagged him, lifting him up and over the mesh fence as the the shoving escalated.

 "I just saw a bunch of people tumbling down and fighting," Freiermuth said. "I looked down at the kid I was signing for, and he looked a little scared, so it was the least I could do."

 Freiermuth also joked the fans weren't fighting over his autograph, but instead they wanted one from Howard.

 "If you're going to fight for an autograph, it can't be Will Howard's," he said with a laugh. While Howard was quick to say he doesn't condone fans -- especially adults -- fighting over his autograph, he added that the fan element of Steelers training camp is part of what makes it special.

 "Yeah, it's crazy," Howard said. "It's a good feeling to be wanted. And at this point, I just want to give them something to cheer about because I really haven't been able to go out in the field and give them any product to really cheer for."

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 The defense won each of the practice-ending two-minute drills. The first came as linebacker Patrick Queen picked off Aaron Rodgers in the end zone on a pass that appeared to be intended for running back Rico Dowdle . On the second, Howard's final heave to the end zone on fourth down was broken up by rookie cornerback Daylen Everette . 
 Despite coach Mike McCarthy saying he was "absolutely" a fan of backs-on-backers, the Steelers' first day of padded practice didn't feature that physical drill. Instead, the Steelers had an offensive line vs. pass rush period during 7-on-7. 
 Wide receiver Cole Burgess left practice on a cart after appearing to injure his knee as he tried to catch a deep pass from Howard. Earlier in the day, Burgess hauled in a deep ball from rookie quarterback Drew Allar . 
 First-round pick Max Iheanachor worked primarily as the second-team right tackle throughout practice and turned in a solid performance. "He's making strides every single day, and he works really hard," said left tackle Troy Fautanu , who was the team's 2024 first-round pick. "I'm excited for him and for the rest of the training camp and how it plays out." 
 Rodgers told Mike Silver of The Athletic that he expected to play in the Steelers' two home preseason games. McCarthy seemingly confirmed the plan, though said it hasn't been finalized. "He'd like to play," McCarthy said Monday morning. "I would like to see him play, but we won't make a decision until we get all the way up to it because there's more that goes into that, just having one player play. It's the combination of players." 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 

 

 Nobody had a louder cheering section than safety Jaquan Brisker at Saturday's practice.

 The Pittsburgh native and former Penn State star had more than 100 family members, all wearing gold shirts customized with his name and No. 3, and numerous coaches from his prep football days sitting in the stands at St. Vincent College for a football practice-turned-family reunion organized by one of his uncles.

 "... My dad texted me and was like, 'Yeah, [the family] is going to come up here,'" Brisker, a 2022 second-round pick, said. "I texted some of the Steelers, and they got them a section. ... Just a lot of love and support, and I really appreciate it."

 "[My teammates] were like, 'Look at the Brisker section,' making jokes and things like that."

 Though Brisker, who spent four years with the Chicago Bears before signing with the Steelers in free agency earlier this year, didn't get a chance to pick off a pass in front of his extended family, he celebrated wildly in their direction after cornerback Brandin Echols broke up a pass from Aaron Rodgers during the final team period.

 "Got to bring the energy," Brisker said. "I'm blessed to step on the field every single day and walk off every single day. I'm blessed to walk off today. And I've been loving it since I was 4. And being a Pittsburgh guy, this is all I breathe was football."

 Afterward, Brisker's family came down to see him on the field and got him to sign each of their shirts. From there, the group was headed to eat a big meal together. Brisker, though, had team meetings.

 "I'm going to miss out the cookout, but it's OK," he said. "Hopefully, they save me a plate."

 

 

 
 Friday, July 31 
To cornerback Asante Samuel Jr ., every year is a "prove-it" year. And through three days of Steelers camp, he has more than done that with several head-turning plays in team periods.
 "You got to prove yourself each and every year," the 2021  Los Angeles Chargers  second-round pick said. "And just coming back from my injuries from last year, played a couple games last year, so trying to build off that and just show them how I was before I got injured."

 Samuel, who joined the Steelers as a free agent last year after a lengthy recovery from a spinal fusion surgery to correct a chronic issue, has benefited from the absence of Joey Porter Jr . (physically unable to perform list with his back) and made the most of his time Friday with a number of pass breakups and near interceptions.

 "He's frankly been one of my favorite players since I arrived here," Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said of Samuel, who made three starts last season and grabbed an interception. "I just love the way he works. He's extremely physical. His ball skills are off the charts. That's a big thing. That's something I really look for in defensive backs. We want to take the ball away, catch the flash of the ball. And he has all that.

 "He's been here every single day, offseason program. He's had two really good practices so far. His first day, he did a really nice job. So I think the young man's a hell of a football player."

 Not only does McCarthy consider him "a hell of a football player" -- Samuel also came up as a prospective U.S. Olympic flag football team member. "I was talking to Art [Rooney II] about the flag football candidates, and I think his name was one of the names come…

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Seattle Seahawks ' camp is taking place in Renton, Washington, and Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Seahawks camp. We will update this file often. What is new with the defending Super Bowl champions? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Seahawks camp 
 
 WR Tory Horton healthy after cracking tibia last season 
 Seattle Pro Bowl DL Williams confirms deal talks 
 Seattle's Nick Emmanwori has ankle surgery, expected to play W1 
 Who are the Khoslas? Meet the family set to buy the Seahawks 
 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The play of the day on Monday was one that Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald had been wanting to see.

 With Seattle's No. 1 offense facing the No. 2 defense in an 11-on-11 session, Sam Darnold found Rashid Shaheed deep down the middle of the field for a touchdown. Shaheed had gained more than a step on speedy rookie cornerback Michael Dansby , and Darnold hit him in perfect stride.

 "We got it thrown over our head finally, so that was a good wakeup call for us on defense," Macdonald said. "But that's definitely a point of emphasis after this first week is trying to get Rashid the ball on some of those deeper targets."

 The Seahawks might not have claimed the NFC's No. 1 seed last year or won Super Bowl LX if it weren't for their midseason acquisition of Shaheed, whom they re-signed in March to a three-year, $51 million deal. But his playmaking mostly came on special teams, where he scored three return touchdowns.

 His offensive production -- an average of 29.3 scrimmage yards over 12 games with Seattle -- left something to be desired, especially considering he had previously played for then-coordinator Klint Kubiak in New Orleans.

 While the playbook wasn't new to Shaheed, the quarterback was, and their lack of familiarity may have played some role in the receiver's underwhelming production. Even on the biggest offensive play he made for Seattle -- a 51-yard catch in the NFC Championship Game -- their timing was off by a hair, as Shaheed had to break his stride just enough to allow the cornerback he had beaten to catch back up and prevent a touchdown.

 The two couldn't connect on a pair of deep throws in the Super Bowl, one of which was sightly overthrown.

 But they did on Monday.

 "There's way more banked reps underneath our belt," Macdonald said of Darnold and Shaheed, who got together for throwing sessions over the summer in Southern California, where both are from. "I think both guys are in a really good place. Kind of the challenge of camp is, how far can we take it? Really, that's what we're focusing on right now, is how far can we take that relationship? How far can we take his route tree? How great of a timing can we create with those two guys?"

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Macdonald said the undisclosed injury that has kept rookie CB Julian Neal out for the last few days is a "shorter-term" issue. 
 Also remaining out Monday were WR Jake Bobo , DL Mike Morris , LBs Jamie Sheriff and Chris Paul Jr ., OLB Jared Ivey and FB Robbie Ouzts . "We're going to try to find some more information with Robbie's situation," Macdonald said. "I'll just leave it at that right now. We'll have an update for you sooner than later." 
 Macdonald recently lauded CB Devon Witherspoon for continuing to bring his usual enthusiasm despite his unsettled contract situation. He gave similar praise Monday to DT Leonard Williams , who recently said that his agents and the Seahawks have talked about an extension. "To be able to manage that and still be a person that he is every day and be the asset that he is for the rest of his teammates and put the football product on the field like he is every day, it's pretty remarkable," Macdonald said. "Spoon's doing the same thing. You really just tip your cap to him, honestly." 
 The Seahawks got a visit Monday from San Antonio Spurs coach Mitch Johnson and several other members of that organization. Johnson is a Seattle native and Seahawks fan. Macdonald said they share an alignment in "how we want to run our programs" as well as the experience of having taken over for a legendary coach (Pete Carroll in Seattle, Gregg Popovich in San Antonio). 
 Among the ex-Seahawks in attendance was Duane Brown , Seattle's left tackle from 2017 to 2021. He appears to have slimmed down significantly since he last played for the Jets in 2023. Said RT Abraham Lucas : "Honestly, I had no idea that was Duane Brown. I hope I look that way when I'm done playing." 
 

 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Arguably no Seahawks player has stood out in any of the first seven practices of camp as much as Elijah Arroyo did Saturday. The second-year tight end was the clear star on a good day for the offense.

 It started in a red zone one-on-one period, when he caught touchdown passes on a high-point fade and a toe-tapper in the back of the end zone. In the subsequent team period, Sam Darnold hit a wide-open Arroyo down the field for another score.

 It was a strong follow-up to Arroyo's performance Friday, which was highlighted by a long reception on a deep throw from QB3 Jalen Milroe .

 It's one thing to make plays like that in a noncontact spring practice, when pass catchers tend to shine because defenders aren't fully contesting throws. Arroyo is doing it in the more realistic setting of training camp. Can he continue to do it when the games begin?

 Drafted 50th in the 2025 draft, Arroyo was as impressive as any Seahawks rookie during the spring and summer, but it didn't translate to regular-season production. He caught 15 passes on 26 targets for 179 yards and a touchdown in 14 games, including the Super Bowl. He spent five games on injured reserve (knee) and was inactive for the NFC Championship Game after returning to the active roster.

 With a first-time playcaller in Brian Fleury,  Kenneth Walker III  gone and fellow running back Zach Charbonnet coming off ACL surgery, there are some legitimate question marks with Seattle's offense. But whether Darnold has enough targets to throw to is not one of them -- especially if Arroyo emerges in Year 2.

 More observations: 

 
 RG Anthony Bradford and LB Ernest Jones IV were back after not finishing practice Friday. 
 FB Robbie Ouzts did not practice. 
 Still sidelined are WR Jake Bobo , CB Julian Neal , DT Brandon Pili , LB Jamie Sheriff and OLB Jared Ivey . 
 The Seahawks have an off day Sunday. 
 Seattle signed LB Joseph Vaughn and waived/injured LB Ja'Markis Weston . 
 

 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 The Seahawks' second practice in pads brought their first fight of this year's training camp.

 Actually, there were a couple, both coming during an 11-on-11 period.

 Defensive tackle Leonard Williams took exception to guard Bryce Cabeldue giving a one-handed shove to safety Rodney Thomas II at the end of a play. As Williams and Cabeldue were going at it, outside linebacker Derick Hall entered the fray and threw Cabeldue down from behind.

 Outside linebacker Connor O'Toole and tackle Bobby Hart got into a post-play scuffle a few minutes later.

 No one appeared to be kicked out of practice as a result. When it was over, Hart and linebacker Tyrice Knight were laughing as they walked off the field together.

 "That's normal," defensive tackle Byron Murphy II said of the tempers flaring. "Just guys trying to get better. It ain't nothing personal. Just guys competing. We get…

The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The San Francisco 49ers camp is taking place in Santa Clara, California, and 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at 49ers camp. We will update this file often. What does  Mike Evans  look like as a top receiver on the 49ers? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive into all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 
 

 Latest news from 49ers' camp 
 
 What's next for 49ers receivers Aiyuk, Deebo and Pearsall? 
 Deebo Samuel on reunion with 49ers: 'Just matter of time' 
 WR Ricky Pearsall to have season-ending knee surgery 
 VP Paraag Marathe exits to focus on soccer clubs

 49ers GM Lynch focused on 'players that are here,' not WR Aiyuk 
 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 3 
 The injuries continue to mount for the 49ers, particularly at wide receiver. On Monday, they added veteran Mike Evans to the list as he did not practice because of a quad strain.

 The injury is not believed to be serious and Evans did some work on the side during the session, but it again left the Niners a bit short-handed. With  Ricky Pearsall (knee) done for the season, rookie De'Zhaun Stribling battling hamstring tightness and Christian Kirk out for the better part of the past week with a calf strain, the team's projected top four wideouts were not available Monday.

 Kirk and Stribling also did some work on the side and should be back soon, but the situation bears watching given the number of injury issues that always seem to plague this team at that position group.

 More observations: 

 
 Mike Brown, the title-winning coach of the NBA's New York Knicks, watched practice Monday. His son Cameron is the Niners' defensive quality control coach. 
 Alex Smith, the former 49ers quarterback and current ESPN analyst, was also in attendance. 
 Running back Kaelon Black (adductor) was another addition to the injury report after he missed the second half of Saturday's practice. 
 Defensive tackle C.J. West and edge rusher Romello Height returned from injuries to participate Monday. 
 WR Deebo Samuel continues to show off fresh legs in camp as he was again quite involved in the offense. With all the injuries at receiver, there's an opening for Samuel to establish a role beyond returning kicks. 
 

 

 

 
 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 While no definitive date has been set for coach Kyle Shanahan to return to full-time duty, he seems to be taking the necessary steps in that direction.

 Before Saturday's practice, Shanahan addressed the team for the first time since his July 14 car accident, according to general manager John Lynch. Then, during practice, Shanahan emerged on the field before team drills and stayed through the end of the session. At one point late in practice, he even stood behind the offense, offering real-time feedback rather than standing next to Lynch in the deep middle of the field.

 "He's doing better," Lynch said. "He got a nice welcome, and it was good to have him up there. We'll continue to do kind of like a phased approach. So that was one threshold. He wanted to get up there. He was cleared to do so. So we'll see where it goes from there."

 More observations: 

 
 Some new additions to the injury report: rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling (hamstring tightness), DL Romello Height (elbow) and DL Cameron Sample (knee) did not participate. DL Keion White (adductor), DL Mikail Kamara (knee) and RB Kaelon Black (undisclosed) did not finish the practice after starting it. Kamara's ailment seemed the most serious as he was taken off on a cart. 
 WR Deebo Samuel took part in one-on-one drills but was limited to about 10 snaps in team drills. He made a trio of catches, including one over the middle for a big gain from QB Brock Purdy . 
 It was a rough day for the offense in general as it could never quite get on track. Purdy overthrew a handful of pass catchers as did Mac Jones . Nobody seemed to get in sync as it went on. Perhaps a sign of fatigue a week into training camp. 
 

 

 Friday, July 31 
 During the team meeting before Friday's first fully padded practice, assistant head coach Chris Foerster emphasized to the 49ers the importance of protecting one another. In that message, Foerster asked his team to be competitive but not fight.

 "I did a great job with that one," Foerster said, laughing.

 In fact, the Niners' first padded practice did end with a couple of skirmishes, the second of which devolved into a full-fledged fight. On the play, tight end Jake Tonges appeared to push off linebacker Fred Warner then catch a pass from QB Brock Purdy . Although there was a flag thrown on Tonges on the play, Warner ran over to Tonges and got in his face, seemingly taking exception at how Tonges got open. The two exchanged words and shoves before OT Colton McKivitz ran in to stand up for Tonges. That led to LB Dre Greenlaw coming in and McKivitz ending up on the ground as the rest of the team surrounded them. The fight broke up quickly.

 Tensions were already bubbling from a play just before that when Greenlaw shoved RB Christian McCaffrey to the ground on the left sideline. McCaffrey stood up and shoved Greenlaw, who seemed to quickly realize who he had shoved and did not retaliate as it broke up quickly. Regardless, Foerster hopes it was just a product of the first day in pads and not a regular occurrence.

 "Fights are a waste of time and energy," Foerster said. "Absolute waste of time and energy."

 More observations: 

 
 WR Deebo Samuel was not yet at practice today. He's expected to get everything signed and squared away today and could be out there as soon as Saturday. All signs point toward him being back in his No. 19 with Jacob Cowing switching to No. 6. 
 Coach Kyle Shanahan was on the field before team drills, coming out around 10:45 and staying for the rest of the practice. It was his longest time spent on the field yet in a practice open to media. 
 The 49ers activated DT Alfred Collins (shoulder) from the PUP list Friday. He took part in his first practice of this camp, albeit with some limitations on team reps, it seemed. 
 A good day for DL Keion White in one-on-one pass rush drills. White had a few convincing victories and seems fully healed from the gunshot wound he suffered in his foot/ankle in February. 
 DE Nick Bosa isn't yet doing team drills or one-on-one, but he spent time with OT Trent Williams doing some work on the side during the one-on-one pass rush drills to start getting back up to speed. 
 Rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling continues to put productive practices together. Mike Evans mentioned Stribling first when asked about other receivers performing in this camp. One thing that has stood out: Stribling makes plays no matter which offensive unit he's with or which defensive unit he's playing against. 
 

 

 

 Wednesday, July 29 
 Christian McCaffrey turned 30 years old on June 7, but early suggestions of his fall off don't appear to be coming to fruition in the early days of camp. Coming off the biggest workload of his career, McCaffrey has not only participated in all three open practices but looked like his usual, productive self in the process.

 Speaking to reporters Wednesday, McCaffrey said he's well aware that a running back with his wear and tear is supposed to have his best days behind him, but he's not spending any time worrying about hitting the 30-year-old milestone.

title: What's next for 49ers receivers Aiyuk, Deebo and Pearsall?
summary: When will Aiyuk be released? And will he sign with Washington? What is Samuel's role after returning to S.F.?
full_text:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Little more than a week into training camp, the San Francisco 49ers are already dealing with plenty of questions.

 Once again, many of those linger over what's going on at wide receiver.

 Brandon Aiyuk is still estranged , Ricky Pearsall will have season-ending surgery on the posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) in his right knee, Deebo Samuel is back and the Niners are hoping at least one of their young wideouts is ready for a bigger role opposite Mike Evans .

 Here's a look at the most pressing issues surrounding one of San Francisco's most intriguing position groups, with additional insight from Washington Commanders reporter John Keim.

 

 Where do things stand between the 49ers and Aiyuk? 
 After announcing Pearsall will miss this season, Niners general manager John Lynch said there was no update on Aiyuk's situation. The ball remains in Aiyuk's court regarding whether he is going to force San Francisco to make a move.

 For now, Aiyuk is on the reserve/left squad list. He has had that designation since December, meaning he doesn't count against the 49ers' 90-man roster or their salary cap. For anything to change, Aiyuk must first apply with the NFL for reinstatement. Aiyuk could then force the Niners to do something by reporting for training camp or, at a minimum, reaching out to the organization and telling it he plans to report.

 

 To this point, Aiyuk has opted against doing any of that. Instead, he has taken to social media to voice his displeasure with the team, the league and the NFL Players Association while simultaneously pushing to land with the Commanders .

 After the Niners re-signed Samuel, Aiyuk posted a cryptic message on Instagram asking, "San Fran wanna see a real reunion?" Presumably, Aiyuk was just trolling since it's clear his time with the 49ers is over.

 The only question left to answer is the same one that has persisted for months: When will the separation happen? -- Wagoner 

 

 Is Washington still a realistic option for Aiyuk if the Niners let him go? 
 Once upon a time, the answer would have been yes. Washington's brass would have been all-in on signing Aiyuk to a low, one-year, prove-it deal with incentives. Commanders general manager Adam Peters was in San Francisco for four seasons with Aiyuk, and Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels has maintained a close relationship with the wide receiver since they played together for one season at Arizona State . Aiyuk could provide a big-play threat that Washington covets.

 Now? The phrase you'll hear is "never say never," but there's been a definite cooling of the Commanders' interest after Aiyuk's Instagram postings over the past month, including some about Daniels .

 As Peters said last week -- speaking about no one in particular -- he "usually" doesn't factor a player's social media posts when deciding whether to acquire him. Then Peters punctuated it with another "usually."

 It also depends on whether Washington adds another veteran wideout. If that does happen, it would likely be Stefon Diggs . He would provide what Washington lacks: a proven veteran opposite Terry McLaurin .

 But if Aiyuk comes free and the Commanders consider signing him, they would have to be convinced those posts were merely an indication of his frustration and not about any deeper issues. -- Keim 

 

 

 What does knee surgery mean for Pearsall? 
 Given all that he has been through in his first couple of seasons, this figured to be an important campaign for Pearsall. After injuries limited him to 20 games across his first two seasons, Pearsall looked poised for a breakout in 2026, before the PCL in his right knee swelled up on him again.

 It's an injury Pearsall has dealt with since Week 4 of last season, and offseason attempts to rest and let it heal did not work out.

 "He's gutted," Lynch said. "We're gutted."

 When healthy, Pearsall has flashed plenty of promise. He had two 100-plus-yard games in the first three contests of 2025 before the knee injury happened against the Jacksonville Jaguars  in Week 4.

 But things out of Pearsall's control have prevented his young career from taking off. He missed six games of his rookie season while recovering from a gunshot wound he suffered in a robbery attempt in San Francisco. He also has dealt with hamstring and ankle issues at various points.

 This latest setback will keep him out somewhere around nine months after he has surgery, which will take place in the next couple of weeks. The Niners hope Pearsall can bounce back and become the impact player they envisioned when they used the No. 31 pick on him during the 2024 NFL draft .

 "Ricky did not miss a game in college [at Florida ]," Lynch said. "And it's been a tough road for him since he's been in the league. But we know he's got a bright future. We're going to get this taken care of, and he'll come back being that same player -- and we look forward to that time."  -- Wagoner 

 
 

 Where does Samuel fit in with the Niners now that he's back? 

 Asked what he expects his role to be in his return with the 49ers, Samuel said he has "no idea." Lynch said Samuel will definitely take on kick return duties, something he did in important spots during his first stint with the team but will now do full time.

 Samuel's role in the offense will be a work in progress based on how those around him fare, how he performs in camp and which other wideouts are healthy.

 It's safe to assume Samuel won't be a focal point of the offensive unit like he once was. Instead, expect the Niners to lean on his versatility and hope that his threat can open things up for their other playmakers.

 "When the ball is in Deebo's hands, there's a lot of special things he can do," 49ers assistant head coach Chris Foerster said. "You find as many different ways to get the ball in his hands so he can impact the game in a special way."  -- Wagoner 

 

 Who among San Francisco's receivers looks ready for a bigger role opposite Evans? 

 It's still early in camp, but Evans provided his answer when asked recently if any of the young wideouts have stood out to him.

 

 "Strib has had a really good offseason at OTAs," Evans said. "And he's continued that during training camp."

 Strib, of course, is  De'Zhaun Stribling , whom the 49ers used their second-round pick (No. 33) on in this year's draft. At 6-foot-2 and 207 pounds with 4.36-second 40-yard dash speed, Stribling offers a size and speed element the Niners have lacked.

 Stribling is having a strong start to his first camp, though he missed Saturday's practice with hamstring tightness. The Niners envision him eventually replacing Evans at the X spot. But for now, Stribling is working all over and would make sense as a supercharged, oversize slot receiver.

 Some of that calculus depends on how soon Christian Kirk returns from a calf injury -- which has kept him out of the early portion of camp -- and where Samuel fits. Demarcus Robinson offers a veteran presence and is someone who can play anywhere, and youngsters Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing also have earned a longer look. Watkins, in particular, has had some standout moments early in camp.

 Either way, Lynch said he feels good about what the Niners have at the position.

 "You're betting on the come on some of these guys," Lynch said. "We feel good about where we're at and a lot of competition there. I think that's been a really exciting group from 1 to 11 or whatever we have in here right now. It's a good group. It's very competitive, and we like where we're at."  -- Wagoner

full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' camp is taking place at the Advent Health Training Center in Tampa, Florida, and Buccaneers reporter Jenna Laine has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Bucs camp. We will update this file often. We are looking at who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Bucs camp 
 
 Mayfield felt 'disrespected' and 'undervalued' by contract offers 
 History says Vea, Mayfield will play with Bucs this season 
 Vea requests trade from Bucs after stalled talks 
 2026 Bucs training camp preview 
 
 
 Monday, Aug. 3 
 Wide receivers Jalen McMillan and Emeka Egbuka were not practicing for the team's first day in pads -- due to being, as coach Todd Bowles put it, "a little sore." Cornerback Jacob Parrish , last year's starting nickelback who is competing for a starting outside cornerback spot, also missed practice with what Bowles said was soreness.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 The Bucs have brought back two-time Olympic hurdling champion Roger Kingdom, who served as the team's speed and conditioning coach under Bruce Arians and is part of a coaching staff revamp that also included members of strength and conditioning department. "Obviously, we're stretching and running and doing dynamic warmups and those type of things, trying to stop some of the soft-tissue injuries," Bowles said. "He does a good job aiding in that and making sure guys are doing what they're supposed to do, as far as running form-wise and the way they're supposed to run. It's really helped us out." 
 The team was forced to practice indoors due to heavy rain for the second straight day. Bowles joked, "I think I've been here about eight years, and this is the second time in a row we've gone indoors. Every other year we've been outside." They'll do it a third day in a row Tuesday as it's a night practice. 
 There's been no movement on Pro Bowl nose tackle Vita Vea 's contract since his 'hold in' began at the start of camp. but the team just installed his image on one of four corners of Raymond James Stadium's exterior, along with quarterback Baker Mayfield , wide receiver Chris Godwin and safety Antoine Winfield Jr . 
 
 
 
 Sunday, Aug. 2 
 Bucs coach Todd Bowles clarified that the hamstring injury that has plagued outside cornerback and 2025 second-round draft pick Benjamin Morrison -- forcing him to miss the start of training camp -- is actually a different hamstring than the one that limited him last season.

 Morrison missed all of preseason last year and played in 10 regular-season games -- with three starts -- as a result of a quad injury and then a right hamstring injury. On top of this, Morrison underwent bilateral hip surgery. He is competing for a starting spot on the outside with Zyon McCollum and Jacob Parrish but has yet to participate in team periods in camp, making his evaluation a tough one and raising concerns over depth at that position.

 "Hopefully he gets some work in this coming week," Bowles said of Morrison. "I would like to see. He was out here moving around better, but I'll see what the trainer says."

 Monday will mark the team's first padded practice of camp.

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Safety Antoine Winfield Jr . picked off quarterback Baker Mayfield on a deep ball pass intended for wide receiver Jalen McMillan , whom he battled on a contested catch. 
 WR  Tez Johnson , who hauled in a deep ball touchdown from QB  Jake Browning  earlier this week and punctuated it with a celebratory backflip, pulled in a touchdown from Mayfield on a crossing route during a red zone period. 
 All-Pro left tackle Tristan Wirfs remains sidelined with a hamstring injury, but like Pro Bowl nose tackle Vita Vea , he was spotted on the sideline during the indoor practice.  Benjamin Chukwuma , who started two games last season, has been getting reps in Wirfs' spot. 
 
 

 Friday, July 31 

 One day after quarterback Baker Mayfield said he felt "disrespected" during his failed contract negotiations with the Bucs and vowed to have a "really big year," Mayfield put together his strongest training camp practice so far. He heaved a deep pass to wide receiver Emeka Egbuka , slipping it past safety Tykee Smith and cornerback Ayden Garnes for a touchdown. He also connected with wide receiver Jalen McMillan for a deep touchdown with cornerback Damarion Williams in coverage.

 "It sucks to see him go through this and whatnot, but it's not going to change his mentality, the way he plays," guard Cody Mauch said of Mayfield, whom he agrees with on having a big year. "He's going to go off."

 
 Outside cornerback Benjamin Morrison , who missed the first two training camp practices with a lingering hamstring injury and is competing for a starting job, did return to practice but was limited to positional drills. 
 All-Pro left tackle Tristan Wirfs was back out on the practice field after spending Thursday indoors to receive treatment for a hamstring injury. Coach Todd Bowles said, "He's not practicing yet, but he's moving around better so we'll just continue to monitor him." 
 

 

 

 Thursday, July 30 

 Tight end Bauer Sharp , a seventh-round draft pick, had a leaping touchdown grab in the corner of the end zone from quarterback Baker Mayfield during red zone. Mayfield also connected with wide receiver Emeka Egbuka for a score with Zyon McCollum in coverage.

 Not to be outdone though -- backup quarterback Jake Browning had multiple connections with wide receiver Tez Johnson , including a 50-plus yard touchdown through the air with Josh Hayes in coverage. In signature Johnson fashion, he did a celebratory backflip.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 The offense may have made some notable plays, but the defense had some strong moments too. Safety Tykee Smith punched the ball loose from Egbuka's hands with safety Antoine Winfield Jr . pouncing for the recovery. 
 Inside linebacker Alex Anzalone made some key stops in coverage against running back Bucky Irving and tight end Cade Otton in the red zone. Coach Todd Bowles said, "He doesn't panic out there like most guys do being at the 'backer spot. He kind of covers like a safety. So, he has very good awareness and headiness about that." 
 Unlike Wednesday, defensive tackle Vita Vea (back) and left tackle Tristan Wirfs (hamstring) were not out on the practice field and instead were inside receiving treatment. Bowles said he does not have a clear timeline for recovery at this time. 
 Cornerback Benjamin Morrison , who missed Wednesday with a hamstring injury, was on the field with teammates but was limited. He is among the players competing for a starting job on the outside. 
 Wide receiver  Chris Godwin Jr ., a 10-year veteran, was given a maintenance day. 
 

 

 Wednesday, July 29 
 Pro Bowl nose tackle Vita Vea did not participate in the team's first training camp practice Wednesday morning, standing on the sidelines during team periods and observing positional work with his defensive line teammates.

 Though, Vea's lack of participation wasn't just about wanting a new contract, which was the primary reason he didn't practice during mandatory minicamp. Bucs coach Todd Bowles said Vea tweaked his back during the team's conditioning test and is "day to day."

 All-Pro left tackle Tristan Wirfs also tweaked his hamstring during the test and did not practice Wednesday.

title: 2026 Tennessee Titans training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Titans training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Tennessee Titans ' camp is taking place at the Vanderbilt Health Football Center, and Titans reporter Turron Davenport has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Titans camp. We will update this file often. We are looking at who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football, and which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Titans news: 

 
 Will Levis: There aren't 32 QBs better than me 
 Titans WRs join Cam Ward in Miami to build chemistry 
 2026 Titans training camp preview 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 The first day of pads had a really good pace and tempo. Both the offense and defense did a good job keeping each other off the ground for the most part.

 The defense had big hits from cornerback Nazeeh Johnson and linebacker Sean Brown , and quarterback  Cam Ward had two hiccups throwing across his body while rolling out -- resulting in interceptions.

 Coach Robert Saleh said the throws across the body are non-negotiable, especially the shallow ones. Safety  Amani Hooker came up with the first interception as a result of what Saleh said was a "poor decision" by Ward. Saleh called the second interception an elite play by defensive lineman  Jermaine Johnson II .

 Ward did have a couple of nice spot throws to  Wan'Dale Robinson  between defenders during team period. He also connected with veteran receiver Calvin Ridley on a well-placed pass to towards the sideline.

 Other observations:  

 
 WR  Elic Ayomanor continues to have a solid camp. He beat Micah Robinson at the line of scrimmage and caught a deep pass in the end zone from  Mitchell Trubisky . The two almost connected on another deep pass but Robinson was called for pass interference. Ayomanor caught a pass on a deep in-breaking route from Ward also. Saleh credited Ayomanor for the offseason preparation and confidence he's playing with. 
 Defensive line coach Aaron Whitecotton didn't like the lack of intensity during individual period, so he made the group do pushups. The defensive line goes nonstop during that period. Whitecotton has them do a lot of work on the sled and with bags but at a very fast pace. 
 JC Latham took part in the first team period but worked with a trainer on the third field for the remaining ones. Latham's absence allowed Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson to get some valuable reps as he competes with Austin Deculus for the swing tackle spot. 
 
 

 

 

 Saturday, Aug.1  
 The Titans hosted fans at training camp for the first time this summer, and they got to see a pretty solid day from quarterback  Cam Ward .

 Ward and Elic Ayomanor connected on a couple of deep passes along the sideline. It's clear Ward trusts Ayomanor to win in jump ball situations, as the second-year tandem has found success on those 50-50 passes in the three practices open to the media.

 Ward was sharp in team and 7-on-7 periods highlighted by a couple of three-completion streaks before giving way to  Mitchell Trubisky .

 Ayomanor has had a solid couple of days, making a living catching passes on deep in-breaking routes in addition to his big plays down the field. He is noticeably bigger and playing with more confidence this camp.

 More observations: 

 
 Offensive tackle  JC Latham returned to practice and took part in the first team period before sitting out the final two. Latham is working to improve his mental approach to the game. He hired a mental coach late last season and is working to better process the game and not let one bad play carryover to the next snap. 
 

 

 Thursday, July 30 

 The defense won the day, highlighted by two interceptions.

 Cedric Gray picked off a pass from Cam Ward that bounced off  Wan'Dale Robinson 's hands along the sideline during the first team period. James Williams Sr . got the other turnover when he stepped in front of a  Mitchell Trubisky  pass intended for Xavier Restrepo .  Jeffery Simmons and the defensive line forced multiple throwaways by Ward during both team periods, as well.

 The offense did come up with a big play when Ward found Elic Ayomanor for a long touchdown. Ward was under pressure but side armed a pass down the field, and Ayomanor skied over  Cor'Dale Flott  to make the catch before outracing the safety to the end zone. Bryce Oliver also came up with a long play when he caught a pass of over 60 yards from Trubisky with Joshua Williams in coverage. Other than those two plays, it was mostly quick passes, and the defense was all over it.

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Right tackle JC Latham came off the PUP list and worked on a third field with the team's training staff. Latham is noticeably bigger after reporting to camp with a slimmed down physique last year. Coach Robert Saleh said Latham is expected to be a full participant when the team practices again Saturday (Friday is a walk thru closed to media). 
 Calvin Ridley appears to be feeling better after dealing with a stomach bug that limited him in practice Wednesday. Ridley took part in team period and showed speed by running away from Flott on a deep pass, but it fell incomplete. 
 Jacob Martin continues to be a plus for the young defensive ends. Martin offered up plenty of tips to rookie Keldric Faulk before practice. The ninth-year veteran had pointers for  Oluwafemi Oladejo  after multiple reps as well. Veteran pass rusher  Jermaine Johnson II  also pointed to Martin as one of the guys that helped him as a rookie with Saleh and the Jets in 2022. 
 Trubisky returned after missing practice Monday because of tightness. Trubisky worked with the second group while Will Levis came in after him. His return relegated Hendon Hooker to an observatory role during team and 7-on-7 periods. 
 

 

 Wednesday, July 29 

 Robert Saleh listed third down, two-minute, and red zone as the three key principles of playing quarterback when asked before practice.

 "When it comes to third down, everyone knows you're about to throw," Saleh said. "Or two-minute, you've got to have it. In the red zone where everything's sped up, and the windows get a lot tighter, that's where the quarterback shines."

 Cam Ward agreed with the sentiment, saying third down is when you win or lose the game. This came after a so-so day for Ward, who targeted  Wan'Dale Robinson  frequently. Ward had a solid red zone team period, connecting with Elic Ayomanor and Carnell Tate for touchdowns. But he wanted more.

 "We had some good plays, but our mindset is to score every chance we get," Ward said. "We for sure have to be better, and I have to be more on time on quicker routes in certain situations."

 
 More observations from the day: 

 
 Before practice, Saleh said Austin Schlottmann and Cordell Volson would be with the first team at center and right guard. Jackson Slater opened up at right guard during the initial team period and got called for a false start on the second play. Volson worked at right guard with the next group alongside rookie center Pat Coogan . 
 Mitchell Trubisky didn't take part in practice due to soreness. That cleared the way for Hendon Hooker to get action in team period and 7-on-7 after not doing so during the open portion of OTAs and minicamp. Hooker had a nice pass to rookie tight end Jaren Kanak during 7-on-7. 
 Calvin Ridley is dealing with an illness that caused him to lose weight. Ridley was limited in practice Wednesday and didn't come out until after the 7-on-7 work. He didn't take part in the team period.

title: 2026 Washington Commanders training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Follow our daily updates from Commanders training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The Washington Commanders camp is taking place in Ashburn, Virginia, and Commanders reporter John Keim has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Commanders camp. We will update this file often. Can Washington bounce back from an injury-plagued 2025 season? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information until the first full week of the preseason begins Aug. 13.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Commanders camp 
 
 Daniels finds voice, aims to fill leadership void 
 Commanders tab ex-All-Pro WR Wes Welker to coach tight ends 
 
 

 Monday, Aug. 3 

 First-round pick Sonny Styles made his presence felt on the first play from scrimmage -- and the first day with pads.

 On an inside handoff to running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt , Styles filled the hole and popped the running back. Washington doesn't do live tackling so Styles then let up, but the impact was felt.

 Through the early part of camp, Styles has stood out because of his length and speed. He has been solid in coverage, particularly when in zone. He broke up a pass to receiver Jaylin Lane in one zone look Monday.

 Styles also showed what he could do as a blitzer, getting paired vs. running back Jeremy McNichols on one pressure -- and using his speed and power to attack his outside shoulder and win the rep. Styles has worked often alongside Frankie Luvu .

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 Corner Trey Amos (fractured fibula) and punter Tress Way (biceps), both of whom are on the physically unable to perform list, will be re-evaluated Thursday. There's optimism about their progress. 
 Quarterback Jayden Daniels made a terrific throw on the run to the back of the end zone for tight end Chig Okonkwo in a red zone drill. Okonkwo was in the back of the end zone with corner Ahkello Witherspoon directly in front of him. Daniels threw the ball to Okonkwo's right, and the tight end waited until the last second to reach over for the ball so Witherspoon wouldn't be able to react. 
 Corner Mike Sainristil broke up passes to the corner of the end zone on consecutive plays. Receiver Terry McLaurin made a nice catch in the corner and tapped both feet in-bounds as fans in attendance cheered. 
 

 Saturday, Aug. 1 
 Washington Commanders tight end John Bates will miss "a couple of weeks" after suffering a strained hamstring in practice Thursday, coach Dan Quinn said Saturday.

 Bates has been one of the NFL's best blocking tight ends and a player Washington values greatly. It does have some depth at the position with Chig Okonkwo , Ben Sinnott as well as Colson Yankoff . 

 Center Nick Allegretti will miss "the next week or so," according to Quinn, after straining a calf muscle on Wednesday, the first day of camp.

 The good news for Washington: receiver  Treylon Burks  returned to practice after missing Thursday because of a foot issue.

 Allegretti's situation also highlights Washington's center depth. He's started four games at center in his career -- a position he considers his most natural -- but 35 at guard. But backup Julian Good-Jones has played two snaps in his career and the third center is rookie sixth-round pick Matt Gulbin .

 "It does give you a window into where people are at," Quinn said.

 Quinn said because they don't view Allegretti's situation as long-term, the team is not in the market to add another veteran. However, after practice, the Commanders had two other linemen working on snaps and initial blocks at center: third-year lineman Brandon Coleman and first-year guard Tyler Cooper .

 Washington's coaches have said in the past that Coleman, who has started at left tackle and left guard in his first two seasons, could play all five line spots. He is currently battling Chris Paul for the starting left guard position.

 

 More observations from the day: 

 
 The Commanders ran a drill simulating a late-game field goal attempt -- after running a play. The field goal unit had to sprint on the field and get in position for the kick. In this drill, incumbent Jake Moody made all three field goals while Drew Stevens made two, missing from 46 yards. Earlier, during another drill, Moody made all six of his field goal attempts while Stevens missed one. 
 Sinnott had a mixed day with two drops -- one coming on a perfect pass from Jayden Daniels into a narrow window. But Sinnott also made multiple catches. 
 One area Daniels has excelled at: getting through his progression in time so if he dumps the ball to his checkdown, that player has room to run. It happened again today with running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt . 
 Linebacker Sonny Styles showed his length and speed. He broke up one pass in zone, using his long arms to close on the ball. Another time he flashed to the area where the ball was thrown. Had there been live hitting, he would have hit the target as the ball arrived. 
 
 
 Thursday, July 30 
 Washington's tight ends have been far more active as a group than they had been the previous two seasons.

 Newly-signed Chig Okonkwo can be used all over, with wide receiver  Terry McLaurin saying he runs routes like a big receiver. That versatility was evident again Thursday, but it's also not just Okonkwo -- all the tight ends, including 2024 second-round pick Ben Sinnott , have run a wider variety of routes.

 "It's not even close," Sinnott said. "So many different variations. Today we're lining up at number one [receiver on the outside], we're running five-step ins, we're running corners, we're running options, we're running flat [routes]. We're just doing everything. It's so much fun. It's a breath of fresh air for this offense and how it uses tight ends."

 More observations: 

 
 Cornerback  Rasul Douglas ended practice by intercepting quarterback Marcus Mariota in the end zone. Douglas was signed after mini-camp in part because of his ability to create turnovers. 
 Julian Good-Jones worked at center in place of Nick Allegretti , who is out with a strained calf muscle. Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he didn't think Allegretti would be out long. He said the same about receiver  Treylon Burks , who did not practice because of a sore foot. 
 Linebacker Odafe Oweh 's speed has been noticeable during the first two days of camp. He has created multiple sack situations. 
 Tight end Colson Yankoff made the catch of the day late in practice, jumping high in traffic for an Athan Kaliakmanis pass in the end zone. Yankoff slammed to the ground, but held onto the ball. 
 

 

 Wednesday, July 29 
 Washington coach Dan Quinn wanted to set an immediate tone for competition in training camp, so the first full-team drill was red zone work. Quinn also focused on 2-point plays, wanting to make it even more competitive. "Those are the moments I want," Quinn said.

 Both sides of the ball could claim success -- and failure.

 Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels tossed one perfect pass to the corner of the end zone that receiver  Treylon Burks  reached up and caught. He also grabbed another high one over the middle. But Daniels was nearly intercepted by corner Mike Sainristil on another pass where the coverage was tight all over.

 "It gets the juices flowing, it gets guys ready," Daniels said.

 The Commanders' offense ranked fourth in red zone success last season -- but was 20th in number of red zone plays. The defense could really use the work in this area, as it ranked sixth in number of red zone plays ... and 31st in red zone success.
